Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves texture quality and visual fidelity of the base model while maintaining global structural consistency in a training-free manner.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: EviRover: Reinforcing Agentic Perception Beyond a Glance
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Kaixuan Fan, Kaituo Feng, Tianshuo Peng, Yilei Jiang, Manyuan Zhang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: EviRover introduces an agentic perception model that enhances visual understanding through interactive learning, outperforming traditional methods and benchmarks in complex scenarios.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Visual perception is conventionally formulated as a one-shot prediction from a single glance at the image, under the assumption that the image content and the model's parametric knowledge suffice to resolve the query. This assumption often fails in real-world scenarios that hinge on fine-grained visual details or require knowledge-intensive and up-to-date information. We term such cases \textit{perception under insufficient evidence} and formulate perception as an agentic process that can obtain information beyond a single glance. To address the absence of data for this setting, we design two dedicated data generation pipelines, yielding EviRover-SFT-5K and EviRover-RL-12K for training. We further construct EviLens, a human-verified benchmark comprising 688 instances across five perception categories. Building on these data, we present EviRover, to our knowledge the first perception agent explicitly trained to resolve perceptual queries through interaction, using supervised fine-tuning followed by agentic reinforcement learning. Experiments show that the 4B EviRover outperforms its backbone by 30 points on average on EviLens, reaching performance comparable to advanced proprietary models. The gains transfer beyond EviLens to WebEyes, conventional perception benchmarks, and general multimodal benchmarks, including a 15-point improvement on BrowseComp-VL. All code, models, and data are released.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: GaugeVLM: Structuring Spatial Supervision with Measured Geometric Interventions
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Hongbo Wang, Zihan Lin, Wenkui Yang, Shiran Ge, Yuang Ai
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: GaugeVLM enhances vision-language models by structuring spatial supervision through geometric interventions, improving performance on spatial metrics and generalizing across domains.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can contradict themselves across views of the same spatial relation and fail to respond when that relation changes. Addressing these failures requires supervision that captures error magnitude and geometric dependencies across observations, both of which remain implicit in training on individual answers or ordinal preferences. Therefore, we introduce GaugeVLM, which makes this structure explicit through controlled object and camera interventions in explicit 3D scenes, producing linked observations with measured differences between spatial relations and shared truths across views. To translate this structure into learning signals, its core objective, GaugeDPO, converts measured errors into preference margins, directly supervises correct canonical rankings across views, and links intervention-induced answer-odds contrasts to measured relation changes with view-specific scales. Our analysis bounds canonical prediction error and establishes that the cross-view and intervention constraints can be jointly satisfied. Empirically, GaugeVLM improves all 10 established spatial metrics over supervised fine-tuning across three VLM backbones, with the main 7B model gaining 15.0 and 18.9 percentage points on MSMU distance and QSpatial+, respectively. These gains also extend to autonomous driving and embodied reasoning, demonstrating the robust generalization across domains.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Zishan Xu, Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Chen, Yifu Guo, Zhengxi Lu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: EnvACE introduces a novel reinforcement learning method that utilizes world rehearsal to internalize environment dynamics, enhancing agent decision-making and performance without external interactions.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Training large language model agents for long-horizon tool use typically relies on interactions with real or synthesized executable environments, whose construction and verification are costly, or on external simulators that are difficult to ground. We introduce EnvACE, an agentic reinforcement learning method that replaces external environment interaction during training with world rehearsal. The policy alternates between acting and rehearsal: it first generates a tool call, then plays the role of the environment to produce the response induced by that action, and conditions subsequent decisions on the rehearsed response. Both roles are jointly optimized end-to-end using task-success rewards. Through world rehearsal, the policy internalizes the relationship between actions and their environment responses in its parameters, yielding an agent world model that directly supports decision making. Across BFCL-v4, tau^2-Bench, VitaBench, and FinMCP-Bench, EnvACE achieves strong and transferable performance, outperforming environment-scaling baselines in the overall evaluation. Controlled studies further show that world rehearsal consistently improves policy learning across model scales. At test time, the internalized world model enables private rehearsal before committed execution, yielding further gains under a moderate rehearsal budget without additional external interaction. Our findings establish world rehearsal as a new path toward scaling LLM agent training beyond the constraints of external environments. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Within-yao/EnvACE.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: OccluDex: Hierarchical 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Learning for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation under Self-Occlusion
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Ziheng Xu, Yueyuan Chen, Xinyuan He, Guoxing Liu, Yuanshuo Tan
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: OccluDex is a hierarchical 3D visuo-tactile learning framework that enhances dexterous manipulation under self-occlusion, achieving superior accuracy in both simulated and real-world tasks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Reliable dexterous manipulation requires continuous estimation of object geometry and hand-object contact throughout interaction. With egocentric sensing, however, the manipulating hand frequently occludes task-relevant object surfaces and contact regions, reducing the visual evidence available for state estimation and thereby making robust closed-loop control and generalization to unseen object geometries particularly challenging. To address this, we present OccluDex, a hierarchical 3D visuo-tactile representation learning framework that integrates global geometric structure with local contact information for robust manipulation under dynamic self-occlusion during hand-object interaction. OccluDex adopts multi-scale masked autoencoding to progressively encode partial 3D geometry and fuses tactile contact tokens with high-level geometric features through cross-modal attention. The encoder is pretrained from synchronized human visuo-tactile demonstrations and transferred as a frozen perceptual backbone for downstream reinforcement learning. We evaluate OccluDex on a faucet rotation task, requiring one full clockwise handle revolution, and a tabletop object reorientation task, requiring a 180-degree tabletop object reorientation without toppling. In simulation experiments, OccluDex demonstrated 12.6% higher accuracy for unseen objects and 8.3% higher accuracy for previously seen objects than the strongest state-of-the-art baseline models. Physical experiments were further performed with a Shadow Hand to demonstrate successful zero-shot sim-to-real generalization on unseen physical objects. This results could enable humanoid egocentric object manipulation for seen and unseen objects even when the manipulating robotic hand occludes vision.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: ChunkTrust: Adapting Execution Horizons for Robot Policies with Action-Expert Evidence
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Fanding Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Shifeng Bao, Mingkang Pu, Shiwei Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: ChunkTrust enhances robot policy execution by dynamically adapting action horizons using action-expert evidence, significantly improving task success rates across various environments.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Robot foundation policies predict action chunks, but how many actions to execute before replanning depends on the current task phase. We introduce ChunkTrust, which treats the execution horizon as a latent variable inferred from action-expert evidence rather than a fixed hyperparameter. Its training-free Action-aware Horizon Selector (AHS) combines intra-chunk spectral stability of generation traces with inter-chunk continuity between executed history and predicted actions. An online Beta posterior with kernel forgetting tracks horizon preferences across replans. A lightweight Query-based Horizon Adapter (QHA) optionally learns a context-conditioned dense prior from complementary evidence, fused with current evidence and episode-local Beta memory while the base policy remains frozen. Across RoboTwin2.0 and RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, AHS improves overall task-averaged success for each evaluated base-policy configuration, including gains of +6.80 percentage points on $π_{0.5}$ over all 50 RoboTwin2.0 tasks and +9.67 percentage points on Qwen3GR00T in RoboCasa. AHS+QHA raises the gain over Base to +9.44 percentage points on the eight-task $π_{0.5}$ evaluation. On four real-world household tasks, AHS improves the equal-task mean normalized process score from 50.4% to 57.5%. Ablations examine the contributions of both evidence terms, temporal memory, and the learned prior. Project page is https://hf618.github.io/ChunkTrust.github.io/

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: SERA: Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation for Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Zihao Chen, Fanxiang Xiong, Hongran Ren, Xuefeng Bai, Zhongxiang Dai
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: SERA optimizes rollout allocation in Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning by equalizing success-dependent likelihood gradients, enhancing performance in reasoning tasks and navigation.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (MaxRL) targets prompt-wise log-success and has shown strong performance on reasoning tasks. Under finite rollout budgets, however, the estimator used by MaxRL attenuates each prompt's likelihood gradient by a factor that depends on its success probability and rollout count. Under uniform rollout allocation, the common rollout count fails to compensate for success-dependent attenuation, leaving low-success prompts more strongly attenuated and distorting their relative contributions to the expected aggregate gradient. We introduce SERA (Scale-Equalized Rollout Allocation), which redistributes a fixed rollout budget to approximately equalize these finite-rollout scaling factors. Building on our theoretical analysis of how finite rollouts distort prompt-wise likelihood gradients, we formulate the allocation as a fixed-budget max--min problem, derive a waterline solution to its continuous relaxation, and introduce a multiplicity correction to remove the additional prompt weighting induced by heterogeneous rollout counts. Experiments show stronger alignment with exact likelihood gradients in a controlled ImageNet setting and improved multi-sample solution coverage over MaxRL on maze navigation and mathematical reasoning under matched training rollout budgets.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Visual Parallel Search: Learning to Search High-Resolution Images with Parallel Tile Inspection and Adaptive Zoom
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Xijia Tao, Yihua Teng, Xinyu Fu, Cheng Gong, Ziru Liu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The Visual Parallel Search framework enhances high-resolution visual question answering by enabling parallel tile inspection and adaptive zoom, significantly improving accuracy and efficiency.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: High-resolution visual question answering often fails because a multimodal model does not acquire the small, spatially localized evidence needed to answer a question. Sequential zooming can recover detail, but it asks the main model to choose a region before obtaining a reliable overview. We introduce VPS, a visual parallel-search framework in which a main agent first invokes grid_search to inspect image tiles in parallel with question-conditioned sub-agents, and then adaptively invokes zoom_in PSisual Parallel Search improves mean accuracy over dedicated zoom-only search in 14 of 15 same-model comparisons, with gains up to 8.0 points and especially strong improvements for smaller main models. ZoomBench retains an approximately 3.2-point gain at every tested size. We further develop a supervision pipeline with hint-free verification and a paired role-specific GRPO surrogate for learning the controller and tile-reader roles. SFT improves observed accuracy on all five benchmark splits, including a 4.17-point gain on HR-Bench 4K. Role-specific RL further reshapes search behavior: main-only RL reduces mean tool use from 2.65 to 2.11 with similar pass@1 in an internal four-response evaluation, while external accuracy changes are mixed. Joint training reveals an asymmetry between local evidence reading and global search control. Together, these results support VPS as an effective inference-time scaffold and a trainable decomposition for visual evidence acquisition.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Kerui Ren, Yingxiang Xu, Kaiwen Song, Linning Xu, Bo Dai
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: Real2Gym transforms real-world video demonstrations into interactive simulation environments, enabling robots to learn and execute manipulation skills effectively in both simulated and physical settings.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Real-world videos provide rich demonstrations of manipulation, but turning them into reusable robot skills requires visually aligned environments, executable physical interactions, and mechanisms for learning from experience. We introduce Real2Gym, an agentic Real2Sim2Real framework that turns human and robot demonstrations into interactive simulation gyms and brings skills acquired in simulation to physical robots. The Real2Sim module reconstructs editable scenes, aligns objects and cameras with the input, validates demonstrated or retargeted actions through native physics execution, and generates task-conditioned variations with action-feasibility checks. Within these environments, the agent generates executable code for manipulation stages, observes their outcomes, and distills successful attempts and failures into reusable task procedures, object-relative motions, and recovery strategies. Through a shared perception-and-control interface, these skills guide subsequent execution in simulation and on real robots, with motions adapted to current observations and no updates to the underlying model weights. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Real2Gym enables high-fidelity simulation environment reconstruction, outperforming GPT-6 Astra Direct Mode by 16.7% in success rate with approximately 74.9% fewer policy-execution tokens across these environments, while exceeding it by 33.3% in physical robot execution success rate across four tasks on a real Franka robot.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Learning Social Navigation from Internet Videos in the Policy State Space
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Jiaming Wang, Duc Thang Nguyen, Jizhuo Chen, Volodymyr Shcherbyna, Diwen Liu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The paper presents a novel method for training social-navigation policies using monocular walking videos to create efficient simulation environments, achieving superior performance in real-world trials.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Training robust social-navigation policies requires simulators with diverse scene layouts, terrain, and human motion, but constructing such environments and specifying pedestrian behavior is costly. We propose an efficient pipeline that converts ordinary monocular walking videos directly into closed-loop social-navigation training environments in the policy's state space. Our key observation is that local social navigation primarily depends on two types of information: where the robot can traverse and how nearby pedestrians move. We therefore represent the static scene as a metric traversability map, which can be rigidly transformed under counterfactual robot motion, while directly replaying the pedestrian trajectories recovered from the video over time. This abstraction allows us to define the forward dynamics directly in the policy's state space and efficiently simulate counterfactual robot states without reconstructing or rendering photorealistic observations. The resulting policy achieves 81.2% success in the independent Arena benchmark, compared with 75.0% for the strongest baseline, and succeeds in 19/20 real-robot trials without policy fine-tuning.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: WorldLine: Action-Driven Visual Simulation for Robotic Manipulation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Shenghe Zheng, Wenbo Li, Jiyao Zhang, Bin Xia, Haoyang Huang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: WorldLine is an advanced action-driven visual simulator that enhances robotic manipulation by learning dynamics from extensive action-free videos and improving trajectory prediction accuracy across various embodiments.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Real-world robot learning is constrained by the cost of collecting experience and evaluating candidate behaviors. Video generation models offer a scalable foundation for visual simulators that predict action outcomes before physical execution. Yet they often favor visual plausibility over accurate action following and coherent robot--object dynamics, while action-conditioned simulators depend on scarce, embodiment-specific data that are difficult to share across incompatible control spaces. We introduce WorldLine, an action-driven visual simulator that decouples transferable dynamics learning from heterogeneous action grounding. WorldLine learns manipulation dynamics from more than 10,000 hours of action-free robot videos and grounds them using over 2,000 hours of action trajectories across more than ten embodiments. An image-space action representation provides a shared control interface across embodiments, while multi-view and failure-enriched training with relational regularization improves interaction-sensitive prediction. Robot-focused few-step distillation enables efficient causal rollout while preserving action-critical motion. Across held-out and out-of-domain settings, WorldLine maintains strong visual quality and robot-motion agreement; on failed trajectories, it improves robot-mask IoU by 0.1626 over the strongest baseline. It predicts trajectory success with 74% mean accuracy across RoboTwin and AgiBot, one percentage point above the strongest baseline. Without RoboTwin training or adaptation, its rollouts improve task success by up to 21.4 percentage points over direct policy execution. Together, these capabilities make WorldLine a scalable and efficient visual simulator for policy evaluation and embodied planning. More results are available at \href{https://zhengsh123.github.io/WorldLine/}{project page}.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforced Fine Tuning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Ruixiao Xu, Wong Lik Hang Kenny, Zhiqian Liu, Jianing Guo, Hanxiao Li
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper introduces a reinforced fine-tuning pipeline for cooperative multi-agent Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing performance through improved coordination and reduced reliance on human demonstrations.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: We study reinforcement learning (RL) methods for cooperative multi-agent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. This problem is challenging because VLAs are pretrained on large-scale single-agent data and therefore lack the fine-grained coordination skills required for inter-robot collaboration. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on multi-robot demonstrations partially bridges this gap, but its performance is bounded by the demonstration data and cannot improve from its own experience. We present a three-stage reinforced fine-tuning (RFT) pipeline for multi-agent VLAs. First, initialization-aware data collection sweeps over initial configurations and invokes human demonstrations only when the pretrained VLA repeatedly fails, yielding robustness to initialization shift with reduced human cost. Second, offline credit-filtered tuning assigns credit to individual agents and fine-tunes on per-agent trajectories with positive advantage rather than on entire joint rollouts. Third, we find existing online RL for VLAs are less effective for hard multi-agent tasks, which we attribute to noisy co-exploration and unstable updates. We instead use online latent-space fine tuning, which freeze the VLA and perform RL in its latent noise space. We evaluate our multi-agent VLA with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ backbones across 11 tasks in RoboTwin, RoboFactory and real-world manipulation with two Franka robots. Our multi-agent VLA improves the average success rate by $+23.1\%$, $+16.4\%$, and $+44\%$ on RoboTwin, RoboFactory, and real-world tasks, respectively. Code available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/mavla_rft-2BC0/.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: GeoVerse: World-Consistent Novel View Synthesis in Geometric Latent Space
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Kerui Ren, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Changjian Jiang, Mu Huang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: GeoVerse synthesizes world-consistent novel views by integrating geometric latent space with video generative appearance priors, enhancing visual quality and geometric consistency.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis from sparse images must reconcile faithful reconstruction of observed regions with plausible completion of unseen content, while maintaining world consistency across viewpoints. Existing geometry-based methods preserve observed scene structure but often struggle to complete unseen regions, whereas video generative models offer rich appearance priors but accumulate inconsistencies during sequential view generation. We propose GeoVerse, a framework that synthesizes world-consistent novel views by performing generation within the geometric latent space of a pretrained 3D foundation model and injecting appearance priors from a video generative model. Specifically, GeoVerse extracts multilevel features from Wan2.2 VACE and injects them into the geometric latent diffusion model via a ControlNet-style adapter, incorporating video-learned appearance priors to enhance structural completion. To enforce cross-view coherence, a global spatial memory continuously aggregates observed and synthesized content, reprojecting target-aligned guidance to anchor subsequent predictions to a shared scene representation. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate improved visual quality and geometric consistency, with a 2.23 dB higher PSNR on DL3DV and 32.4% lower ATE on Mip-NeRF360 compared to GLD.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: DSWM: Decomposed Spatio-Temporal World Model for Demand-Driven UAV Base Station Repositioning
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Shengjie Zhong, Zhongliang Zhao, Jingxuan Chen, Xianbin Cao, Xinmei Qiang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The DSWM model enhances UAV base station repositioning by integrating demand-driven planning with a latent recurrent state, achieving superior performance across multiple datasets.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle base stations (UAV-BSs) are expected to cover traffic demand that shifts across space and time, yet most repositioning schemes either re-solve an optimization problem per slot or learn reactive policies without an explicit demand model. We cast demand-driven fleet repositioning as latent-space decision-time planning and propose DSWM, a decomposed spatio-temporal world model: an agentic controller that perceives the demand field through a rolling observation window, retains operational context in a latent recurrent state, reasons about candidate motions by imagined rollouts under an uncertainty penalty, and coordinates the fleet through replanned first actions. DSWM learns a recurrent state-space model shaped by an exponential-moving-average (EMA) based latent predictive objective with variance regularization. It attaches a differentiable service simulator that replays the association, probabilistic line-of-sight channel, and Shannon rate chain inside latent rollouts. Planning uses a cross-entropy method whose imagined demand is anchored on the current observation window with mixing coefficient $ρ=0.95$. On a unified pipeline over three real datasets (Milan CDR (call detail record), Shanghai Telecom, YJMob100K) and 14 methods including five reproduced IEEE baselines, DSWM attains weekday served ratios of 0.889, 0.908, and 0.898, ranking first among non-ablated configurations on every dataset. On Milan it improves over the strongest non-learning baseline (Greedy, 0.780) by 0.109, a margin that comes from decision-time use of observations rather than prediction accuracy.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: RoXDrive: Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Action-Faithful Rollouts
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Hongbin Lin, Chaoda Zheng, Yiming Yang, Xiangyu Li, Shijia Chen
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: RoXDrive is a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework that enhances end-to-end autonomous driving by ensuring action-faithful world-model rollouts, significantly reducing safety violations in real-world scenarios.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving policies are commonly trained via imitation learning on logged demonstrations without observing the consequences of their own actions, leading to causal confusion in closed-loop real-world deployment. To address this issue, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training offers a promising alternative by leveraging world models as interactive training environments to enable future scene generation for policy improvement. Nevertheless, existing approaches either rely on reconstruction-based simulators, offering limited counterfactual interaction, or adopt synthetic simulators to enable long-horizon closed-loop interaction at the cost of a substantial sim-to-real gap. Recently, video world models have exhibited the ability to generate realistic multi-step future rollouts but may not faithfully reflect action conditions, resulting in action-vision mismatch. In this paper, we introduce RoXDrive, a plug-and-play closed-loop RL framework that enables reliable policy optimization by identifying action-faithful world-model rollouts, consisting of two stages: 1) Model pre-training: In addition to imitation-based policy pre-training, we devise an Action-Vision Faithfulness Evaluator for inverse dynamics estimation with our geometry-aware auxiliary trajectory supervision, enabling long-horizon assessment of whether visual dynamics faithfully reflect the conditioning ego actions. 2) Action-faithful RL post-training: Agents iteratively interact with world models to form long-horizon scene rollouts, retaining only action-faithful ones for dense safety-aware scoring and scene-level closed-loop RL post-training. Extensive experiments on nuScenes and an in-house dataset with over 130K training scenarios demonstrate consistent gains across planners, reducing safety violations by 27.6% with DiffusionDrive on nuScenes and 33.7% with Qwen3-VL on the internal data.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: MVG-WAM: Multiple View Geometry-Aware World-Action Modeling for Robotic Manipulation
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Wenbo Chen, Tianfu Li, Haoxuan Xu, Zhihao Cao, Zhenghan Chen
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: MVG-WAM enhances robotic manipulation by integrating multi-view geometric relationships into action prediction, achieving high success rates in benchmark and real-world tasks.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: World-Action Models (WAMs) couple visual dynamics with action prediction, bringing the rich priors of pretrained video models to robotic manipulation. However, their multi-view interfaces typically tile images or concatenate tokens, leaving the geometric relationships among synchronized cameras implicit. This makes it harder to connect global scene context with the local geometry required for interaction. We introduce the Multi-View Geometry-Aware World-Action Model (MVG-WAM), which organizes these observations as related projections of one physical world rather than separate images on a canvas. Our model combines an epipolar-constrained global state with view-indexed geometric states jointly inferred from synchronized observations. Camera-aware routing supplies each video region with its corresponding geometric context and the shared global state, explicitly structuring the representation used for action prediction. We further ground the geometry-aware representation in metric scale through multi-horizon future-depth supervision, without requiring depth decoding during action rollout. MVG-WAM achieves average success rates of 99.1% on LIBERO and 92.07% on RoboTwin 2.0, demonstrating competitive performance across both benchmarks. Real-world experiments on Cobot Magic further demonstrate a 91.3% success rate across 150 trials spanning three manipulation tasks.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: SkillFlow: Flow-Driven Recursive Skill Evolution for Agentic Orchestration
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Tiesunlong Shen, Haoran Luo, Wenjin Liu, Zikai Xiao
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: SkillFlow introduces a flow-based framework for agentic task orchestration, enhancing skill evolution and credit assignment while outperforming existing methods across various complex tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: In recent years, a variety of powerful LLM-based agentic systems have been applied to automate complex tasks through task orchestration. However, existing orchestration methods still face key challenges, including strategy collapse under reward maximization, high gradient variance with opaque credit assignment, and unguided skill evolution whose decisions are typically made by directly prompting an LLM to judge rather than derived from principled training signals. To address these challenges, we propose SkillFlow, a flow-based framework that takes a trainable Supervisor as the agent and a structured environment with dynamic skill library and frozen executor, automating task orchestration through multi-turn interaction. SkillFlow employs Tempered Trajectory Balance (TTB), a regression-based flow-matching loss that samples trajectories proportional to reward, preserving diverse orchestration strategies rather than collapsing to a single mode. The same flow objective yields a jointly learned backward policy that provides transparent per-step credit assignment at zero additional inference cost. Building on these flow diagnostics, a recursive skill evolution mechanism determines when to evolve, what skills to create or prune, and where decision gaps lie -- closing the loop from training signal to autonomous capability growth. Experimental results on 14 datasets show that SkillFlow significantly outperforms baselines across question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and real-world interactive decision making tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/SkillFlow.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: ReactiveBFM: Reactive Closed-Loop Motion Planning Towards Universal Humanoid Whole-Body Control
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Xiao Chen, Weishuai Zeng, Xiaojie Niu, Zirui Wang, Jianan Li
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: ReactiveBFM is a real-time closed-loop motion planning framework that enhances humanoid agility and reactivity by mitigating exposure bias and enabling on-the-fly replanning.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: While current Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) provide robust control priors for humanoids, they only execute pre-defined reference motions. As a result, they are vulnerable to environmental shifts and incapable of reactive whole-body coordination. Naively cascading them with generative motion planners fails to achieve true reactivity, as inevitable tracking discrepancies induce fatal cumulative exposure bias. To bridge this gap, we propose ReactiveBFM, a real-time closed-loop planning-control framework. At its core, we effectively mitigate exposure bias via a scheduled prefix sampling curriculum, forcing the generative planner to actively learn error-recovery behaviors from imperfect physical states rather than ground-truth trajectories. Systematically, to reconcile the severe latency mismatch between auto-regressive planning and high-frequency tracking, we introduce an asynchronous replanning mechanism. Combined with trajectory chunking to temporally ensemble spatial references, our system guarantees spatio-temporally fluid execution without physical jitter. Deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid, ReactiveBFM demonstrates unprecedented physical agility across a vast repertoire of text-conditioned closed-loop motions. Notably, ReactiveBFM achieves zero-shot moving target reaching, showcasing intricate whole-body coordination and on-the-fly replanning. In sim-to-sim benchmarking under severe perturbations, ReactiveBFM achieves a 93.1% success rate, significantly outperforming cascaded open-loop baselines by 28.6%.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: In-Context Learning World Models for Robot Dual-Arm Manipulation of Soft Garment with Partial Observations
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Hengyi Sim, Quentin Rouxel, Dennis Hong, Darwin Caldwell, Fei Chen
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: This paper introduces a Soft-Object World Model leveraging in-context learning for dual-arm manipulation of garments, enhancing generalization and performance with minimal real-world data.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Robust manipulation of soft objects, such as garments, is a critical skill for service and household robots to adopt, but remains challenging due to its high-dimensional state space, and material-dependent deformations. Humans address this challenge by using mental world models that "imagine" the shape and material properties from partial observations, which enables them to predict how actions affect future states. As such, embedding such world models in robots allows for better generalization in manipulating a wide variety of garments in the real world. However, learned world models typically require large amounts of real world data that is strenuous to collect, and a mechanism to infer latent properties that govern dynamics. We present a Soft-Object World Model that performs generative full-state estimation and action-conditioned dynamics prediction using a transformer backbone trained on large-scale simulated soft object interactions, with measures to mitigate the sim-to-real gap. By learning to infer latent shape and material cues through in-context learning over a variable-length partial point-cloud history, the model generalizes across robot embodiments, material parameters, garment types and shapes, and manipulation coordination modes without weight updates. The world model is then integrated with a Goal-Conditioned action planner for motion synthesis. We validate the approach in simulation and real world for bimanual garment folding, reporting improvements in reconstruction fidelity, prediction accuracy, and task success.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: EBV-CAN: Vision--Language Grounding for Contact-Aided Endoscope Navigation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Chi Kit Ng, Shuchang Liu, Jinsong Lin, Yidong Zhang, Xizi Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: EBV-CAN integrates vision-language grounding for endoscope navigation, achieving high localization accuracy and successful task completion through a novel dataset and policy framework.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Flexible endoscopes exploit structural compliance to traverse narrow lumens, pipes, and cavities, where navigation involves distributed environmental contact. This compliance makes tip motion depend on the evolving support configuration. We present external bird's-eye-view contact-aided navigation (EBV-CAN), a vision-language policy that combines one initial global static bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state. Three supervised semantic queries locate the tip, next waypoint, and instructed target on the cached global image; their residual representations predict bending and insertion commands. We introduce the Vision-Language Contact-Aided (VLCA) dataset, linking 517 demonstrations and 75k action samples to 958k spatial entries and 93k remaining-route records. On 50 held-out episodes, tip-coordinate and waypoint localization reach 97.5% and 94.8%. Swapping the target instruction under identical observations changes target attention and motor output across 17 dual-target episodes. Across 1,920 physical trials of eight policies trained under a shared protocol, EBV-CAN achieves 183/240 successes (76.25%) under automatic blue-area scoring. Gated recurrent unit behavior cloning (GRU-BC) achieves the lowest matched-task offline mean absolute error (MAE), 0.056, and 1/240 physical successes, establishing distinct rankings for action imitation and task completion. Successful multi-guide executions and representative failures connect spatial progress, steering transitions, and visibility to physical navigation.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Zhefan Rao, Meng Chu, Xuan Zhang, Jingfan Chen, Guohao Cai
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper presents Dual Exam, a framework for evaluating the interaction between Multimodal Agents and World Models across various domains, revealing performance inconsistencies and challenges in reciprocal learning.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Han Hu, He Chen
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: This study evaluates the limitations of vision-language models in recognizing human activities through thermal imaging, revealing challenges in fine-grained action detection and reliability for human-robot interaction.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras. As vision-language models (VLMs), originally developed for RGB imagery, are increasingly integrated into embodied systems for scene understanding and high-level planning, thermal sensing offers a promising way to extend activity perception to low-light and privacy-sensitive settings. However, the failure modes of VLMs in thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction (HRI) remain underexplored. We fill this gap by evaluating seven locally deployable VLMs, including models developed for physical AI and robotics, on two person-centric thermal datasets. Our diagnostic tasks examine fine-grained action recognition, activity timeline reconstruction, and the ability to withhold unsupported answers. Paired RGB recordings serve as a performance reference, while controlled variations in frame sampling, thermal input presentation, and reasoning are used to assess whether the observed errors can be mitigated. Our results show that models can recognize broad activity categories but struggle with fine-grained actions such as coughing, sneezing, and yawning. They also produce inaccurate event timelines and hallucinate actions involving objects. Simple thermal input preprocessing and additional reasoning offer only limited, model-dependent gains. Abstention behavior also varies across models even under explicit instructions, limiting their reliability for practical robotic use.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Haoyue Liu, Xiaoying Tang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper reveals that world models misjudge returns due to inadequate representation of critical event transitions, suggesting improvements through targeted event patches for better planning accuracy.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. Across the 44 Atari-100k model--collection pairs that pass our reliability checks, including three released families, event patches outperform random patches in 39 (sign test p=1.4 x 10^{-7}), with a median gain of +44 percentage points. (2) The remaining error is structured: a complementary patch separates errors at true events from those elsewhere, while an eight-step timing tolerance recovers few events missed by our deterministic models. This structure also guides repair: a rule recorded before four repair outcomes were known predicts when a diffusion model repairs these failures. Event patches improve plan ranking, and the same concentration appears on control tasks with rare reward events.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Make it Walk: Computational Design of LEGO Walkers
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Siqi Li, Fancheng Gao, Chi-Wing Fu, Peng Song
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: This paper introduces a computational method for designing versatile LEGO walkers with stable locomotion and diverse gaits using innovative gear-linkage mechanisms and synchronized motor control.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: LEGO walkers are walking automata constructed from modular LEGO Technic bricks. They exhibit intriguing locomotion and are also highly reconfigurable through the modular Technic bricks, making them widely applicable in education, recreation, and robotics research. However, existing LEGO walkers are designed mostly by reusing existing single-actuator walking mechanisms. Although the locomotion is stable, their fixed walking gaits limit their adaptability and versatility. This paper presents the first computational solution capable of designing LEGO walkers that not only walk stably, but also support a variety of walking gaits. Our idea is twofold. First, we control the foot motion trajectory of each leg mechanically via a specifically-designed gear-linkage mechanism, in which we incorporate a pair of 3D-printed non-circular gears to work with a LEGO Technic mechanism. Second, we drive each leg by an independent motor and synchronize the timings of multiple leg motions via a simple yet adaptable control algorithm, enabling stable and versatile locomotion. Importantly, we take this modeling as a foundation to co-design the morphology and control of the LEGO walkers to meet the target locomotion and appearance. Leveraging our approach, we created a variety of LEGO walkers, demonstrating various walking gaits and appearances, and fabricated some of them to show their locomotion capability in the real world.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Liu Cao, Botian Xu, Ruoqu Chen, Jiajun Liu, Mingzhi Pei
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: HuMiT introduces a low-latency humanoid teleoperation system using a compact reference tracking policy, achieving competitive performance with minimal computational requirements.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Guidance in Robotic Neck Ultrasound
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Siqi Fan, Ran Liu, Zixuan Yang, Xiaoyu Fu, Xiaoqing Gao
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper presents a two-stage action-conditioned world model for guiding robotic ultrasound probes through anatomical landmarks, achieving notable success rates in real-world applications.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Ultrasound examinations typically follow specific scanning protocols that require navigating through an ordered sequence of anatomical landmarks and target imaging planes. We present a local action-conditioned world model framework for goal plane probe guidance in robotic ultrasound. Autonomous ultrasound tasks often require large numbers of probe-motion trajectories for training, but collecting high-quality demonstrations is labor-intensive and explicit simulators are difficult to build because ultrasound appearance depends on contact, tissue deformation, and view-dependent acoustic artifacts. We address this problem with a two-stage model-based learning pipeline. First, a latent conditional diffusion world model predicts future ultrasound observations from recent context frames, probe motions and temporal offset. Second, a goal-conditioned temporal transformer predicts ordered probe motions and is fine-tuned using rewards from the frozen world model. Experiments on the self-collected dataset show that the world model preserves action-dependent anatomical structure on target-directed scans. In real-world closed loop experiments, the framework achieves success rates of 70.0\% for carotid guidance and 65.0\% for thyroid guidance. These results demonstrate the potential of learned ultrasound dynamics for training goal-directed robotic probe navigation within protocol-constrained organ specific tasks.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Exploration via Activation-Space Steering for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Yunan Zeng, Jinhao Jing, Xi Cheng, Yuwang Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper presents Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), enhancing reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by diversifying training rollouts to improve reasoning performance on mathematical benchmarks.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-Math-17k, ASE improves average Mean@8 across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks over GRPO by 4.87 and 1.87 percentage points, respectively, under the same rollout budget.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: EchoNav: Evidential BEV Completion from Historical Observations for Visual Navigation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Diwen Liu, Yiyang Shao, Borui Wang, Chi Zhang, Yunhui Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: EchoNav introduces a novel evidential BEV completion framework for visual navigation, leveraging historical observations to enhance obstacle inference and achieve superior navigation success rates.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Visual navigation in cluttered environments requires robots to recover previously observed structure and infer obstacles and free space that remain occluded. We present a framework that combines temporal aggregation and occupancy completion in an evidential bird's-eye-view (BEV) representation predicted from short RGB sequences. A decoder adapts frozen VGGT-Omega features and combines historical residual proposals using cellwise weights and a learned no-update option. The BEV predictor produces a local map in the latest ego frame without depth or camera-pose inputs or explicit geometric warping. The evidential model treats observed free space separately and predicts occupancy with associated confidence across the remaining supported region. We train the predictor on simulated RGB sequences paired with complete and visibility-masked occupancy annotations. Our experiments evaluate navigation in simulation and on a wheeled robot, with additional demonstrations on quadruped and humanoid robots. In simulated sequential two-goal navigation, our system achieves 89.6% success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 32.5 percentage points. Across 60 wheeled-robot trials in 20 scenes, it achieves 73.3% success, compared with 33.3% for the strongest evaluated baseline.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Siyuan Ma, Yu Qi, Cheng Ye, Ruotian Peng, Xinyi Xu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper introduces RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal language models as judges of embodied video generation, revealing gaps in alignment with human judgments and presenting RoboJudge-9B as a superior model.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Provisioning Robust and Efficient LiDAR Perception for Autonomous Driving
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Tingxu Han, Zijie Shen, An Guo, Lyuke Wang, Chunrong Fang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: This paper presents a method for enhancing LiDAR perception in autonomous driving by improving robustness to point-cloud corruption while reducing latency and memory usage.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: LiDAR-based 3D object detection is a core perception service for autonomous driving, but deployment requires robustness to point-cloud corruption while meeting latency and memory requirements. Existing approaches address robustness and resource efficiency separately, resulting in compact detectors that are fragile under corruption or robust detectors that remain costly to deploy. We therefore formulate LiDAR perception provisioning as constructing a detector that remains accurate under point-cloud corruptions while meeting constraints on inference latency and peak GPU memory. To achieve robustness, we first craft corrupted samples that mimic extreme weather conditions. Then we train candidate detectors offline by ordering clean and corrupted samples by perturbation sensitivity, through which detectors learn more from hard corrupted samples. We estimate perturbation sensitivity using an ensemble of seven heterogeneous 3D detectors by tracking changes in confidence, BEV overlap, and unmatched detections. To improve efficiency, we narrow the network and use offline neighborhood-density measurements to determine how many points and neighbors each sampling stage processes. We evaluate our method using AP (Average Precision) under clean and corrupted conditions, inference latency, and peak allocated GPU memory. On KITTI for Car detection with PointRCNN, our method improves Moderate AP under corruption by 3.32 points over the original detector while reducing mean latency by 19.8% and peak allocated GPU memory by 53.9%. Across two datasets, two detector architectures, and three object classes, our method improves AP under corruption by 4.03 points on average over the corresponding original detectors, while reducing mean inference latency and peak allocated GPU memory by 14.4% and 38.0%, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/drunklibai/robust-efficient-lidar-perception.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Haocheng Wang, Youquan Liu, Weiyu Guo, Aokai Zhang, Donghang Wu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: RoboCasa-Shift introduces a benchmark for evaluating vision-language-action policy robustness in long-horizon tasks, highlighting the complexity of failure dynamics under distribution shifts.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Xinyu Fang, Yuchi Wang, Weihao Yu, Rongyao Fang, Zhaohai Li
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: BlenderWorld introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal models in realistic 3D creation tasks, revealing significant challenges in spatial coherence and structural accuracy.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: AffordanceWAM is a generative model that enhances robot manipulation by integrating affordance-aware predictions from diverse human videos and robot actions for improved interaction and performance.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Generalizable robot manipulation requires predicting how a scene will evolve, identifying where interactions are feasible, and determining how to act. Action-labeled robot videos directly supervise control but are costly and limited in diversity, whereas egocentric human videos capture diverse interactions but lack robot actions and differ in embodiment and appearance. We introduce AffordanceWAM, an affordance-aware generative World Action Model that represents object-centric spatiotemporal affordance through Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap, within the generated future World. This representation grounds visual prediction in task-relevantant objects and interaction regions for action generation, and provides shared interaction targets across human and robot videos. Built on a pretrained video diffusion Transformer, AffordanceWAM uses separately parameterized World and Action Experts, coupled through Masked Joint Self-Attention, to jointly predict future RGB observations, Scalar Affordance fields, Affordance Heatmaps, and continuous robot actions under a unified flow-matching objective. Human videos supervise all three future-World streams, whereas robot trajectories additionally provide action supervision, enabling transfer without human action labels or retargeting. Experiments on RoboCasa, CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D, and real-world manipulation demonstrate consistent gains over RGB-only and robot-data-only baselines. Under fixed robot supervision, RoboCasa performance improves monotonically as affordance-annotated human video scales. These results support affordance as an effective interface for both vision-language-action learning and human-to-robot transfer.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: When Does Backpropagating Through Policy Memory Matter? Separating Representation Credit from Closed-Loop Credit
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Xingjian Li, Jianhua Z. Huang, Junli Duan
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The study investigates the impact of memory credit routes in policy training, revealing that representation credit is crucial under noisy conditions, while closed-loop credit can be selectively truncated.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: When a policy with memory is trained through a differentiable simulator, credit can reach what it stores along two routes: \emph{representation credit} teaches the network that writes the memory what to summarize, while \emph{closed-loop credit} travels back through the physical states that earlier actions produced and that the memory later stored. Stopping gradients at stored history, as truncated backpropagation and Transformer-XL do, removes both routes at once. Keeping every forward computation identical and removing one route at a time, we trained Transformer policies for quadrotor tracking to determine when each route matters. Credit through memory improved learning only when velocity observations were noisy or hidden. When velocity was hidden, mildly decaying the gradient between consecutive physical states ($γ= 0.8$) eliminated the truncation cost of removing closed-loop credit while leaving representation credit essential, a separation that held in 14 of 16 new seeds. Two further systems bound this result: in a fixed-wing aircraft, representation credit could replace closed-loop credit on its own, leaving no cost to separate, and in a cart-pole, training with full state-edge credit was too unstable to compare the routes. In both the quadrotor and a fully observed vessel model, static gradient norms failed to predict which cut cost more, so memory truncation choices are best guided by short training runs.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: CoworkEnv synthesizes executable training environments for AI coworkers, enhancing coordination and communication capabilities through structured tasks and validation, leading to improved performance in long-horizon tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Weishuo Sun, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: TrajWAM introduces a trajectory-guided world action model that enhances dynamic robotic manipulation by predicting target motion and enabling efficient one-step action inference.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Hairuo Wei, Yunfan Ren, Renda Yang, Qiangsheng Huang, Zhongyu Li
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: This paper presents a LiDAR-inertial odometry framework for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots that learns motion uncertainty, significantly improving accuracy in challenging environments.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Bokang Yang, Jiaxu Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: Unisense is a unified MLLM framework that enhances embodied sensory understanding by integrating diverse modalities through a two-stage training process, outperforming existing models.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Recent embodied systems increasingly build on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for their pretrained understanding and reasoning capabilities, but their perception of the physical world remains largely limited to basic modalities such as vision and audio. However, broadening MLLMs to more diverse sensory modalities from the physical environment is challenging: their representations are often weakly connected to the MLLM and vary substantially in structure and statistics, while their interpretation still requires shared high-level understanding and reasoning. We therefore propose Unisense, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture. Unisense follows a two-stage training process: (i) aligning sensory representations with language to establish a language-accessible interface; and (ii) tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM to provide specialized processing for different sensory modalities. To support broad sensory learning, we curate Unisense-1M, a large-scale embodied sensory training corpus comprising 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities. We further evaluate Unisense on 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding. Across these heterogeneous sensing tasks, Unisense achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Yingshuang Zou, Xiaoyu Shi, Yawen Luo, Ziang Li, Qinghe Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: Mise-en-Video introduces a controllable multi-shot video generation framework that enhances narrative consistency and spatial control through hierarchical attention and 3D layout guidance.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: The paper presents FunCAD-Harness, a framework that improves functional CAD design by translating abstract requirements into physical tests, enhancing mechanism success rates through simulation feedback.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Ruixiang Wang, Qingming Liu, Yueci Deng, Guiliang Liu, Zhen Liu
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: EVA enhances video generative models for robotic planning by aligning visual outputs with executable actions through inverse dynamics rewards, reducing artifacts and improving task success.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Video generative models offer a promising basis for robotic planning by predicting future visual rollouts from observations and task instructions. However, their training objectives typically lack explicit constraints on robot executability. Generated rollouts can exhibit embodiment-related artifacts, including arm deformation and temporal discontinuities, while the actions decoded from these rollouts may be unstable or violate robot motion limits. We term this mismatch between generated robot behavior and embodiment-specific execution requirements the executability gap. We introduce Executable Video Alignment (EVA), a post-training framework that uses action-space feedback to improve both the visual integrity of generated robot motion and the feasibility of decoded actions. EVA trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on robot demonstrations and freezes it to decode actions from generated videos. We compute a reward from these actions that penalizes non-smooth motion and violations of velocity and acceleration limits, and use it to guide reinforcement-learning updates to the video generator. By feeding decoded-action constraints back into video generation, EVA links visual and action-level improvements through a shared alignment signal. Experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real bimanual robot show that EVA reduces embodiment-related visual artifacts and improves task success when executing IDM-decoded actions. Further experiments show that video models fine-tuned with EVA generate more effective video--action pairs for training downstream VLAs.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
机器人与人工智能实验室.authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
机器人与人工智能实验室.summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
机器人与人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

机器人与人工智能实验室.title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
