深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: When a policy with memory is trained through a differentiable simulator, credit can reach what it stores along two routes: \emph{representation credit} teaches the network that writes the memory what to summarize, while \emph{closed-loop credit} travels back through the physical states that earlier actions produced and that the memory later stored. Stopping gradients at stored history, as truncated backpropagation and Transformer-XL do, removes both routes at once. Keeping every forward computation identical and removing one route at a time, we trained Transformer policies for quadrotor tracking to determine when each route matters. Credit through memory improved learning only when velocity observations were noisy or hidden. When velocity was hidden, mildly decaying the gradient between consecutive physical states ($γ= 0.8$) eliminated the truncation cost of removing closed-loop credit while leaving representation credit essential, a separation that held in 14 of 16 new seeds. Two further systems bound this result: in a fixed-wing aircraft, representation credit could replace closed-loop credit on its own, leaving no cost to separate, and in a cart-pole, training with full state-edge credit was too unstable to compare the routes. In both the quadrotor and a fully observed vessel model, static gradient norms failed to predict which cut cost more, so memory truncation choices are best guided by short training runs.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: CoworkEnv synthesizes executable training environments for AI coworkers, enhancing coordination and communication capabilities through structured tasks and validation, leading to improved performance in long-horizon tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: TrajWAM: An Efficient Trajectory-Guided World Action Model for Dynamic Robotic Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Haohan Geng, Sha Zhang, Weishuo Sun, Guanting Ye, Wenhao Yu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: TrajWAM introduces a trajectory-guided world action model that enhances dynamic robotic manipulation by predicting target motion and enabling efficient one-step action inference.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires robots to anticipate target motion while replanning fast enough to avoid executing outdated actions. Existing approaches either rely on fast reactive control without an explicit future target state or encode anticipated motion only implicitly. World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising alternative by coupling future visual prediction with action generation, but scene-level video objectives may underrepresent target dynamics that are critical for manipulation, while iterative video-action denoising introduces substantial latency. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-guided world action model for efficient dynamic robotic manipulation. Our key insight is to explicitly ground future visual imagination in predicted target-object motion and use the resulting future representation to condition action generation, while preserving this anticipation pathway after acceleration. Given a short history of object masks, a history-conditioned motion predictor forecasts future masks encoding the target object's trajectory. A lightweight Trajectory ControlNet then steers a pretrained video model toward trajectory-consistent futures. The resulting future representation conditions an action expert to predict executable action chunks. To enable one-step inference without breaking this interface, we introduce a decoupled distillation scheme that combines distribution matching for the video backbone, Trajectory ControlNet realignment, and action rollout distillation to support accurate one-step action prediction conditioned on the compressed future representation. Comprehensive evaluations in simulation and the real world show that TrajWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on dynamic object manipulation tasks while enabling efficient one-step video-action inference. Project page: https://kevingeng3.github.io/TrajWAM/.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Learning Wheel Motion Uncertainty for Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry on Quadrupedal Wheel-Legged Robots
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hairuo Wei, Yunfan Ren, Renda Yang, Qiangsheng Huang, Zhongyu Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper presents a LiDAR-inertial odometry framework for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots that learns motion uncertainty, significantly improving accuracy in challenging environments.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Wheel kinematics can support odometry for quadrupedal wheel-legged robots when LiDAR geometry provides weak motion constraints. However, slip and contact loss make rolling predictions unreliable, and contact state alone cannot determine their reliability across motion directions. We propose a tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-kinematic odometry framework that retains analytical rolling predictions and learns per-wheel, direction-dependent process covariances from proprioceptive history. The estimator maintains moving wheel-center states, allowing the learned uncertainty to regulate the influence of rolling predictions through forward-kinematic corrections. Degeneracy-aware projection (DAP) complements this mechanism by suppressing LiDAR constraints along geometrically weak directions. The learned covariance network (CovNet) is trained through a differentiable filter using simulated velocity supervision and deployed on the real robot without fine-tuning. On the six room sequences with the highest degeneracy ratios in our indoor dataset, the method reduces mean per-sequence position root mean square error (RMSE) by 66.2% relative to FAST-LIO2 and by 31.0% relative to a fixed-covariance variant. In a severely degenerate corridor run, it achieves an endpoint position error of 0.198 m, compared with 7.531 m for FAST-LIO2. These results demonstrate robust odometry under challenging geometric and wheel-motion conditions. We plan to publicly release our code and multimodal dataset. Project website: https://weihairuo.github.io/wheel-motion-uncertainty/

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Beyond Omni: A Unified MLLM for Embodied Sensory Understanding
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Shiyun Xiong, Dongming Wu, Peiwen Sun, Bokang Yang, Jiaxu Wang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Unisense is a unified MLLM framework that enhances embodied sensory understanding by integrating diverse modalities through a two-stage training process, outperforming existing models.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Recent embodied systems increasingly build on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for their pretrained understanding and reasoning capabilities, but their perception of the physical world remains largely limited to basic modalities such as vision and audio. However, broadening MLLMs to more diverse sensory modalities from the physical environment is challenging: their representations are often weakly connected to the MLLM and vary substantially in structure and statistics, while their interpretation still requires shared high-level understanding and reasoning. We therefore propose Unisense, a unified embodied MLLM framework that supports diverse physical sensory modalities within a shared multimodal architecture. Unisense follows a two-stage training process: (i) aligning sensory representations with language to establish a language-accessible interface; and (ii) tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM to provide specialized processing for different sensory modalities. To support broad sensory learning, we curate Unisense-1M, a large-scale embodied sensory training corpus comprising 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities. We further evaluate Unisense on 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding. Across these heterogeneous sensing tasks, Unisense achieves strong performance and outperforms both generalist and specialized models on most benchmarks, demonstrating the potential of pretrained MLLMs as unified models for embodied sensory understanding.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yingshuang Zou, Xiaoyu Shi, Yawen Luo, Ziang Li, Qinghe Wang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Mise-en-Video introduces a controllable multi-shot video generation framework that enhances narrative consistency and spatial control through hierarchical attention and 3D layout guidance.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Wenqian Zhang, Yangyi Huang, Zigeng Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhen Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper presents FunCAD-Harness, a framework that improves functional CAD design by translating abstract requirements into physical tests, enhancing mechanism success rates through simulation feedback.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: EVA: Aligning Video World Models with Executable Robot Actions via Inverse Dynamics Rewards
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Ruixiang Wang, Qingming Liu, Yueci Deng, Guiliang Liu, Zhen Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: EVA enhances video generative models for robotic planning by aligning visual outputs with executable actions through inverse dynamics rewards, reducing artifacts and improving task success.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Video generative models offer a promising basis for robotic planning by predicting future visual rollouts from observations and task instructions. However, their training objectives typically lack explicit constraints on robot executability. Generated rollouts can exhibit embodiment-related artifacts, including arm deformation and temporal discontinuities, while the actions decoded from these rollouts may be unstable or violate robot motion limits. We term this mismatch between generated robot behavior and embodiment-specific execution requirements the executability gap. We introduce Executable Video Alignment (EVA), a post-training framework that uses action-space feedback to improve both the visual integrity of generated robot motion and the feasibility of decoded actions. EVA trains an inverse dynamics model (IDM) on robot demonstrations and freezes it to decode actions from generated videos. We compute a reward from these actions that penalizes non-smooth motion and violations of velocity and acceleration limits, and use it to guide reinforcement-learning updates to the video generator. By feeding decoded-action constraints back into video generation, EVA links visual and action-level improvements through a shared alignment signal. Experiments on RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real bimanual robot show that EVA reduces embodiment-related visual artifacts and improves task success when executing IDM-decoded actions. Further experiments show that video models fine-tuned with EVA generate more effective video--action pairs for training downstream VLAs.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Qize Yu, Jiadi You, Yuran Wang, Jiaqi Liang, Bowen Ping
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: AffordanceVLA introduces a structured affordance learning framework that enhances vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation through precise perception-action mappings.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Tianchun Wu, Zhiqing Tang, Hanlin Zhao
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: EndoVLA-OOV is a language-conditioned policy for robotic endoscopy that enhances out-of-view target acquisition, achieving up to 93.3% success through advanced vision-language-action integration.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Map2Vid introduces a novel framework for generating navigation videos from BEV maps, enhancing human-friendly control and evaluation through a large-scale dataset and integrated signals.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: MVISTA-4D: View-Consistent 4D World Model with Test-Time Action Inference for Robotic Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Jiaxu Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Tianlun He, Jingkai Sun, Qiang Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: MVISTA-4D introduces a view-consistent 4D world model for robotic manipulation, enabling comprehensive scene dynamics prediction and optimized action inference from single-view RGBD inputs.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: World-model-based imagine-then-act becomes a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, yet existing approaches typically support either purely image-based forecasting or reasoning over partial 3D geometry, limiting their ability to predict complete 4D scene dynamics. This work proposes a novel embodied 4D world model that enables geometrically consistent, arbitrary-view RGBD generation: given only a single-view RGBD observation as input, the model imagines the remaining viewpoints, which can then be back-projected and fused to assemble a more complete 3D structure across time. To efficiently learn the multi-view, cross-modality generation, we explicitly design cross-view and cross-modality feature fusion that jointly encourage consistency between RGB and depth and enforce geometric alignment across views. Beyond prediction, converting generated futures into actions is often handled by inverse dynamics, which is ill-posed because multiple actions can explain the same transition. We address this with a test-time action optimization strategy that backpropagates through the generative model to infer a trajectory-level latent best matching the predicted future, and a residual inverse dynamics model that turns this trajectory prior into accurate executable actions. Experiments on three datasets demonstrate strong performance on both 4D scene generation and downstream manipulation, and ablations provide practical insights into the key design choices.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: ELAN4D: Embodiment-Centric 4D Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models via Plug-and-Play Adaptation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Zeyuan He, Bowen Yang, Zhirui Fang, Keru Zhou, Lei Jiang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: ELAN4D enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating 4D predictive supervision from robot keypoint tracks, improving robustness and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promise for robotic manipulation, yet most existing policies operate reactively by directly regressing actions from current observations, without explicitly modeling future dynamics. This limits their ability to generalize under out-of-distribution perturbations. To address this issue, we propose ELAN4D, an embodiment-centric, 4D-aware training framework that enhances VLA policies with future robot keypoint tracks as predictive spatio-temporal supervision. Using only forward kinematics from proprioceptive states, we derive 3D displacement tracks of robot keypoints, such as joints and the end-effector, with negligible preprocess cost. These tracks provide metric and compact supervision without requiring external trackers or reconstruction. A plug-and-play auxiliary branch with a lightweight track decoder injects this 4D signal into the action expert while preserving the pretrained vision-language backbone through gradient isolation. The track decoder is discarded during inference, leaving the base policy interface unchanged. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0 and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that ELAN4D consistently improves over strong VLA baselines, achieving the best overall performance and substantial gains under out-of-distribution perturbations, including camera, background, and layout shifts. These results highlight the effectiveness of embodiment-centric 4D supervision for building more robust and generalizable manipulation policies.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework enabling humanoid robots to perform dynamic badminton skills and engage in multi-skill rallies with humans.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: High-speed racket sports provide a demanding testbed for humanoid robots, requiring time-critical decisions, precise striking, and dynamic whole-body coordination. In badminton, fast-changing shuttle trajectories require timely contact decisions, while successful returns demand precise racket pose and velocity within a brief contact window and across a broad three-dimensional striking workspace. Human motion data provide valuable priors for such athletic skills, but usable badminton references are limited and imperfect. Direct tracking provides insufficient executable variation for diverse shuttle conditions, while purely task-driven optimization may produce unnatural motion. We therefore present a three-stage hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic humanoid badminton. First, task-randomized motion augmentation expands sparse annotated hitting events into executable target-conditioned stroke variations, forming a continuous latent skill space. Second, a high-level planner outputs continuous latent skill codes to compose these skills online according to the observed shuttle state. Third, a context-conditioned adversarial regularizer encourages more natural planner-level skill usage while preserving return performance. In real-world deployment, our system sustains multi-skill rallies with human players, including forehand, backhand, and highly dynamic jump returns. This is the first real-world humanoid racket-sport system to demonstrate multi-skill human--robot rallies including highly dynamic jump returns.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: R$^2$ Flow introduces a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM-based agents that enhances task accuracy and skill evolution through flow-based training and evidence verification.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable procedures. Flow-based training fits this loop: it samples procedures in proportion to reward, and the flow through each skill credits it for the next library revision. Three obstacles stand in the way of making this self-improvement reliable: flow training suffers strategy collapse over tree-structured histories; nonnegative flow-based credit rewards frequent use as if it were benefit; and library edits rest on the task reward the policy optimizes. We introduce R$^2$ Flow, a recursive self-improvement framework that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates on a shared-state orchestration graph. The graph merges histories that differ only in the order of independent steps, allowing flow training to pool evidence across equivalent executions. A flow-share readout of the trained flow, invariant to the backward policy, and a separate signed utility rank which skills to change, verifier evidence decides whether an edit is warranted, and a residual-variance plateau sets when to update. Committed edits reshape the graph the next policy learns on, realizing recursive skill evolution. Across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, R$^2$ Flow improves task accuracy and library-edit precision over heuristic orchestration, reinforcement learning, and skill-evolution baselines, and transfers across executors. Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/r2flow.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: NativeMEM: Native Memory Compression for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Ziye Wang, Modi Shi, Chaojun Ni, Jiazhi Yang, Mengdi Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: NativeMEM introduces an efficient memory compression method for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing long-horizon robotic manipulation performance while reducing latency and memory usage.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: How can pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models retain long-horizon visual histories with high-frequency updates without sacrificing efficiency? Existing approaches rely on external memory management, which restrains either the memory horizon or the reactiveness of pretrained policies. To this end, we present NativeMEM, a VLA policy that features long-term and real-time updated memory. At its core is an efficient memory encoding scheme, Native Memory Compression, which repurposes the VLA's own vision encoder to compress each historical frame from each camera view into a single token. Appended to the input sequence, these memory tokens enable the pretrained VLA to attend over long-term history with negligible latency overhead, requiring neither an external planner nor a freshly initialized memory module. To align the memory tokens with the pretrained policy, we first develop a generic memory tokenizer under the supervision of a frozen VLA on memory-demanding data, and then unfreeze the VLA for task-specific fine-tuning. NativeMEM consistently outperforms prior methods, boosting success rates from 32.4% to 84.0% in simulation and up to 98.7% on real robots, while maintaining low inference latency and GPU memory usage. Notably, NativeMEM exhibits high data efficiency by achieving competitive results with prior arts using only 20% of the training data.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: FlexPart: Text-Controlled Semantics-Aware 3D Part Segmentation at Flexible Granularity
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yiqun Zhao, Jiachen Xu, Yihao Zhi, Yunfei Zhao, Zibo Zhao
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: FLEXPART is a novel framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation that enables flexible, semantics-aware part extraction, outperforming existing models in accuracy and granularity.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: A 3D asset admits multiple valid part decompositions, while semantics-aware segmentation should reflect both the desired granularity and the parts a user wants to extract. Ideally, a practical segmentation model should strive for a simple principle: what you ask for is what you get. However, realizing this goal is hindered by two core obstacles: the lack of multi-granularity training data and the absence of a holistic control mechanism. We propose FLEXPART, a unified framework for text-controlled 3D mesh segmentation. To establish flexible control, we introduce a holistic control prompt comprising semantic part names with location and shape clauses. To support this mechanism, we utilize an automated Vision-Language Model (VLM) pipeline to construct a large-scale dataset of multi-granularity partitions and their corresponding prompts. Driven by this data, FLEXPART generates a view-independent part-identity field in native 3D space, directly assigning discrete part IDs to mesh faces. To compel the model to respect semantic conditions rather than rely on geometric priors, we train the model using randomized background dropping. Furthermore, an inference-time VLM planner can automatically complete descriptive clauses from 2D renderings, allowing users to simply name the desired parts in ordinary words. FLEXPART with planner-completed prompts outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 15% in mIoU, even when that baseline receives ground-truth guidance. On our held-out FLEXPARTBENCH, FLEXPART leads at each granularity and improves average mIoU by 22% over the strongest baseline. With only the requested part names supplied by the user, it also improves IoU by 35% over the strongest click-driven baseline on selective segmentation.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: R$^2$Orch introduces a recursive self-play framework for agent orchestration that enhances skill learning and evaluation, outperforming traditional methods across various complex tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Reward Engine: Reward-Centric Self-Evolution for Open-Ended Tool Agents
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Litong Feng, Ji Qi, Yiran Cheng, Shaowu Pan, Xinyu Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The Reward Engine constructs a stable, experience-based reward system for open-ended tool agents, improving execution consistency and aligning closely with benchmark evaluations.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Open-ended tool agents can complete the same objective through different tool paths, and their quality depends jointly on the interaction trace, environment state, and final artifacts, so such tasks rarely admit an executable ground-truth reward. The central challenge is therefore to construct a reward from existing experience that exposes the current policy's failures while remaining stationary during optimization. We introduce Reward Engine, which, like a self-motivated student, first works out what success requires and then optimizes toward it. From the task and initial trajectories, it builds a RewardPack of testcases for required correctness and rubrics for graded quality, each executed as a check that returns a judgment with evidence. The frozen RewardPack then guides the agent to revise and select its outputs, and can also serve as a reward for reinforcement learning. On WorkBuddy Bench Office and Claw-Eval, the constructed reward largely agrees with the benchmark graders, not reversing their ordering on 82.3\% and 80.5\% of candidate pairs. Used to revise executions, it raises three-run consistency ($\mathrm{Pass}^{3}$) over Baseline from 45.0\% to 54.0\% and from 78.4\% to 83.7\%.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking with Diverse Dynamic Expressions
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yani Zhang, Dongming Wu, Wencheng Han, Xingping Dong, Shengcai Liao
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper introduces referring multi-object tracking (RMOT) to enhance object localization using diverse language expressions and a novel Transformer-based framework, TempRMOT, achieving state-of-the-art results.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Referring understanding is a fundamental task that bridges natural language and visual content by localizing objects described in free-form expressions. However, existing works are constrained by limited language expressiveness, lacking the capacity to model object dynamics in spatial numbers and temporal states. To address these limitations, we introduce a new and general referring understanding task, termed referring multi-object tracking (RMOT). Its core idea is to employ a language expression as a semantic cue to guide the prediction of multi-object tracking, comprehensively accounting for variations in object quantity and temporal semantics. Along with RMOT, we introduce a RMOT benchmark named Refer-KITTI-V2, featuring scalable and diverse language expressions. To efficiently generate high-quality annotations covering object dynamics with minimal manual effort, we propose a semi-automatic labeling pipeline that formulates a total of 9,758 language prompts. In addition, we propose TempRMOT, an elegant end-to-end Transformer-based framework for RMOT. At its core is a query-driven Temporal Enhancement Module that represents each object as a Transformer query, enabling long-term spatial-temporal interactions with other objects and past frames to efficiently refine these queries. TempRMOT achieves state-of-the-art performance on both Refer-KITTI and Refer-KITTI-V2, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach. The source code and dataset is available at https://github.com/zyn213/TempRMOT.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: PhyMix: Towards Physically Consistent Single-Image 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Implicit--Explicit Optimization
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Dongli Wu, Jingyu Hu, Ka-Hei Hui, Xiaobao Wei, Chengwen Luo
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: PhyMix introduces a framework that integrates a Physics Evaluator to enhance physical consistency in single-image 3D indoor scene generation, improving reliability for robotics and AI applications.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Existing methods for single-image 3D indoor scene generation often produce visually plausible results that violate real-world physical constraints, limiting their reliability in robotics, embodied AI, and virtual environment design. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics Evaluator that assesses four aspects (geometric priors, contact, stability, and deployability) through nine sub-constraints, establishing a benchmark for evaluating physical consistency. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art methods produce scenes with substantial physical inconsistencies despite their visual plausibility. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that incorporates feedback from the Physics Evaluator into both training and inference to improve the physical plausibility of generated scenes. Specifically, PhyMix comprises two components: (i) implicit alignment via Scene-GRPO, a critic-free group-relative preference optimization strategy that uses physical evaluations to guide the generator toward physically plausible layouts, and (ii) explicit refinement via verifier-guided agentic repair, which translates evaluator diagnostics into executable scene-editing skills to correct residual violations at inference time. PhyMix unifies physical evaluation, preference-based alignment, and agentic inference-time correction to improve physical plausibility while retaining the observed scene content. Experiments show improvements in reconstruction quality and physical plausibility, while qualitative examples on stylized and real-world images illustrate the applicability of the framework beyond synthetic inputs.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: ReTerm: Recovery Training for Self-Improving Terminal Agents
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Wei Xie, Kaituo Feng, Shiming Fu, Yong Liu, Xiangyu Yue
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: ReTerm enhances terminal agents' error recovery through self-improvement training, utilizing a custom dataset and an online RL algorithm, significantly boosting task completion rates.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Terminal agents have shown strong abilities in complex coding tasks. However, they often struggle to recover from errors during long-running execution (e.g., command errors, faulty implementations), eventually leading to task failures. To this end, we present ReTerm, a self-improving terminal agent trained by learning how to recover from its own failed terminal tasks. To support its training, we construct a customized data pipeline and produce ReTerm-10K, a high-quality dataset that provides effective recovery demonstrations for SFT cold start. Furthermore, we propose ReTerm-GRPO, an online RL algorithm that forks from the agent's own failure states to generate multiple independent self-recovery attempts. By learning from whether these attempts successfully complete the task, the agent self-improves through its own recovery experience. Built on Qwen3.5-9B, our ReTerm-9B achieves 34.8% Pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2.0, improving over the base model by 14.6 points. Further analysis shows that our method achieves consistently higher recovery rates across diverse error categories compared with standard GRPO training. All code, data and model are released at https://github.com/twothsnd/ReTerm.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: RoPE-Flow introduces an end-to-end framework for monocular robot pose estimation using flow matching, enhancing accuracy and consistency through innovative feature extraction and loss functions.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Anvil is a unified framework enhancing embodied spatial intelligence through innovative data generation, training, and benchmarking, significantly outperforming existing models in various benchmarks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Tianjiao Yu, Zhilin Ou, Yifan Shen, Xinzhuo Li, Yuanzhe Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: CoDA is a co-evolution framework that enhances robot training by integrating simulation data engines and action policies through a shared memory of failures and learning progress, significantly improving out-of-distribution success rates.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hengxuan Xu, Fengbo Lan, Zhixin Zhao, Shengjie Wang, Mengqiao Liu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The AIDE framework enhances robot interaction with ambiguous instructions by integrating vision-language reasoning and interactive exploration, achieving high success rates in task planning and execution.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Enabling robots to explore and act in unfamiliar environments under ambiguous human instructions by interactively identifying task-relevant objects (e.g., cups or beverages for "I'm thirsty") remains challenging for existing vision-language model (VLM)-based methods, due to inefficient reasoning and limited environmental interaction. These factors hinder real-time task planning and execution. To address this, we propose Affordance-Aware Interactive Decision-Making and Execution for Ambiguous Instructions (AIDE), a human-inspired dual-stream framework that integrates interactive exploration with vision-language reasoning: mirroring the complementary deliberative and intuitive processes of human cognition, Multi-Stage Inference (MSI) serves as the decision-making stream and Accelerated Decision-Making (ADM) as the execution stream, enabling zero-shot affordance analysis and interpretation of ambiguous instructions. Experiments in simulation and real-world settings show that AIDE achieves over 80% task planning success rate and more than 95% closed-loop continuous execution accuracy at 10 Hz, surpassing existing VLM-based methods in diverse open scenarios.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Ming Shin Cindy Sung, Duan Leijiahao, Haoxiang Wang, Boning Tan, Liangna Fu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: LIBERO-Industry introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation under industrial constraints, revealing performance degradation with increasing complexity across various task scenarios.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hanzhen Wang, Boxiang Lyu, Zhongxiang Dai, Siyang Gao, Dake Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper presents novel offline reinforcement learning algorithms using optimized certainty equivalents, establishing theoretical bounds and addressing risk sensitivity in decision-making under uncertainty.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Automated Reward Design
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Sitao Cheng, Tianle Li, Xuhan Huang, Xunjian Yin, Difan Zou
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL) enhances automated reward design by using a dual-training framework that adapts reward structures based on inner policy performance feedback.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Crafting effective reward signals remains a central challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) for complex reasoning. Existing methods for automated reward optimization search with a fixed proposer which never learns from its costly trials. We present Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL), a dual-training framework for autonomous discovery of reward structures. An outer-loop proposer composes a reward from task primitives, and an inner policy trains with this reward. The proposer itself learns by policy gradient from the validation performance of the inner policy. Thus, DERL utilizes past-trial feedback to shape its reward-proposal distribution, an empirical meta-gradient of task success. We validate DERL on embodied (ALFWorld), scientific (ScienceWorld), and mathematical (GSM8K, MATH) reasoning. On multi-turn agent benchmarks, DERL outperforms strong baselines, significantly on out-of-distribution tasks. In mathematics, DERL improves on the outcome reward where directly added primitives hurt. Further analyses under matched compute show that our proposer effectively captures the meta-gradient to discover useful reward signals.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: VGGT-Diff: Visual Geometry Meets Diffusion for Sparse-View Novel View Synthesis
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Shijia Chen
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: VGGT-Diff integrates geometry-based routing with a diffusion model for enhanced novel view synthesis from sparse views, achieving state-of-the-art performance through robust conditioning and consistency techniques.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: We present VGGT-Diff, a geometry-routed multi-view diffusion model for sparse-view novel view synthesis. Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods face a fundamental trade-off: reconstruction-based approaches preserve observed geometry but struggle to synthesize unseen regions, while diffusion-based methods provide strong generative priors yet rely on implicit source-to-query correspondence. VGGT-Diff bridges these regimes by routing visual geometry latents from VGGT-Ω into a pretrained video diffusion model. Each visual token is associated with a 3D point and confidence, then transformed into query-aligned latent conditions through a confidence-aware Visual Geometry Router (VGR) that preserves front and back surface evidence. These conditions guide joint target-view denoising, while Point-Track Residual Consistency (PTRC) regularizes predicted-clean residuals along reliable 3D tracks, improving multi-view stability. We further introduce robust geometry conditioning, combining training-time regularization with inference-time guidance for improved robustness. Experiments show competitive or state-of-the-art performance across interpolation and extrapolation under different viewpoint difficulties. Our code is available at https://github.com/chenkangjie1123/VGGT-Diff.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Xin Li, Xiaohuan Gu, Yifan Wang, Shaobin Ling, Tianli Shi
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent, enhances embodied spatial intelligence by diagnosing failures and refining strategies through metacognitive reflection and memory consolidation.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: EvoWeave: Composing Reusable Agent Experience through Operation Level Graphs
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Guanhua Zhu, Bo Shen, Lei Zhang, Fadi Deek, Zhi Wei
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: EvoWeave is a framework that enhances interactive agents' task performance by efficiently composing reusable operations through a structured experience memory and dependency graph.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Different tasks often require interactive agents to perform similar operations at intermediate steps. Retrieving an entire past workflow can introduce irrelevant steps, whereas retrieving isolated operations can discard the dependencies needed to reuse them. We introduce EvoWeave, a framework for experience memory that represents abstract states as nodes and reusable operations as directed edges with input and output contracts, provenance, and capability references. A planner decomposes the current task into a dependency graph; operation retrieval and bounded directed search then assemble relevant experience fragments. An execution agent can inspect these fragments and their referenced capabilities, while reflection separates concrete execution evidence from reusable abstractions. We study the framework across four benchmarks, five evaluation settings, and three language model backbones. Across backbones, AppWorld Normal and Challenge task goal completion average 51.91 and 27.99, respectively, exceeding the baseline without memory by 6.99 and 4.99 percentage points. An AppWorld ablation associates directed connections with an additional improvement of 2.08 points over independent operation cards. The results motivate composition of reusable operations while exposing tradeoffs in retrieval overhead and conditions for valid reuse.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Tong Lei, Dahan Wang, Peter Bell
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper explores how different textual interface designs impact prompt optimization for audio-visual question answering in multimodal reasoning systems, revealing trade-offs in interpretability and optimization difficulty.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) has shown strong effectiveness for text-based LLMs and LLM systems, but its application to audio-visual understanding systems requires suitable textual interfaces through which multimodal reasoning can be exposed to text-based optimizers. We investigate how the design of textual interfaces affects prompt optimization for multimodal reasoning, on the audio-visual question answering task. We compare three interface designs, including a direct inference system consisting of a single omni-modal large language model (OmniLLM), a captioner-reasoner system, and an agentic architecture in which a primary agent orchestrates subagent OmniLLMs. Experiments with Qwen3-Omni and Gemini show that direct prompt optimization provides model-dependent gains; the captioner-reasoner system and the agentic system expose more interpretable optimization interfaces but are harder to optimize, where error analysis of cases affected by optimization is conducted. Our study highlights textual interface design as an important factor in making prompt optimization effective for omni-modal reasoning systems. Our implementation details are specified in GitHub repo.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: This paper outlines the evolving concept of agentic robots, categorizing research into four domains while addressing challenges and future directions for enhancing robotic intelligence and adaptability.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: ReAT: Residual Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Robot Policies
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Dijia Zhan, Zhuo Li, Xuemiao Xu, Sun Zheng, Jinyi Li
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper presents Residual Action Tokenization (ReAT), enhancing autoregressive robot policies by enabling tokens to iteratively refine action reconstructions, improving performance across various tasks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Autoregressive robot policies rely on action tokenizers to convert continuous action chunks into compact sequences of discrete prediction targets. Existing tokenizers can reconstruct action chunks from discrete codes, but often leave implicit what each individual token contributes to the reconstructed action. We introduce Residual Action Tokenization (ReAT), which gives each token an explicit role in refining the current action reconstruction. It uses the decoded reconstruction as feedback to construct the next token from the remaining action error. This closes the loop between encoding and decoding, making each new token responsive to the errors left by the actual decoded prefix. Across 19 manipulation tasks spanning three simulation benchmarks and real-world settings, 8-token ReAT policies outperform the evaluated baselines in task success; on LIBERO, even 4-token ReAT surpasses the evaluated 8-token action-tokenization baselines at half the token budget. These results suggest a path toward action tokenization that supports self-corrective policy learning, helping autoregressive policies learn to progressively refine their own action plans.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: EndoRSI: Physical-Evidence-Driven Recursive Improvement of Endoscopic Robot Policies
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Tianchun Wu, Siu Hing Lui, Hanlin Zhao
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: EndoRSI is a self-improving robotic system that refines endoscopic policies through iterative physical experimentation and human oversight, significantly enhancing insertion success rates.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Artificial intelligence is beginning to automate scientific discovery, yet physical robot-policy research still relies on scientists and engineers to interpret experimental failures and decide how controllers should be revised. We present EndoRSI (Endoscopic Recursive Self-Improvement), a human-governed, self-improving robotic research system in which the embedded EndoForge coding agent iteratively develops and refines endoscopic robot policies using evidence from physical experiments. Physical execution remains isolated within a safety-constrained runtime under human authorisation. In motorised endoscopy, validation evidence first caused the agent to reject an initial action representation, while subsequent physical experiments falsified an offline-supported insertion strategy by revealing hazardous closed-loop behaviour absent from the source data. Failed physical rollouts were then incorporated into policy revision; insertion success subsequently increased from 2/21 in the first generation to 17/21 in the fourth. The frozen final policy retained competence across visual and hardware shifts and was the best performing autonomous policy across six independent ex-vivo porcine specimens. These results show that physical robot interaction can serve as experimental evidence for agent-driven robot policy research.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Jingwei Song, Zhisheng Chen, Bingfan Zeng, Jing Tang, Yubo Hou
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: MC-EvoBench is a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to evaluate and audit the transferability and durability of embodied capabilities in self-improving agents.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: A central challenge in embodied recursive self-improvement is enabling agents to convert interaction history into capabilities that persist beyond one world and transfer to later tasks. A saved memory or successful final action does not by itself establish that a reusable capability was acquired; evaluation must separate capability change from carried-over resources, unequal source exposure, and early execution failures. We construct MC-EvoBench as a controlled Minecraft benchmark with a fixed catalog of 19 registered evolution chains, including 12 primary evaluation chains and seven calibration or probe chains, together with three graph-aligned paired probe families for transfer. The benchmark represents each task as a task-state graph, defines stage-level environment verifiers, assigns matched source and target roles, resets the target world, and permits only a declared agent artifact to cross the source-target boundary. For each probe, no-prior, related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions are evaluated under matched environment-step budgets and five seeds; we report TSR, WGP, and VMP and retain provenance records. The benchmark reveals a consistent direct-capability gap between controller and planner-backed variants, while related experience yields no stable transfer: it does not improve either tool probe, its small wood-species gain hinges on one seed, and all intervals include zero. Stage audits further show that early wood-collection and crafting bottlenecks often leave later capabilities unobserved. MC-EvoBench thus offers a controlled testbed for durable, transferable embodied capabilities. Code and data are available at https://github.com/xzw-ustc/mc-bench-open-source

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yuhong Liu, Shenxi Wu, Junyi Chi, Beichen Zhang, Xuanlang Dai
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: SpatialASM enhances Large Vision-Language Models by integrating Active Spatial Mentalization through training-time spatial simulation, improving their spatial reasoning capabilities across multiple benchmarks.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: When solving complex spatial reasoning tasks, ordinary humans naturally revisit the scenes from task-relevant viewpoints and mentally reconstruct the spatial layouts from those viewpoints. But can Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) proactively think in the same way? We term this ability Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM), an intrinsic component of visual intelligence that remains substantially underdeveloped in current LVLMs. To bridge this gap, we introduce SpatialASM, a scalable framework to internalize ASM into LVLMs through training-time spatial simulation. SpatialASM employs an allocentric novel-view generator to ground hypothetical viewpoints in visual evidence and produces two complementary forms of supervision: i) explicit ASM trajectories that teach LVLMs when and how to adaptively invoke view planning and imagination during spatial reasoning, and ii) automatically-constructed perspective-taking tasks that further strengthens viewpoint-conditioned scene imagination. On seven benchmarks spanning relatively perception-oriented spatial understanding to more challenging tasks requiring multi-image, cross-view and viewpoint-transformation reasoning, SpatialASM yields performance gain on LVLMs of four LVLM backbones in spatial reasoning while retaining their original general vision capabilities. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves average accuracy across the seven spatial benchmarks. And the synthesis of ASM trajectories provides a scalable pathway to alleviate the scarcity of spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision for eliciting active viewpoint exploration and mental scene simulation.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Xinzhe Wang, Changjian Jiang, Kaiwen Song, Xudong Li, Kerui Ren
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: MIRAGE integrates feed-forward visual geometry with LiDAR-IMU data for accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity Gaussian reconstruction, outperforming existing vision-only methods.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. In contrast, LiDAR--inertial estimation provides metrically accurate motion but lacks the image-space consistency needed for high-fidelity reconstruction. We propose $MIRAGE$, which anchors feed-forward visual geometry to LiDAR--IMU metric motion and regulates online pose corrections according to correspondence support and cross-modal agreement, jointly enabling accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity Gaussian reconstruction. Experiments on Oxford Spires, M2DGR and INS show that MIRAGE achieves accurate metric trajectory estimation, outperforming COLMAP, a widely used but computationally expensive reference for vision-only benchmarks. Motivated by the scarcity of long-horizon monocular benchmarks for large-scale indoor reconstruction, we further build a multimodal data-collection platform and use MIRAGE to establish accurate 6-DoF reference trajectories for a new vision-only benchmark. We benchmark recent monocular large-scale reconstruction methods on this dataset, providing a systematic evaluation of their performance in long-horizon indoor scenes.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: PartiGen: Part-Aware Representations for Language-Conditioned Humanoid Motion Generation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Chuxuan Huang, Zhanxiang Cao, Tianyue Zhan, Haoyang Li, Yang Zhang
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: PartiGen is a part-aware framework that generates humanoid motion from language by integrating anatomical structure and improving kinematic consistency, achieving significant performance enhancements in simulation and real execution.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Translating language into humanoid motion requires coordinating body parts, determining motion duration, and producing references suitable for robot execution. We introduce PartiGen, a part-aware latent diffusion framework that incorporates anatomical structure into a shared whole-body motion representation. Part-specific attention processes anatomically masked frame features, and its outputs are fused to combine local limb information with whole-body context. Conditioned on text and motion history, the model generates motion primitives autoregressively. Forward-kinematics supervision encourages kinematic consistency, while a learned end-of-sequence predictor selects a frame-level endpoint after generation. On HumanML3D retargeted to the Unitree G1, PartiGen achieves a segment-level FID of 3.165, a 16.8% reduction over TextOp, and improves R@1 by 1.4 percentage points. In the duration study with 16-frame primitives, endpoint prediction reduces mean absolute duration error from 12.471 to 3.080 frames compared with a fixed-length cutoff. We further evaluate robot execution using a pretrained, frozen GRIT tracker: 409 of 500 generated references (81.8%) pass the posture-based stability screen in MuJoCo. Following simulation screening and manual selection, 26 of 27 attempted motions are judged successful on the real G1.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Self-Evolving Spatial Reasoning in Vision Language Models via Geometric Logic Consistency
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Junming Liu, Yuqi Li, Yifei Sun, Maonan Wang, Yiming Cheng
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The SAGE framework enhances spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models by integrating geometric logic consistency and self-evolution, improving robustness and generalization across transformations.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made striking progress, yet their spatial reasoning remains fragile. Models that answer an original input correctly can still fail under valid transformations with predictable answer mappings, revealing a gap between instance-level correctness and robust spatial reasoning. To address this, we propose Spatial Alignment via Geometric Evolution (SAGE), a self-evolving framework that improves robust spatial reasoning through geometric and linguistic duality operations. SAGE incorporates duality consistency into GRPO training, encouraging models to produce coherent answers across original and transformed inputs. SAGE co-evolves duality generation and solution, allowing the model to continually expose and address its own reasoning weaknesses. A dynamic operation pool identifies challenging operations and retires mastered ones, keeping training focused on informative duality signals. SAGE is model-agnostic, data-efficient compared to prior post-training methods, and can be applied as a lightweight adaptation stage to any existing VLM. Experiments on video and spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines and enhanced generalization to unseen data.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Environmental Feedback Modeling Matters: Rethinking Feedback Treatment in Agentic Hindsight Self-Distillation
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Hangxi Guo, Fengyuan Liu, Yue Wang, Yuhua Qi, Haoyi Xiong
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).summary: The paper introduces SELF, a framework that enhances reinforcement learning by optimizing environmental feedback modeling alongside hindsight self-distillation, significantly improving agent performance.
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning is commonly used to train language agents in interactive environments, but cannot be directly applied when rewards are unavailable. Recent methods use environmental feedback as privileged context for hindsight self-distillation, but our analysis suggests that simply conditioning the teacher on feedback is insufficient, motivating us to rethink how environmental feedback is used in agentic self-distillation. Given that environmental feedback contains rich supervision for modeling how the environment responds to agent actions, we introduce \textit{agentic SElf-distilLation with environmental Feedback modeling} (SELF), a framework that jointly optimizes environmental feedback modeling and hindsight self-distillation. SELF learns to predict environmental responses while distilling guidance from a feedback-conditioned self-teacher into the policy. Our analysis reveals a mutually reinforcing mechanism: environmental feedback modeling strengthens hindsight supervision and policy learning, while self-distillation enhances the model's ability to model environmental feedback. With Qwen3-8B, SELF outperforms SDPO and GRPO by 6.4 and 4.1 percentage points in $τ$-bench success rate, and by 10.71 and 3.57 percentage points in AppWorld task goal completion, respectively. These results show that SELF uses environmental feedback more effectively within agentic self-distillation, improving agent capabilities.

深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
深圳市人工智能与机器人研究院 (AIRS).authors_text: Yi Ma, Tianpei Yang, Yaodong Yang, Weixun Wang, Hongyao Tang
