The key insight is that rollouts reaching corresponding physical situations can serve as references for one another: their terminal outcomes provide evidence for assessing local progress. We introduce Physical Relations for Inferring Credit from Episodes(PRICE), with two components: (i) a physical relational graph that pools current and historical outcomes at corresponding chunk boundaries to estimate success potentials; and (ii) confidence-gated credit assignment that uses changes in these potentials to refine trajectory-level supervision. Our analysis connects oracle potential changes to the terminal-success objective and provides a finite-sample directional bound for outcome-independent evidence pools. Independent continuation tests show that PRICE's retained credits align with local progress, while experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real robots demonstrate improved task success over outcome-based baselines and faster learning.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: ETHER: Aligning Emergent Communication for Hindsight Experience Replay
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Kevin Yandoka Denamganaï, Daniel Hernandez, Ozan Vardal, Sondess Missaoui, James Alfred Walker
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: ETHER enhances Hindsight Experience Replay in goal-conditioned RL by using Emergent Communication to learn goal relabelling and predicate functions from natural language instructions.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) enhances sample efficiency in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) by relabelling failed trajectories with goals that were actually achieved. However, HER assumes access to a goal relabelling function and a predicate function that determines whether a goal has been satisfied. These assumptions break down in instruction-following tasks, where goals are expressed in natural language and differ from the state space. We formalize this as the Hindsight Reinforcement Learning problem, which shows the need to jointly learn these functions alongside the RL policy. To address it, we propose ETHER (Emergent Textual Hindsight Experience Replay), an agent that leverages Emergent Communication. ETHER uses a referential game (RG) to train a speaker and a listener to develop a grounded, artificial language describing environment states. It partially aligns this emergent language with instruction language using co-occurrence patterns between task instructions and RL observations. Experiments on BabyAI's PickupDist task show that ETHER's learned RG speaker and listener can function as the goal relabelling and predicate functions of HER, improving sample efficiency despite imperfect language alignment. Our work bridges Emergent Communication and goal-conditioned RL, opening the door to wider applications of HER.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: CAST: Causal Advantage-Structured Training with Spatially Grounded Compositional Rewards for Diffusion Models
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Shu Yu, Chaochao Lu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: CAST enhances diffusion model training by optimizing SDE window selection, decomposing rewards into verifiable semantic units, and improving sample efficiency, achieving significant performance gains.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Online reinforcement learning has been extended to flow matching for diffusion model (DM) image generation. However, this paradigm faces three limitations: (1) Window selection. Existing methods manually set the stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling window, i.e., the denoising steps where exploration noise is injected. We instead determine it from each model's denoising trajectory. (2) Reward saturation. Current methods rely on scoring models trained on human annotations; we find that such scores are extremely high and nearly indistinguishable on the latest SOTA open-source DMs, making advantage estimation largely ineffective. (3) Sample inefficiency. A single scalar reward collapses different failure modes into almost identical scores, leaving minimal gradient guidance for targeted improvement. To address these issues, we propose CAST (Causal Advantage-Structured Training), an RL fine-tuning method for pretrained DMs, which (1) identifies the denoising step at which each model fixes the objects and their spatial arrangement in the image and uses that timing to set the SDE window, (2) decomposes each prompt via Causal Scene Graphs (CSG) into verifiable-atoms, i.e., minimal semantic units such as an object, count, attribute, or spatial relation that can each be checked independently, and rewards each atom separately, and (3) projects the signed atom-level advantages into pixel space through teacher-forced attention and uses them to spatially weight the SDE policy objective. We fine-tune two of the strongest open-source DMs, FLUX.2-dev and Qwen-Image-2512, with CAST, and evaluate them on GenEval 2, a compositional benchmark, and on Qwen-Image-Bench for overall quality. Within almost the same training budget, CAST's improvement over the base model on the most challenging GenEval 2 prompts is up to 3.07x that of Flow-GRPO, while overall generation quality also improves.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: LIBERO-Agent: Evaluating General-Purpose Agents for Direct Embodied Manipulation
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Zijie Diao, Yitong Chen, Sicheng Xie, Tianyi Lu, Wujian Peng
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: LIBERO-Agent benchmarks general-purpose agents in robotic manipulation, revealing performance gaps in complex tasks and highlighting GPT-6 Astra's strengths and weaknesses in interaction and execution.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: General-purpose agents can plan, use tools, and revise their behavior from feedback, but it remains unclear whether these capabilities transfer from digital environments to embodied manipulation. To investigate this question, we introduce LIBERO-Agent, an agent-native benchmark for evaluating these agents in robot manipulation tasks. Rather than asking agents to submit task-level Python control programs or operate through high-level robot skills, LIBERO-Agent provides an interactive robotic environment where agents can select which observations to inspect, process them with their own tools, and issue native action commands. LIBERO-Agent integrates 200 tasks into a common interaction framework and provides a 30-task primary suite that separates perception, short-horizon execution, and long-horizon composition. Results reveal a pronounced reliability gap: while agents perform well on perception and easy short-horizon tasks, their performance degrades substantially on hard short-horizon and long-horizon tasks. Richer observations improve short-horizon manipulation, while demonstration benefits depend on the agent and format. Among these agents, GPT-6 Astra achieves the strongest overall performance. Further analysis shows its major advantage lies in mechanism interaction, especially when sustained physical contact is needed, while its remaining failures stem from cross-stage interference and geometric errors.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Learning Skills from Historical Action Trajectories: Action Experience Dictionary for World Action Models
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Qi Lyu, Jiahua Dong, Hao Shen, Xudong Wang, Hongyuan Yu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: This paper presents an Action Experience Dictionary (AED) that enhances World Action Models by enabling skill reuse and improving action prediction through historical trajectory encoding and motion-aware supervision.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) couple visual dynamics prediction with action generation, yet they do not explicitly support the reuse of action experience across manipulation tasks. Furthermore, existing WAMs struggle to capture underlying cross-task semantic relationships that could guide target action prediction, as redundant background elements interfere with the extraction of key visual information. To address these challenges, we develop a novel Action Experience Dictionary (AED) that encodes historical physical action trajectories into shared action embeddings to support skill reuse and model cross-task relationships. Specifically, we first aggregate historical actions to align with visual observations and retrieve action embeddings from the AED using a pretrained action tokenizer. Subsequently, we visually condition the pooled embeddings through cross-attention and prepend them to noisy action tokens, providing interaction context and action intent for prediction. To model action-related motion and reduce reliance on irrelevant background cues, we introduce a motion-aware transition loss that supervises visual feature change prediction over random temporal intervals. Experiments on simulation benchmarks and in real-world cross-embodiment settings verify the effectiveness of our AED. The anonymous project website is available at \href{https://github.com/JiahuaDong/AED}{AED}.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: EviRover: Reinforcing Agentic Perception Beyond a Glance
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Kaixuan Fan, Kaituo Feng, Tianshuo Peng, Yilei Jiang, Manyuan Zhang
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: EviRover introduces an agentic perception model that enhances visual understanding through interactive learning, outperforming traditional methods and benchmarks in complex scenarios.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Visual perception is conventionally formulated as a one-shot prediction from a single glance at the image, under the assumption that the image content and the model's parametric knowledge suffice to resolve the query. This assumption often fails in real-world scenarios that hinge on fine-grained visual details or require knowledge-intensive and up-to-date information. We term such cases \textit{perception under insufficient evidence} and formulate perception as an agentic process that can obtain information beyond a single glance. To address the absence of data for this setting, we design two dedicated data generation pipelines, yielding EviRover-SFT-5K and EviRover-RL-12K for training. We further construct EviLens, a human-verified benchmark comprising 688 instances across five perception categories. Building on these data, we present EviRover, to our knowledge the first perception agent explicitly trained to resolve perceptual queries through interaction, using supervised fine-tuning followed by agentic reinforcement learning. Experiments show that the 4B EviRover outperforms its backbone by 30 points on average on EviLens, reaching performance comparable to advanced proprietary models. The gains transfer beyond EviLens to WebEyes, conventional perception benchmarks, and general multimodal benchmarks, including a 15-point improvement on BrowseComp-VL. All code, models, and data are released.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: UniWAM Technical Report: Unified Mobile Manipulation via Mixed-Stream World-Action Modeling and Manipulation Anchor Pose Supervision
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Wei Xue, Keliang Liu, Mingzhang Cui, Jinhua Xie, Jinjie Wei
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: UniWAM integrates mixed-stream world-action modeling with Manipulation Anchor Pose supervision, enhancing mobile manipulation performance through joint representation learning and large-scale data utilization.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Mobile manipulation requires precise navigation to a manipulation-ready pose followed by reliable object interaction. These two stages differ in action spaces and visual requirements, which complicates unified policy learning. In addition, collecting diverse real-world navigation data with explicit manipulation-ready pose supervision remains costly and difficult to scale. We introduce UniWAM, a unified mixed-stream world-action model with separate action encoders and output heads for navigation and manipulation, sharing a common backbone. This design supports joint representation learning on independently sampled navigation and manipulation data. UniWAM supports independent inference for either stream and batch-parallel inference for both. We further introduce Manipulation Anchor Pose (MAP) supervision for where to stop and how to orient for manipulation. An automated pipeline constructs MAP-Data from large-scale 3D scenes, yielding over 1.5 million episodes and 7,500 hours. MAP-Data provides per-frame target-object bounding boxes and image-plane MAP coordinates as auxiliary navigation supervision. Together with projected end-effector trajectories for manipulation, these prediction targets provide stream-specific image-plane supervision for action learning from egocentric observations. With large-scale MAP-Data, UniWAM outperforms the strongest external baselines on our MAP-Bench by 30.1\% in position error and 44.0\% in heading error. Across 24 real-robot tasks, UniWAM achieves leading results in MAP navigation and mobile manipulation, with competitive manipulation performance. We have released code, data, and benchmark.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Ego4WAM: What Matters When Scaling Egocentric Human Data for Robot Learning?
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Zhihao Sun, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Haoyi Jiang, Wei Feng
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: Ego4WAM systematically analyzes how human-robot alignment, task diversity, supervision, and data usage strategies influence the effectiveness of egocentric human data in robot learning.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Egocentric human data provides a scalable source of experience for robot learning, but varies substantially in human-robot alignment, behavioral coverage, and available supervision. Existing work shows favorable scaling with increasing human data, but it remains unclear which data properties drive downstream robot gains and how to use such data throughout the training pipeline. We present a systematic study of egocentric human data with different alignment and supervision under a unified world-action model framework. With the model backbone fixed, we disentangle the effects of human-robot alignment, data duration and task diversity, action supervision, and data usage strategies. We find that aligned human demonstrations substantially improve out-of-distribution generalization and reduce target-task robot data requirements; data duration and task diversity affect downstream capabilities differently; and video-only supervision remains effective without action labels, providing a strong foundation for subsequent video-action training. We validate these findings through closed-loop policy evaluation on both real robots and RoboDojo. Rather than treating data duration as the sole scaling axis, Ego4WAM shows how alignment, task diversity, available supervision, and usage strategy jointly shape the value of egocentric human data for robot learning.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: VehicleArena: A Realistic Urban Environment for Multi-Agent Driving
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jie Yang, Jiajun Chen, Jiazheng Zhou, Mianqiu Huang, Yining Zheng
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: VehicleArena is a 3D urban-driving benchmark for evaluating independently operating agents navigating dynamic environments, highlighting emergent interactions and their impact on traffic flow and performance.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Real-world embodied agents often pursue independent objectives within a shared physical environment, where their actions can alter the conditions faced by others. Existing benchmarks, however, typically assume shared goals or explicitly prescribed interaction protocols, leaving such emergent physical coupling underexplored. We introduce VehicleArena, a 3D urban-driving benchmark for studying independently operating agents in a dynamic shared world. In VehicleArena, LLM-controlled agents must fulfill evolving passenger requests while navigating complex traffic, and each agent's driving decisions can reshape traffic flow, delays, risks, and subsequent observations for surrounding agents. The benchmark provides 112 evaluation tasks spanning single-agent and multi-agent driving. Across nine evaluated models, the highest arrival rates reach only 65.0% on single-agent tasks and 65.6% on multi-agent tasks, while strong passenger-request or cabin scores do not reliably translate into successful trip completion. Moreover, in matched multi-agent runs, every tested focal policy reduces the arrival rate of surrounding vehicles relative to the simulator's native traffic controller, revealing measurable externalities beyond the focal vehicle itself.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: JointEdit3D: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Editing in a Unified Latent Space
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Xinnan Zhu, Ruijie Xu, Jiayu Ying, Daoguo Dong, Jiachen Xu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: JointEdit3D enables efficient 3D scene editing by utilizing a unified latent space for asymmetric inpainting, enhancing quality and structural integrity while preserving unedited content.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Existing 3D scene editing methods typically rely on per-scene optimization over explicit 3D representations or cascaded edit-and-reconstruct pipelines, resulting in high test-time cost, limited 3D awareness, and structural inconsistencies. To couple appearance synthesis with geometry prediction, we adapt a pretrained unified RGB-geometry latent space to feed-forward scene editing. Given a source video and an edited reference image, JointEdit3D performs asymmetric latent inpainting: it observes only the edited RGB reference latent and jointly generates the remaining RGB latents and the entire geometry latent along the source trajectory. JointEdit3D introduces a dedicated SceneAnchor Branch to inject source-scene structure without forcing direct copying, and adopts edit/background-aware losses to balance edited-region fidelity with unedited-content preservation. To address the lack of paired resources for standardized 3D scene editing evaluation, we introduce SceneEdit3D-15K, a dataset with 15K paired editing samples and renderer-provided 3D annotations, together with SceneEdit3D-Bench, a curated 100-sample benchmark. Experiments show that JointEdit3D improves edited-region quality and 3D structural completeness over prior baselines while maintaining competitive background preservation.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Long Li, Qichao Zhao, Yue Yang, Fan Xu, Zhe Wang
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The Spotter framework enhances embodied models by allowing a vision-language model to monitor and correct errors, significantly improving performance and efficiency in robotic tasks.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Current embodied models do not respond to their own failures, although what just went wrong could inform a small adjustment on the next attempt, the kind of reflection behind the gains of thinking in language models. We test whether they can repair a known error, which requires producing a correction and judging whether it is right. Stopped at a failure and allowed to retry, they seldom repair it through their own randomness or from a language description of the error, and best-of-N selection cannot pick the successful candidate after a failure. We attribute this to training only on successful demonstrations and to inputs too narrow to show what went wrong, and conclude that reflection must come from a vision-language model (VLM), which takes in far more information, such as the episode history and text, and is more general. Prior VLM-led work has the VLM plan every step and invoke the embodied model as a tool, placing the VLM on the critical path. We propose Spotter, which reverses the roles: the embodied model leads and executes continuously, while the VLM runs in parallel, monitors through a lightweight local screener, intervenes only when an error is detected, reflects on and corrects it, and returns control. We run Spotter with Qwen and with GPT as the VLM, and both improve the embodied models; with GPT, Spotter improves Cosmos Policy and $π_{0.5}$ by 5.6 and 7.5 percentage points on RoboCasa, and raises $π_{0.5}$ from 47.2% to 57.0% on the Hard setting of RoboTwin 2.0 and from 53% to 83% on a real robot. Because the VLM steps in only when an error is confirmed, a successful episode with Qwen takes only 13 to 16 s longer than with the embodied model alone and about 70% less time than with a VLM-led baseline using the same model. Our code is available at https://github.com/zqc3117/Spotter.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Beyond Token Importance: Preserving Spatial Scaffolds for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jiayu Chen, Shuyong Gao, Jingkai Jia, Xiaosheng Bu, Jiyuan Fu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The paper introduces GeoScaffold, a visual token pruning method that enhances vision-language-action inference by preserving spatial structures, achieving significant efficiency and success rates.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Existing VLA pruning strategies primarily select individual visual tokens according to task-level semantic relevance, while overlooking the spatial information required for robotic manipulation. To examine this limitation, we construct a simple Stride baseline that uniformly samples tokens along the flattened one-dimensional visual sequence, representing a purely geometric pruning strategy. Surprisingly, Stride outperforms semantic pruning and random pruning at certain pruning ratios, but collapses when the token budget is only slightly reduced. We characterize this phenomenon through the spatial coverage radius, defined as the largest spatial blind spot induced by the retained token set after pruning. Our analysis reveals a strong correlation between the spatial structure of retained tokens and task success, suggesting that reliable VLA pruning requires preserving not only task-relevant tokens but also the spatial scaffold of the scene. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose GeoScaffold, a training-free visual token pruning method that partitions each image into spatial regions, allocates inter-region token budgets using task-relevance weights, and selects intra-region scaffold tokens via farthest point sampling to reduce the local coverage radius. On pi 0.5 and LIBERO, GeoScaffold retains only 20% of visual tokens while preserving a 93.2% average success rate, and achieves a 1.78 times prefill speedup over the unpruned baseline.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: EgoHumanoid-V2: Human-to-Humanoid Transfer of Coordinated Whole-Body Skills for Loco-Manipulation
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jin Chen, Yiming Jiang, Chongyang Xu, Modi Shi, Shijia Peng
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: EgoHumanoid-V2 enables effective human-to-humanoid transfer of coordinated loco-manipulation skills using a novel coarse-to-fine alignment approach, achieving zero-shot performance on real-world tasks.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Human demonstrations capture diverse scenes and rich whole-body skills without requiring robot teleoperation. Prior work on egocentric transfer has emphasized scene generalization in loco-manipulation under decoupled control, leaving direct transfer of coordinated whole-body skills less explored. We present EgoHumanoid-V2, the first egocentric human-to-humanoid skill transfer framework for coordinated whole-body loco-manipulation. At its core, coarse-to-fine action alignment combines kinematic reference correction with dynamics-aware refinement. It improves end-effector pose accuracy while preserving whole-body coordination. We also use robot-arm rendering and training-time image augmentation to reduce the visual embodiment gap and improve viewpoint robustness. On four real-world tasks, vision-language-action (VLA) policies trained on aligned human data show zero-shot skill transfer without target-task robot demonstrations. Task scores are comparable to those of policies trained on teleoperation data at a lower collection cost. These results support human data as direct skill supervision.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Yang Zhang, Jiangyuan Zhao, Chenyou Fan, Jiayu Hu, Xiu Yuan
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The V-JEPA Policy framework leverages predictive visual latents from a frozen encoder to effectively build world-action models, outperforming traditional methods in various benchmarks.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple future visual-state prediction with action generation. By adapting video generators or image-editing models pretrained at scale, a prominent line of recent WAMs inherits both predictive knowledge and the models in which it was learned. We ask whether a predictive visual latent space induced by large-scale predictive pretraining can instead provide a sufficient foundation for effective WAM learning without inheriting a complete pretrained visual generative model. To answer this question, we introduce V-JEPA Policy, a simple framework that builds a WAM on the latent space of a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. An instruction-conditioned future-latent predictor and a flow-matching action expert are jointly learned from scratch in a single downstream stage, with the predictor's future-informed context key--value states conditioning action generation. With 0.9B total parameters, of which 0.6B are trainable, V-JEPA Policy achieves competitive performance with representative WAM and vision-language-action baselines across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa-GR1. Comparing visual foundations under the same downstream framework and training budget identifies V-JEPA latents as more effective than the discriminative, reconstructive, and video-understanding-oriented alternatives, particularly under distribution shifts. Beyond task-specific learning, pretraining the predictor on DROID video--instruction pairs without action labels and adapting it into a WAM yields substantial gains in downstream control and out-of-distribution generalization. Together, these findings establish predictive visual latents as a foundation for effective WAM learning from task-specific demonstrations and for transferring future-modeling knowledge acquired from broader in-the-wild videos. Our code is available at https://github.com/breez3young/VJEPA-Policy.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Exemplar2VQA: A Scalable Exemplar-Driven Visual Question Answering Generation Framework via Multi-Agent Coding
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Jiayu Ying, Qijian Tian, Ruijie Xu, Xinnan Zhu, Daoguo Dong
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: Exemplar2VQA is a scalable framework that generates high-fidelity spatial question-answer pairs using multi-agent coding, enhancing performance in visual question answering across diverse benchmarks.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Advancing spatial intelligence in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is bottlenecked by the scarcity of complex, scalable 3D question-answer (QA) data. While manual annotation is labor-intensive, directly utilizing LLMs to synthesize these QA pairs often fails due to their inherent deficiencies in spatial and geometric computation. We introduce Exemplar2VQA, a scalable exemplar-driven visual question answering generation framework that rapidly synthesizes large-scale spatial QA pairs in simulated environments via multi-agent coding. By equipping collaborative agents with a meticulously designed library of geometric utilities, Exemplar2VQA bypasses LLMs' spatial reasoning flaws through deterministic code execution. Crucially, the framework exhibits remarkable versatility: taking diverse static object-centric spatial query templates as exemplars, it seamlessly and autonomously scales them into massive, high-fidelity synthetic datasets. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL (3B/7B) exclusively on Exemplar2VQA-generated synthetic indoor data yields significant performance improvements across various diverse benchmarks. Furthermore, its effectiveness is not limited to in-domain indoor datasets but also robustly extends to outdoor and mixed-scene benchmarks. These results establish Exemplar2VQA as a scalable and powerful paradigm for bridging the sim-to-real gap in Embodied AI. Our code is at https://github.com/yingjiayu12/Exemplar2VQA

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Explore, Execute, Evolve: A Skill Acquisition and Reuse Loop for Embodied Agents
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Sicheng Xie, Yitong Chen, Haidong Cao, Shunlin Lu, Zuxuan Wu
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: RoboSkill enhances robotic task execution efficiency by integrating skill acquisition and reuse in a feedback-driven loop, significantly improving success rates and reducing runtime.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action and world-action models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in robotics, yet generalization to unseen tasks remains challenging. More recently, general-purpose multimodal agents have shown great potential for zero-shot robotic task solving. However, they often incur high execution costs by reasoning and exploring the physical world from scratch. To reduce these costs, we introduce RoboSkill, a framework that connects skill acquisition and reuse through an Explore, Execute, Evolve loop. Within this loop, the agent explores to gather task-relevant information, executes tasks while adapting to feedback, and evolves its skill library based on execution records. It then reuses these skills to guide exploration and execution in the next cycle, closing the loop. To improve loop efficiency, we complement vision with tactile feedback to reduce uncertainty during physical interaction. We further augment textual guidance with reusable code to reduce reasoning overhead during skill reuse. On LIBERO-10, RoboSkill improves first-episode success rates by 12.5--25.0 percentage points and reduces average runtime by 7.6--72.4% across four agents. On real robots, it improves success rates by 8.3 percentage points and reduces average runtime for successful trials by at least 14.4%.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: AgentBug-Smith: Automatically Reproducing Real-World Harness Bugs in Agentic Systems
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Yiming Cheng, Alfin Wijaya Rahardja, Mengshi Zhang, Zihao Chen, Zhenpeng Chen
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: AgentBug-Smith automates the reproduction of real-world harness bugs in agentic systems, outperforming existing methods and establishing a scalable benchmark for evaluating and improving software agents.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Agent harness bugs exhibit unique characteristics and remain challenging for state-of-the-art software agents to repair. Progress in this area is further hindered by existing benchmarks, which contain only a small and fixed number of executable harness bugs while requiring hundreds of human hours to construct. This work presents AgentBug-Smith, an automated harness bug reproduction approach that continuously discovers and reproduces real-world harness bugs from open-source agentic systems. Across different backbone LLMs, AgentBug-Smith consistently outperforms existing bug reproduction techniques designed for general software, achieving 10.67% - 27.56% higher success rates of reproducing harness bugs. By applying AgentBug-Smith to open-source agentic systems in the wild, we construct Live-Harness-Bench, a live and extensible benchmark that currently contains 200 reproducible harness bugs. We further demonstrate the utility of Live-Harness-Bench through two downstream applications. First, we use Live-Harness-Bench as the evaluation benchmark to systematically evaluate state-of-the-art software agents, revealing their limited capabilities in repairing real-world harness bugs. Second, we use Live-Harness-Bench as a knowledge base of real-world harness bug fixes, from which reusable repair skills can be distilled to improve existing software agents, increasing their harness-bug repair rates by 6.32%. Together, AgentBug-Smith and Live-Harness-Bench establish a scalable foundation for continuously evaluating and improving software agents on harness bug repair, turning real-world agent failures into executable evaluation instances and reusable knowledge for harness improvement, thus contributing to the ultimate goal of recursively self-improving agents.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: Rethinking Representations for World-Action Modeling
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Haoyi Jiang, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Zhihao Sun, Zequn Chen
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: The paper introduces ReWAM, a representation-centric world-action model that enhances robot policy learning through feature calibration and action-grounded shaping, achieving high success rates without generative pre-training.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: World-action models jointly learn robot policies and predict future observations, making the representation space an interface between control and prediction. We study the design of this space through controlled comparisons, finding that neither reconstruction fidelity nor pre-trained perceptual features alone ensure effective policy learning. These findings motivate ReWAM, a representation-centric world-action model built on pre-trained DINO features. Feature Calibration and a Temporal Representation Bottleneck organize these features into compact world states suited to dynamics modeling. Action-Grounded Representation Shaping routes only action-loss gradients to the bottleneck, thereby letting the policy shape what the representation encodes while the world model learns how it evolves. Without generative video pre-training, ReWAM achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0. On RoboDojo, it achieves an average score of 12.29 and a success rate of 8.28% using approximately 600 hours of embodied pre-training data.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: CAR-VLA: Complexity-Aware and Risk-Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Xiaolei Chen, Zhuolin He, Yuxuan Liang, Xu Li, Haotian Chen
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: CAR-VLA is a novel driving VLA model that integrates scene complexity and dynamic risk to optimize reasoning depth and urgency for autonomous driving scenarios.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Existing adaptive reasoning methods for driving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models primarily focus on whether to reason, overlooking how reasoning should differ across driving situations. Our key insight is that while scene complexity informs reasoning depth, dynamic risk is equally critical for deciding how to reason in time-critical situations. We therefore propose CAR-VLA, a unified driving VLA model that jointly considers scene complexity and dynamic risk to guide reasoning depth, urgency, and focus. CAR-VLA maps four complexity--risk categories to three reasoning modes: \textit{Fast Intuition} for direct trajectory generation in simple low-risk scenes, \textit{Slow Thinking} for deliberate reasoning in complex low-risk scenes, and \textit{Reflex Response} for compact, hazard-focused reasoning in high-risk scenes regardless of complexity. Rather than merely shortening deliberation, Reflex Response centers reasoning on the most critical hazard and the immediate safe response. We train CAR-VLA through progressive supervised learning that links scene assessment, reasoning-mode selection, and trajectory generation, followed by reasoning-augmented reinforcement learning to improve driving quality and reasoning behavior. Experiments on NAVSIM v1(91.1 PDMS), NAVSIM v2(90.3 EPDMS), and Navhard(35.0 EPDMS) demonstrate competitive driving performance. Qualitative comparisons on navtest and in-house high-risk scenarios further illustrate risk-aware reasoning and hazard-responsive trajectory generation. The code for this paper will be released publicly at: https://github.com/chenxl124578/CAR-VLA.git

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: GeoVerse: World-Consistent Novel View Synthesis in Geometric Latent Space
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Kerui Ren, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Changjian Jiang, Mu Huang
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: GeoVerse synthesizes world-consistent novel views by integrating geometric latent space with video generative appearance priors, enhancing visual quality and geometric consistency.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis from sparse images must reconcile faithful reconstruction of observed regions with plausible completion of unseen content, while maintaining world consistency across viewpoints. Existing geometry-based methods preserve observed scene structure but often struggle to complete unseen regions, whereas video generative models offer rich appearance priors but accumulate inconsistencies during sequential view generation. We propose GeoVerse, a framework that synthesizes world-consistent novel views by performing generation within the geometric latent space of a pretrained 3D foundation model and injecting appearance priors from a video generative model. Specifically, GeoVerse extracts multilevel features from Wan2.2 VACE and injects them into the geometric latent diffusion model via a ControlNet-style adapter, incorporating video-learned appearance priors to enhance structural completion. To enforce cross-view coherence, a global spatial memory continuously aggregates observed and synthesized content, reprojecting target-aligned guidance to anchor subsequent predictions to a shared scene representation. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate improved visual quality and geometric consistency, with a 2.23 dB higher PSNR on DL3DV and 32.4% lower ATE on Mip-NeRF360 compared to GLD.

智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).authors_text: Hongcheng Gao, Hailong Qu, Yu Lei, Henghui Sun, Haoyang Li
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).summary: EngiWorld introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating autonomous agents in engineering, highlighting significant performance gaps in current models across diverse design tasks and software platforms.
智能人机交互实验室 (MemX).debug_abstract: Autonomous agents have made rapid progress in general-purpose computer use, but reliable automation of professional industrial engineering remains out of reach, as engineering workflows demand reasoning over geometric and physical constraints and dependencies preserved across software and design stages. We present EngiWorld, the first benchmark structured around the complete design loop: 1,301 expert-curated tasks spanning 6 engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, and 3D visualization) and 26 professional software platforms, with both GUI and CLI interfaces and 6 task types ranging from software-selection to open-ended tasks. We further introduce an artifact-centric evaluation methodology built on a unified domain-verifier suite, which programmatically checks the geometric validity, physical feasibility, and rule compliance of final and intermediate artifacts, and scores quantitative design tasks continuously by specification attainment rather than binary success. Evaluation of seven frontier models reveals a substantial capability gap: the strongest model achieves an EngiScore of only 44.3, and just 3.6% of multi-software attempts succeed. EngiWorld provides the first rigorous foundation for measuring progress toward agents that operate professional engineering software end to end.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Initialization-Free LEO Doppler Positioning via Semidefinite Relaxation: A Cold-Start Approach
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Baoshan Song, Weisong Wen, Qi Zhang, Bing Xu, Penggao Yan
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning method using semidefinite relaxation, achieving accurate positioning without prior location knowledge in cold-start scenarios.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite Doppler measurements offer an alternative source of positioning information for Internet of Things devices when Global Navigation Satellite System signals are unavailable. Conventional local optimisation methods depend on an accurate initial position and can fail during a complete cold start. We propose an initialization-free LEO Doppler positioning framework based on semidefinite relaxation. The method reformulates the nonlinear positioning problem into a semidefinite programme to obtain a receiver position estimate without prior location knowledge. We analyse relaxation tightness under noiseless conditions and derive sufficient noise bounds under parameter disturbances. Simulations and field experiments using opportunistic Iridium-NEXT signals evaluate initialization sensitivity, positioning accuracy and computational cost. In the field experiment, the proposed method achieves a three-dimensional positioning error of 140 m without an initial position, whereas local solvers converge to poor solutions under large initial offsets. Using the semidefinite estimate to initialise Gauss-Newton or Dog-Leg reduces the positioning error to 130 m. The framework provides a cold-start initialization stage for subsequent local refinement in opportunistic LEO positioning. The implementation and datasets are publicly available to support reproducibility and further research.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: PATH: Preference-Aware Traversability Estimation for Robotic Teleoperation in Off-Road Navigation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xianghao Meng, Wenshuo Wang, Cheng Shao, Lewei Feng, Qingxiao Liu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: PATH-Net enhances robotic teleoperation by integrating operator preferences into traversability estimation, optimizing cost maps and speed profiles for off-road navigation.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Traversability estimation is critical for ground vehicle teleoperation, yet existing methods often neglect the human operator's preferences for speed and risk tolerance. To address this gap, we propose PATH-Net, a Preference-Aware Traversability estimation Hierarchical Network that adaptively generates preference-conditioned traversability cost maps and speed profiles for off-road teleoperation. Our framework integrates visual and geometric bird's-eye-view features with short-term historical vehicle states through a multi-head shared-backbone architecture. Our PATH-Net infers traversability cost maps while optimizing speed recommendations by using maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning and sparse speed supervision. Our method incorporates operator preference via an asymmetric feature aggregation mechanism, splitting inference into a cost branch that prioritizes high-risk traversability regions and a speed branch that outputs preference-adjusted recommended speeds. Experiments with 15 operators across 225 teleoperated trajectories show alignment with user-specific navigation strategies, achieving modified Hausdorff distance of 0.17 m (aggressive) and 0.15 m (conservative). In the questionnaire assessment, participants reported lower NASA-TLX workload scores with PATH-Net recommendations than without recommendations, decreasing from 34.7 to 22.2. These results support preference-conditioned trajectory and speed recommendation for off-road teleoperation.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Leming Shen, Qiang Yang, Xinyu Huang, Zijing Ma, Yuanqing Zheng
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: AgentDP automates model optimization and adaptation for heterogeneous embedded AI applications using LLMs, significantly reducing adaptation time by 80% and improving task accuracy by over 13%.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zhefan Rao, Meng Chu, Xuan Zhang, Jingfan Chen, Guohao Cai
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents Dual Exam, a framework for evaluating the interaction between Multimodal Agents and World Models across various domains, revealing performance inconsistencies and challenges in reciprocal learning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: PhyMo: Learning Physical Dynamics with Accurate and Continuous Motion from Multi-View Videos
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shangjia Liu, Jinxi Li, Siyuan Zhou, Bo Yang, Bing Wang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: PhyMo is a framework that accurately learns physical dynamics and continuous motion from multi-view videos by employing a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation and a Continuous Motion Evolution module.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Recovering dynamic 3D scene geometry, appearance, and the physical motion states that govern scene evolution from multi-view videos is important yet challenging. A key difficulty is that appearance can be deceptive. Under rendering supervision alone, a model may fit the observed images by changing color or opacity to compensate for inaccurate deformation, rather than recovering the true evolving geometry and motion. This issue is especially severe in scenes with fast or locally complex motion, where inaccurate trajectories can still produce plausible images over the observed frames, but lead to unreliable reconstruction and discontinuous future prediction. In this paper, we propose PhyMo, a framework for learning evolving dynamics from multi-view videos. We introduce a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation that drives the model to recover accurate motion from deformation, rather than relying on appearance shortcuts to explain observed motion. On top of this, we propose a Continuous Motion Evolution module with bidirectional kinematic continuity constraint to promote temporally consistent evolution of displacement, velocity, and acceleration. Together, these designs yield geometrically faithful interpolation and continuous motion extrapolation. Experiments on four dynamic scene benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Preserving Operator Intent Under Actuation Constraints: Teleoperation of Manipulators with Coupled Transmissions
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xuhan Miao, Zijin Han, Yutong Shen, Haidong Huang, Shanliushui Gao
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents a novel teleoperation method for manipulators that addresses actuation constraints and preserves operator intent through coordinated motor saturation and advanced feedback mechanisms.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Teleoperation enables intuitive control of remote engineering robots for precision tasks. Existing direct joint-mapping methods have two limitations: independent motor saturation disrupts pitch-roll coordination in differential wrists, while fixed mappings struggle with abrupt tracking changes caused by gravitational loads and actuation constraints. We propose an actuator-constraint-aware leader-follower teleoperation method that jointly models leader gravity compensation, leader-follower joint mapping, and follower differential-wrist control. Specifically, we perform coordinated saturation in motor space according to the available gravity margin and integrate continuous angle unwrapping, feedback-state monitoring, and feasible-reference updates. This preserves the operator's motion direction, reduces coordination distortion, and suppresses recovery transients during saturation or brief communication failures. Real-robot experiments demonstrate smoother wrist trajectories and more continuous recovery than direct mapping.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Likui Zhang, Zhe Zhu, Zhihao Zhan, Yibo Bai, Hanlin Wang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: AtomicRL enhances long-horizon robotic manipulation by optimizing credit assignment and exploration through atomic task structures, achieving significant performance gains in both simulation and real-world applications.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Joint-Angle Invariance of Jacobian-Based Performance Indices for Serial Robotic Manipulators
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yaohua Zhou, Mingdao Lin, Jiayu Song, Xixin Zhao, Haidong Huang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper explores joint-angle invariance of Jacobian-based performance indices in serial robotic manipulators, enhancing efficiency in performance evaluation and optimization while reducing computational demands.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: This article investigates the joint-angle invariance (JAI) of Jacobian-based performance indices for serial robotic manipulators. We identify kinematic conditions under which representative performance indices, including manipulability, stiffness, and other Jacobian-derived indices, remain independent of the first and last joint angles. This property allows a systematic reduction in the effective configuration-space dimensionality, thereby simplifying the performance evaluation. The utility of JAI is demonstrated through two application scenarios: workspace performance map construction and task layout optimization. Comparative results show that the proposed JAI-based strategy reduces computational effort and storage requirements without compromising the effectiveness.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Ziyong Wang, Yupei Lin, Runxuan Huang, Liang Lin, Dongyu Zhang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: GPT-6-Astra effectively utilizes tactile feedback and multimodal context to enhance robotic manipulation success, outperforming traditional models without extensive pretraining or task-specific fine-tuning.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yilei Man, Yang Chen, Jingcai Guo
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, enhancing Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures by integrating temporal context for improved action planning in latent world models.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Learning latent dynamics is fundamental to building action-conditioned world models for planning. Among existing families, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) offer a natural framework by modeling transitions directly in latent space rather than at the pixel level. However, two issues remain in JEPA-based world models: (i) physical grounding lacks explicit aggregation of temporal context and (ii) action planning always overly relies on generic sampling distributions. To this end, we propose $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning. Specifically, during learning, we incorporate a shared causal temporal module that aggregates temporal context within observation and prediction sequences under physical state supervision, grounding both in task-relevant physical states. When planning, we further introduce action inference through stepwise conditioning of a generative action distribution on the current and goal latent representations together with their evolving discrepancy, yielding anchored proposals that guide model-based online refinement. Together, physical state supervision guides temporal representation learning, while the action prior guides search through the learned world model. Experiments demonstrate improved planning performance on manipulation tasks, including tasks with increasing temporal separation between initial and goal observations. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/myl11045/G-JEPA.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Difference-in-Differences on a Censored Rating Scale Can Manufacture an Effect: Evidence from a Pre-Registered LLM-Judge Audit
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Shuyi Fan, Boyuan Deng, Mengyu Xu, Xinhong Xie, Chenyang Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The study reveals that bounded rating scales in LLM-judge audits can create misleading effects, as evidenced by a significant interaction that doesn't reflect true preferences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: LLM-judge audits assess bias by comparing ratings across matched conditions. Difference-in-differences designs compare two candidate responses within each item and then compare that contrast across a manipulated attribute, with an endpoint read off a bounded rating scale. Building on prior work on nonlinear difference-in-differences, we show in closed form that when ratings are bounded, a severity shift common to both responses produces an observed interaction whenever the scale bounds attenuate it unequally. We examine this problem in a pre-registered audit comprising 990 calls to a frozen pedagogy judge. The registered primary analysis did not detect an effect of a stated novice or advanced profile on scaffolding preference. The only nominally significant secondary interaction concerned the productive-struggle sub-score ($+0.378$ points; $p = 0.002$). A post-hoc construction with zero differential preference reproduced 79 to 85% of this interaction using the observed severity shift and the scale floor alone. The observed interaction therefore does not identify differential preference on the latent scale.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Cross-Visibility-Gap Identity Persistence for 4D Scene Graphs
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jiahui Hu, Li Gao, Yu Liu, Pengzhan Zhou
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents CVG-SGM, a method for maintaining object identity in 4D scene graphs through historical relational memory, achieving high accuracy in identity recovery despite visibility gaps.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: 4D scene graphs require persistent object identity when an object disappears inside an opaque carrier and later reappears as a fresh detection. When appearance and target-centric motion are unavailable, identity recovery must rely on relational history. We formulate cross-visibility-gap identity persistence as historical-node recovery through a remembered target--carrier binding. We introduce CVG-SGM, a perception-frontend-compatible transfer--maintain--read memory. Geometry-weighted cross-node interaction transfers target-specific evidence into carrier states, a shared per-node GRU maintains this information during transport, and a two-time readout combines stored carrier--identity compatibility with current detection--carrier geometry to recover the historical identity. In the controlled one-identity-per-carrier setting, CVG-SGM achieves 1.000 re-link accuracy, compared with 0.570 for both no-memory and parameter-count-matched no-write controls. It also generalizes to scene-disjoint, unseen longer visibility gaps. On real RGB-D/SAM2 feature-level episodes, it correctly re-links 36/36 held-out detections, compared with 28/36 for the strongest fixed carrier--identity control. Counterfactual carrier-memory swaps redirect predictions according to the swapped bindings, supporting the role of stored relational information in identity recovery. The current approach remains limited by shared-carrier identity ambiguity and does not provide end-to-end raw-video re-identification.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Provisioning Robust and Efficient LiDAR Perception for Autonomous Driving
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Tingxu Han, Zijie Shen, An Guo, Lyuke Wang, Chunrong Fang
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper presents a method for enhancing LiDAR perception in autonomous driving by improving robustness to point-cloud corruption while reducing latency and memory usage.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: LiDAR-based 3D object detection is a core perception service for autonomous driving, but deployment requires robustness to point-cloud corruption while meeting latency and memory requirements. Existing approaches address robustness and resource efficiency separately, resulting in compact detectors that are fragile under corruption or robust detectors that remain costly to deploy. We therefore formulate LiDAR perception provisioning as constructing a detector that remains accurate under point-cloud corruptions while meeting constraints on inference latency and peak GPU memory. To achieve robustness, we first craft corrupted samples that mimic extreme weather conditions. Then we train candidate detectors offline by ordering clean and corrupted samples by perturbation sensitivity, through which detectors learn more from hard corrupted samples. We estimate perturbation sensitivity using an ensemble of seven heterogeneous 3D detectors by tracking changes in confidence, BEV overlap, and unmatched detections. To improve efficiency, we narrow the network and use offline neighborhood-density measurements to determine how many points and neighbors each sampling stage processes. We evaluate our method using AP (Average Precision) under clean and corrupted conditions, inference latency, and peak allocated GPU memory. On KITTI for Car detection with PointRCNN, our method improves Moderate AP under corruption by 3.32 points over the original detector while reducing mean latency by 19.8% and peak allocated GPU memory by 53.9%. Across two datasets, two detector architectures, and three object classes, our method improves AP under corruption by 4.03 points on average over the corresponding original detectors, while reducing mean inference latency and peak allocated GPU memory by 14.4% and 38.0%, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/drunklibai/robust-efficient-lidar-perception.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: GeoBridge: Evolving Transferable Decoder Topologies for Geometric Vision
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Rui Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Ran Cheng
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: GeoBridge introduces an evolutionary framework for optimizing transferable decoder topologies in geometric vision, enhancing depth estimation and Gaussian reconstruction through adaptable multi-scale feature processing.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Depth estimation and Gaussian reconstruction share a need for multi-scale feature processing, yet use different prediction interfaces and training objectives. Whether a decoder's internal computation can be optimized once and reused across these systems remains a structural design question. Search over primitive configurations alone leaves the organization of transformations fixed. To address this gap, we propose GeoBridge, an evolutionary framework for transferable decoder topologies. First, GeoBridge makes stage-internal topology searchable through residual, sequential, and parallel composition of configurable primitives. Shape-preserving composition retains the stage interfaces of a fixed multi-scale scaffold. Second, a functional-tree encoding supports stage-aware crossover and hierarchical mutation, while a gradient sensitivity-alignment proxy evaluates candidates without training. Multi-objective evolution balances this proxy with computation and parameter cost. Third, selected topologies are instantiated and trained in target systems with task-specific prediction interfaces. A single source search takes approximately 12 GPU hours. GeoBridgeNet-A3 achieves the best depth accuracy among four adapted decoder baselines under a common encoder and training protocol on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI. The same topology reaches 27.11 dB PSNR in Gaussian novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K, and its refined representations support open-vocabulary segmentation on LERF. These results support decoder topology as a reusable design object across the evaluated geometric vision systems. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/EMI-Group/GeoBridge-NAS.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: When Better Policies Leave Harder Failures: Coverage Shift in VLM Success Monitoring
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Isabel Guan, Dingyuan Zhang, Shipeng Lyu, I-Ming Chen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The study reveals that improved robot policies can obscure monitoring of residual failures, termed coverage shift, highlighting a disconnect between task success and failure detectability.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Can a better robot policy become harder to monitor? We study a fixed vision-language model (VLM) that judges success while a policy improves. In a controlled 20-seed tray-placement experiment, training selects only simulator-verified successes. Success rises from 66.8% to 97.0%, and accepted hover failures fall from 5.0% to 0.9% of executions. Yet the judge accepts 50.0% of remaining hovers, versus 31.1% under untrained sampling. These residual failures more often lie below the tray rim, which can conceal the gap beneath a grasped cube. A separate boundary probe accepts 148/160 below-rim hovers and 0/160 above-rim hovers. We call this change in conditional monitoring sensitivity coverage shift: learning changes which failures reach a fixed judge. A broader diagnosis covers nine judges and 1,392 stimuli. Judge-filtered experiments across eight settings further show heterogeneous effects of state-dependent acceptance. The results distinguish task improvement from failure detectability and motivate reporting absolute misses, conditional misses, and audit coverage together.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: MUSE: Benchmarking Assembly Structure and Interface Geometry in Multi-Component Text-to-CAD Generation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Xiaoyu Dong, Zeng Chenbo, Zhi Li, Xiao-Ming Wu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: MUSE introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-component Text-to-CAD generation, emphasizing assembly structure and interface geometry beyond mere geometric similarity.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently advanced text-driven 3D generation, yet generating CAD models that satisfy practical design requirements remains challenging. Existing benchmarks focus primarily on single-part CAD models and geometric similarity, providing limited assessment of assembly structure and interface geometry. To address this gap, we introduce MUSE, a Text-to-CAD benchmark for generating multi-component, editable boundary representation (B-Rep) assemblies. MUSE pairs practical design instances with structured \textit{Design Specifications} and evaluates generated outputs across four dimensions: code executability, geometric validity, structural and interface fidelity, and functional consistency. We further introduce Structure and Interface Evaluation (SIE), which combines reference Physical Assembly Graphs with direct B-Rep analysis to assess component correspondence, connectivity, interface types, and interface clearances. Experiments on proprietary and open-weight LLMs show that high execution success does not necessarily translate into correct assembly structure or interface geometry. Together, MUSE provides a benchmark and evaluation framework for studying multi-component Text-to-CAD generation beyond shape similarity. Our project website, including the leaderboard, dataset, and code, is available at \url{https://dong7313.github.io/muse-benchmark/}.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: MemForest is a memory compression framework that efficiently partitions and merges agent memory, achieving significant storage reduction and retrieval speedup while maintaining high performance.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yun Wang, Chiyu Wang, Fan Jiang, Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: TriFold introduces a 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes complex scenes into structured latents, enhancing reconstruction and generation through adaptive spatial representation and occupancy prediction.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Recent progress in 3D generation has motivated growing interest in compact generative representations of complex 3D scenes. For native 3D Gaussian scenes, however, learning such representations remains challenging due to widely varying primitive counts, nonuniform spatial density, and differences in geometry and appearance even among spatially neighboring primitives. In this work, we introduce TriFold, a native 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes Gaussian scenes into a fixed-layout triplane latent and jointly reconstructs their geometry and appearance. The key insight is to impose structural regularity on the latent space while preserving the spatial adaptivity of the underlying Gaussians. During encoding, we use cell-wise learned queries to aggregate projected Gaussians into multiple slots per cell, reducing the information loss caused by single-feature pooling. During decoding, occupancy prediction identifies active regions, where query-based set prediction and candidate selection reconstruct local Gaussian sets with spatially varying primitive counts. Building on this representation, we train a latent flow-matching model for conditional scene-level 3DGS generation, enabling point-cloud-conditioned synthesis and single-image-conditioned amodal generation. Experiments demonstrate that TriFold achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and generation from a single image that provides only a partial observation of the scene, validating its effectiveness for native 3D Gaussian representation learning. https://fantasy-amap.github.io/TriFold

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: NestedVLA: Learning to Consolidate and Generate Skills for Vision-Language-Action Models
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Guodong Du, Wanyu Lin
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: NestedVLA introduces a novel approach for consolidating skills in Vision-Language-Action models by using a nested hypernetwork for task-adaptive parameter generation, outperforming traditional methods.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models promise generalist robotic agents, yet consolidating skills learned across heterogeneous tasks and environments remains difficult: training data is fragmented across platforms, joint multi-task training suffers from interference, and model merging tends to introduce parameter conflicts or require architectural changes. We instead advocate a paradigm in which skills are first learned independently and then consolidated post hoc. To this end, we propose NestedVLA, which replaces parameter aggregation with parameter generation: a nested hypernetwork, conditioned on the target task, synthesizes task-adaptive action-expert parameters that compose with a frozen base VLA. Task-specific compressed VLM residuals are retained separately. This formulation enables flexible task-conditioned skill reuse while mitigating interference. Across three RL benchmarks (MetaWorld, ManiSkill, CALVIN), NestedVLA outperforms the strongest model-merging baseline by 41 pp on average, matches per-task fine-tuning within 1 pp on ManiSkill, and substantially closes the gap on CALVIN, pointing toward a storage-efficient route to skill consolidation. Code is available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026-NestedVLA.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: GRASP: Global-Local Representation Alignment and Spatial-Physical Grounding for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Zeyuan Ren, Guanxun Zhao, Qi Li, Hao Wang, Wenlong Liao
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper presents a training framework for bimanual robotic manipulation that aligns global-local representations and incorporates spatial-physical grounding to enhance task success and adaptability.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that directly regress joint-space actions avoid the deployment-time cost of inverse kinematics. However, their training objectives remain misaligned with task success, as joint-space losses ignore the unequal physical consequences of joint errors and visual conditioning lacks explicit focus on hand-object interaction regions. To address these issues, we propose a training-phase prior injection framework for fine-grained bimanual manipulation. First, a physics-grounded flow-matching loss maps the implicit clean-action estimate at every noise level through differentiable forward kinematics (FK) and supervises the resulting Tool Center Point (TCP) pose and inter-arm relative pose, with a bounded noise-level weighting that compensates gradient decay. Second, we introduce a global prediction query group distilled from a frozen DINOv3 teacher through future-frame feature prediction, together with a local interaction query supervised by Grounding DINO at the attention level. Both teachers are removed at inference, and the deployment pipeline is that of a standard joint-space flow policy, adding only the learned query pathway. Simulation and real-robot experiments on long-horizon bimanual tasks show that the two priors are complementary across different deployment settings. The full model excels in in-distribution deployment, while the distilled query branch is preferable under strong visual randomization.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Yujie Feng, Xiaobin Wang, Jinluan Yang, Xiaonan Shi, Pengjun Xie
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: This paper critiques skill-policy co-evolution in self-improving agents, revealing fragility due to skill drift, and introduces the CO-evolution Drift Audit (CODA) for better evaluation.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Skill-policy co-evolution, in which an agent's policy model and its skill bank improve each other during training, is a promising paradigm for self-improving agents. Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. In this paper, we first establish, through theoretical and empirical analysis, that the fragility hidden by this blind spot is not incidental. The acceptance rule these methods share (cooperative acceptance) ties a policy's competence to the bank it co-evolved with, leaving it fragile once skills drift, regardless of the implementation; empirically, sensitivity to skill drift grows as co-evolution training proceeds. We therefore introduce the CO-evolution Drift Audit (CODA), a deployment-oriented evaluation protocol that simulates skill drift and, alongside success rate under worst-case drift, introduces two new metrics: a consistency rate under meaning-preserving edits and a resistance rate to corrupted skills. Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success is 5-13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52-93% of the delivered bank's gain over the no-skill baseline. CODA thus reframes the target of co-evolution, from peak performance on the co-evolved bank to the ability to harness skills however they evolve, and provides a shared standard against which future methods can be audited.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: All-in-One Memory: Process-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Memory Agents
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Bingbing Wang, Jingjie Lin, Weiming Qiao, Jing Li, Ruifeng Xu
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem) framework integrates retrieval and memory construction in reinforcement learning, enhancing answer accuracy in long-context tasks through a unified reward system.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Large language models increasingly rely on external memory to answer queries grounded in long-horizon histories such as multi-session dialogues and lengthy documents. However, existing memory methods often optimize retrieval and memory construction separately, without a shared reward space for evaluating search, writing, and stopping decisions.
