Existing affordance datasets and benchmarks remain misaligned with this setting, as they typically focus on grasping or object-level affordances, rely on synthetic scenes, or assume a single instruction-region correspondence. We present Affordance2Action (A2A), a benchmark-centered learning framework for scene-level, task-conditioned part affordance grounding. At its core is A2A-Bench, a manipulation-oriented benchmark that covers both single-region and multi-region instruction correspondences in everyday scenes, with the latter highlighting the ambiguity and diversity of affordance grounding in realistic multi-object environments. To construct it at scale, we build A2A-AffordGen, an agent-assisted annotation pipeline that combines language-model filtering, interactive part segmentation, instance-level mask-out refinement, task-reasoning instruction generation, and human verification. A2A-Bench's supervision further supports diverse downstream applications, with real-time affordance grounding and affordance-conditioned manipulation policies as two representative examples. Experiments show that A2A exposes substantial gaps in generic segmentation, VLM-based grounding, and affordance distillation baselines, while improving task-level localization and providing useful spatial priors for downstream manipulation.

上海人工智能实验室.title: MixVLA: Adaptive Mixing of Non-Invariant Information for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Models
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Pingrui Zhang, Yu Zhang, Pengyuan Wu, Bin Wang, Haoming Song
上海人工智能实验室.summary: MixVLA enhances zero-shot generalization in Vision-Language-Action models by adaptively mixing non-invariant information, improving robustness without additional data or architectural changes.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved remarkable advances in robotic manipulation, yet their zero-shot generalization under out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions remains limited. These models often entangle task-relevant invariant structure with environment-specific non-invariant factors, causing policies to rely on spurious appearance cues during action prediction. In this work, we propose \textbf{MixVLA}, a model-agnostic training framework that improves the generalization of VLA models without requiring additional OOD data or architectural modifications. The key component of MixVLA is \textbf{Adaptive Mixing of Non-Invariant Information (AMI)}. AMI stochastically mixes non-invariant representations to regularize distribution-specific variability while preserving complementary predictive cues. The mixed non-invariant features are then fused with invariant representations for final action prediction, resulting in improved robustness without sacrificing policy expressiveness. Extensive experiments across challenging manipulation settings, including LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, the RoboTwin perturbation suite, and real-world tasks, demonstrate that MixVLA improves overall zero-shot robustness while retaining strong in-domain performance.

上海人工智能实验室.title: BORA: Bridging Offline Reinforcement Learning and Online Residual Adaptation for Real-World Dexterous VLA Models
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Zhongxi Chen, Yifan Han, Bin Qiu, Zhangliang Gao, Yanming Shao
上海人工智能实验室.summary: BORA integrates offline reinforcement learning with online residual adaptation, enhancing dexterous manipulation in real robots through efficient human-guided corrections and lightweight model updates.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide strong behavioral priors for dexterous manipulation, yet adapting them on real robots remains challenging because high-DoF contact failures are difficult for humans to correct and online interaction is expensive. We present BORA, an offline-to-online reinforcement learning system that integrates an action-conditioned critic into a consistency-policy VLA and reuses the learned critic for frozen-base residual adaptation. To obtain executable corrective data, BORA combines wearable arm--hand teleoperation with a demonstration-guided local policy that translates coarse human intent into coordinated, embodiment-specific finger motions for contact-rich skills. Online robot rollouts and human corrections are mixed with offline data to update only a lightweight residual actor, avoiding full-model fine-tuning. We evaluate BORA on six real-world tasks using single-arm and bimanual platforms equipped with two dexterous-hand models. With only 20 online trajectories per task, BORA improves average success from 60.8% to 82.5% on standard objects and from 52% to 70% on held-out objects, while policy assistance substantially improves intervention reliability in bimanual twisting. These results demonstrate a practical route from executable human correction to efficient real-robot VLA adaptation.

上海人工智能实验室.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Junshu Pan, Zhizhang Fu, Shulin Huang, Yiran Ding, Zifan Cheng
上海人工智能实验室.summary: The paper introduces Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), enhancing reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by improving token-level credit assignment to boost reasoning accuracy.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet their predictions remain sensitive to task-irrelevant prompt features. We investigate this sensitivity through semifactual prompt interventions that preserve the underlying problem and its answer. Our analysis reveals substantial variation in token-level sensitivity and shows that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding improves reasoning accuracy without updating model weights. These findings highlight a limitation of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which assigns the same outcome-derived advantage to every response token and may reinforce potential spurious dependence alongside useful reasoning. Motivated by this observation, we introduce Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), a causally inspired variant of GRPO that incorporates semifactual stability into token-level credit assignment. SCAPO measures token probability drift for fixed responses under semifactual interventions and uses normalized stability scores to reduce advantages for relatively unstable tokens during early training, while granting no additional credit for stability alone. On Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, SCAPO improves AIME 2024-2026 accuracy over GRPO by 5.63 and 4.17 percentage points, respectively. At both model scales, SCAPO achieves the best results on most evaluated mathematics benchmarks and all evaluated out-of-distribution benchmarks among the compared methods. These results suggest that semifactual stability provides an effective training signal for improving reasoning and generalization through finer-grained credit assignment in RLVR. The code is available at https://github.com/DtYXs/SCAPO.

上海人工智能实验室.title: JointEdit3D: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Editing in a Unified Latent Space
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Xinnan Zhu, Ruijie Xu, Jiayu Ying, Daoguo Dong, Jiachen Xu
上海人工智能实验室.summary: JointEdit3D enables efficient 3D scene editing by utilizing a unified latent space for asymmetric inpainting, enhancing quality and structural integrity while preserving unedited content.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Existing 3D scene editing methods typically rely on per-scene optimization over explicit 3D representations or cascaded edit-and-reconstruct pipelines, resulting in high test-time cost, limited 3D awareness, and structural inconsistencies. To couple appearance synthesis with geometry prediction, we adapt a pretrained unified RGB-geometry latent space to feed-forward scene editing. Given a source video and an edited reference image, JointEdit3D performs asymmetric latent inpainting: it observes only the edited RGB reference latent and jointly generates the remaining RGB latents and the entire geometry latent along the source trajectory. JointEdit3D introduces a dedicated SceneAnchor Branch to inject source-scene structure without forcing direct copying, and adopts edit/background-aware losses to balance edited-region fidelity with unedited-content preservation. To address the lack of paired resources for standardized 3D scene editing evaluation, we introduce SceneEdit3D-15K, a dataset with 15K paired editing samples and renderer-provided 3D annotations, together with SceneEdit3D-Bench, a curated 100-sample benchmark. Experiments show that JointEdit3D improves edited-region quality and 3D structural completeness over prior baselines while maintaining competitive background preservation.

上海人工智能实验室.title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Ganlin Yang, Zhangzheng Tu, Yuqiang Yang, Sitong Mao, Junyi Dong
上海人工智能实验室.summary: EventVLA introduces a sparse visual evidence memory framework that enhances long-horizon VLA policies by dynamically capturing task-critical visual events, improving success rates by 40%.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Memory remains a critical bottleneck for long-horizon robotic manipulation, as standard Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often fail when task-relevant cues become occluded or unobservable over time. While existing memory-augmented methods utilize historical context, they either suffer from severe information bottlenecks, incur high latency via decoupled dual systems, or rely on unselective buffers that accumulate massive visual redundancies. To address these limitations, we introduce EventVLA, an end-to-end framework founded on the concept of sparse visual evidence memory that comprises two core components: foundational visual anchors to retain initial and short-term contexts, and a dynamic Keyframe Evidence Memory (KEM) module. Specifically, KEM directly predicts future keyframe probabilities from the VLA's latent embeddings to autonomously capture and store sparse, task-critical visual events. This foresight-driven mechanism empowers the policy to dynamically evaluate the future causal utility of current observations, preserving transient visual evidence before it becomes unobservable. Furthermore, we propose RoboTwin-MeM, a diagnostic benchmark specifically designed to evaluate non-Markovian manipulation tasks with interactive visual evidence. Extensive evaluations show that across 17 memory-requiring simulation tasks and 4 real-world bimanual tasks, EventVLA achieves an average success rate improvement of +40% over state-of-the-art memory-augmented VLAs.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: Plausible Future, Wrong Choice: Steering World-Action Models toward Intended Future
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Zhuohao Li, Jiawei He, Yuxuan Yan, Lang Zhou, Yinghao Li
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: The paper introduces TaskWAM, a framework that mitigates Stage Confusion in World-Action Models by using Mode and State Tokens to ensure task-aligned future predictions.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied generalist policies by jointly modeling future world evolution and robot actions across diverse manipulation tasks. However, representing diverse futures is only the first step: a capable WAM must also generate futures that match the requirements of the current task and execution progress. In long-horizon manipulation where similar observation-action segments occur across different tasks and stages, existing approaches may generate locally plausible yet misdirected rollouts to drift toward wrong task stage, i.e., a phenomenon we term Stage Confusion. To address this problem, we propose TaskWAM, a closed-loop, stage-aware framework that represents fine-grained task requirements with Mode Tokens and tracks execution progress with State Tokens, forming a structured task state to steer world--action generation toward intended future. We further introduce StageBench, a controlled multi-stage manipulation benchmark with parameterized stage variations and automated evaluation.Extensive experiments on both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks demonstrate that TaskWAM effectively reduces confusion and achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, TaskWAM provides strong plug-and-play transfer across heterogeneous WAM architectures and robot embodiments, including single-arm robots, dual-arm grippers, dexterous hands, and humanoid robots.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Wen Xue, Yong Liu, Xueheng Li, Si Wu, Yong Xu
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: LayerEditor introduces a unified framework for high-quality image editing that generates reusable RGBA layers through instruction-guided editing and Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Zhizhou Wang, Yaxi Lu, Zhong Zhang, Zikun Hu, Xin Cong
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: VeriCUA introduces a proactive reward agent that optimizes verification strategies for GUI agents, significantly improving task success and efficiency over existing methods.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning for computer-use agents increasingly relies on proactive reward agents that interact with the post-execution GUI environment to verify what recorded screenshots cannot reveal. The reliability of such verification hinges on two coupled decisions: what to check and when to stop. Existing methods leave these decisions to prompted foundation models. However, neither scaling up the model nor providing few-shot examples reliably improves verification: prompted Judges ranging from 4B to GPT-5.4 all plateau at 68%-70% macro-average agreement. This is because the value of a check depends on the environment rather than the task alone, and becomes apparent only through execution. Learning from execution is itself constrained, as the Actor's terminal state cannot be faithfully replicated during training, allowing only one verification attempt per state. We introduce VeriCUA, a proactive reward agent that learns its verification strategy from these single attempts. A trainable Judge decides what to check and when to stop, while a frozen Probe executes the checks in the live environment. Online reinforcement learning optimizes the Judge for both verdict correctness and efficient Probe use, with returns normalized across terminal states. Trained only on OSWorld and evaluated without further training on MobileWorld and WebArena-Verified, VeriCUA achieves the highest reward agreement across all three benchmarks and lies on the agreement-cost Pareto frontier among proactive verifiers. It surpasses few-shot GPT-5.4 by 5.36 points with 47.6%-59.8% fewer Probe tokens, and even a 1B VeriCUA exceeds every prompted Judge. As the reward for Actor RL, it raises task success by 3.21 points overall and 5.40 points on held-out multi-application tasks. These results identify the verification strategy, not verifier scale, as the key to reliable GUI rewards.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: SenseSwarm: Swarm Exploration via Neural Structure Estimation with Shared World-Anticipation for Rapid Mapping
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Mingkai Liu, Hoiian Au, Qian Zhang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: SenseSwarm enhances swarm exploration efficiency by using a shared neural map predictor, enabling faster and more accurate mapping of unknown environments compared to traditional methods.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: A robot swarm covers a building faster with more robots, but the map is only as complete as the space the robots have physically visited. We target the amount of an unknown building a decentralized swarm knows at each instant, ahead of physical coverage. SenseSwarm serves a lightweight learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and folds the predicted structure back into a stigmergic guidance field. Its 709K-parameter predictor is fine-tuned on the swarm's own multi-front observations, which we show is necessary: a single-robot predictor collapses on such views. We build a benchmark of twelve real building floors from HouseExpo, HKUST, and KTH, up to 24,000 square meters, and run 1,620 simulations across nine coordination methods, swarm sizes 32 to 512, and three seeds. On physical coverage the swarm is near parity with a greedy frontier planner, as expected. On map reconstruction, every non-predictive baseline needs 1.3 to 1.9 times longer to reach an 80 percent known map, and SenseSwarm holds an equal-time area lead of about 670 square meters, up to 1,359. Folding the prediction into the shared field matters: the same predictor applied per robot matches our speed but suffers a 6.9 times higher inter-robot contact rate at 512 robots. The prediction is computed once per shared map, so its cost stayed flat from 32 to 512 robots.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: All-in-One Memory: Process-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Memory Agents
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Bingbing Wang, Jingjie Lin, Weiming Qiao, Jing Li, Ruifeng Xu
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: The All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem) framework integrates retrieval and memory construction in reinforcement learning, enhancing answer accuracy in long-context tasks through a unified reward system.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Large language models increasingly rely on external memory to answer queries grounded in long-horizon histories such as multi-session dialogues and lengthy documents. However, existing memory methods often optimize retrieval and memory construction separately, without a shared reward space for evaluating search, writing, and stopping decisions. To address this, we propose All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem), which organizes these operations as transitions over a shared evidence state and directly evaluates the semantic quality of each action in a unified reward space. AiO-Mem compiles heterogeneous histories into source-traceable multi-view events, providing a shared substrate for retrieval and memory writing. A unified memory policy actor then rolls out complete interaction trajectories over this shared evidence state. A separate trajectory-conditioned process reward model is trained through evidence-grounded supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level DPO to assign process scores to the collected trajectories. These scores are aggregated into an action-balanced trajectory reward and used by Process-Aligned DAPO (PA-DAPO) to optimize the memory policy. Across long-context memory benchmarks, AiO-Mem consistently improves answer accuracy over both static memory systems and RL-trained memory agents.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: DEFlow: Deep Equilibrium Flow Maximum-Entropy Reinforcement Learning
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Ruslan Ageev, Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Jiarong Li, Wenbo Ding
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: DEFlow introduces a deep equilibrium flow policy that enhances sampling efficiency and off-policy training in reinforcement learning, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Expressive flow policies can represent multiple high-value actions, but sampling them with few integration steps while retaining tractable action densities remains challenging. We introduce DEFlow, a deep equilibrium flow policy that replaces explicit Euler sampling with implicit Euler integration and solves all intermediate actions jointly as an equilibrium system. We combine implicit differentiation with a discrete change-of-variables formula for the final-action density, enabling off-policy training within soft actor-critic without backpropagating through solver iterations. DEFlow achieves an average relative improvement of approximately 10% in mean successful coverage over the strongest baseline across four Multi-Goal docking variants. It also achieves the highest mean time-averaged return on four of five manipulation tasks, while remaining broadly competitive across five MuJoCo tasks. These results support implicit flow policies for tasks requiring both diversity and precision, at the cost of additional nonlinear and linear solves. Primary

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: MVGraph: Benchmarking LVLMs on Evidence Composition across Multi-View Visual Graph
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Yingjie Zhu, Han Cheng, Xuefeng Bai, Youcheng Pan, Yang Xiang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: MVGraph is a benchmark for assessing large vision-language models on multi-graph reasoning, highlighting challenges in evidence alignment and composition across interrelated visual graphs.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: We introduce MVGraph, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models (LVLMs) on multi-graph reasoning where the evidence required by a query is distributed across multiple interrelated visual graph views. Although such evidence commonly resides in source-specific graphs, temporal snapshots, or local observations, existing graph reasoning benchmarks remain confined to a single self-contained structure, assessing only graph perception and reasoning while leaving the alignment and composition of evidence across views underexplored. MVGraph comprises 8k instances spanning 8 \textit{graph-theoretic} tasks, abstracted from two multi-graph scenarios (partial and temporal graph views). Each problem is programmatically constructed and verified to be unsolvable from a single view. Beyond end-to-end evaluation, we decompose multi-graph reasoning into four complementary capabilities---Perception, Alignment, Composition, and Reasoning---and design 29 diagnostic tasks with 64k instances to probe each one, along with golden intermediate representations for evaluating the intermediate process. Across 15 LVLMs, we reveal the difficulty of multi-graph reasoning and identify cross-view edge alignment and relation-level composition as prominent bottlenecks through stage-oriented diagnostics. Meanwhile, temporal constraints and increasing view counts expose further capability boundaries. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AAAndy-Zhu/MVGraph.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Shiao Wang, Xiao Wang, Yuhe Ding, Jiarui Xu, Zikang Yan
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: UniMergeTrack introduces a hierarchical model merging approach for RGB-X visual object tracking, enhancing performance through task-specific optimization and cross-task knowledge integration.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: RGB-X tracking leverages complementary modalities, such as thermal infrared, event, or depth, to improve robustness under challenging conditions. Existing general-purpose RGB-X trackers typically follow two paradigms: independent task-specific training and joint training across modality combinations. However, the former suffers from knowledge isolation and model redundancy, while the latter introduces optimization interference across heterogeneous tasks. In this work, we present UniMergeTrack, a new model merging paradigm that preserves task-specific optimization while enabling effective cross-task knowledge integration. UniMergeTrack first trains modality-specific trackers independently and then performs hierarchical model merging. Specifically, transferable backbones are merged across RGB-X tasks via high-pass-filtered merging, and complemented by lightweight task-specific experts that preserve modality-specific cues. Tracking heads are merged within each task using optimal transport-guided channel alignment to mitigate hidden channel mismatch. A subsequent distribution alignment fine-tuning stage further improves compatibility between the unified backbone and task-specific heads. Extensive experiments on the LasHeR, RGBT234, VisEvent, VOT-RGBD22, COESOT, and CDTB benchmarks demonstrate that UniMergeTrack achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across RGB-Thermal, RGB-Event, and RGB-Depth tracking tasks, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen datasets. The source code will be released upon acceptance. The source code of this paper will be released on https://github.com/Event-AHU/OpenEvTracking.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: Jag: Direct Box Prediction for Efficient Visual Grounding
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Xiuyuan Zhu, Ke Lu, Hao Wu, Zijin Du, Dongming Zhang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: Jag introduces a direct box prediction method for visual grounding, enhancing accuracy and efficiency by adapting a pretrained multimodal model with geometric supervision.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Visual grounding combines image--language understanding with geometric prediction, yet autoregressive multimodal models often express a box as a coordinate sequence. Sequential decoding adds computation to the multimodal processing needed for localization. Adapting these representations to box geometry offers a route to direct prediction. We present Jag, which adapts a compact pretrained multimodal model for direct continuous box prediction. A lightweight regression head reads the last valid input-token state, conditioned on the image and referring expression, and predicts all four box coordinates together. Geometric supervision jointly adapts the language backbone, visual merger, and regression head, allowing localization losses to shape both the multimodal representations and the coordinate mapping. Inference retains image--language processing and returns the box in one forward pass, without coordinate generation or text parsing. Across benchmarks, Jag consistently improves grounding accuracy over its base model across the observed target sizes and expression groups. Component ablation show that jointly adapting the representations and head substantially improves accuracy over training the head alone. Against existing specialized grounding models, it achieves competitive accuracy with lower single-request latency and GPU memory use. These results show how supervision tailored to the geometric answer can specialize a compact pretrained multimodal model for accurate grounding and efficient direct prediction. Project page: https://xyzzzh.github.io/Jag/

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: UniCounting: Instance-Aware Proposal Consolidation for Image-Query-Free Multi-Category Counting
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Jinshi Liu, Pan Liu, Lei He, Weichao Luo, Rui Qian
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: UniCounting introduces a novel method for image-query-free multi-category counting by leveraging instance-aware structural inference to predict category counts from RGB images without explicit category input.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Visual counting is commonly formulated as counting a single specified target, with a model receiving an image-specific exemplar, text query, or target category and returning a single count. We instead study fixed-vocabulary image-query-free multi-category counting. A global vocabulary is fixed for each run, and, given only an RGB image, the model predicts a complete category--count vector without being told which categories appear. We present UniCounting, which casts counting as instance-aware structural inference over an over-complete proposal set. Generic segmenters produce duplicate masks, partial views, and proposals from neighboring instances; semantic scores can name them but cannot determine which denote the same object. Frozen SAM~2.1 generates masks, while frozen DINOv2 and OpenCLIP provide relation and category features. A 3,267-parameter category-shared relation head predicts same-instance affinities from instance-mask-derived supervision. Sparse graph construction, representative selection, labeling, and background-margin admission then convert each admitted component into one count with replayable group evidence. Only the relation head is trained, without count or density-map targets. On COCO clean500, UniCounting obtains lower point-estimate vector $\ell_1$ error and absent-class false mass than calibrated OWLv2-All80, with comparable micro presence F1. Under a matched decoder, the learned relation reduces both errors relative to mask containment, mask IoU, CLIP, and DINO, while revealing a fragmentation--merge trade-off. We also report transfer diagnostics on OmniCount-sub, FSC-147, and CARPK.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: EviViT: Evidence-Adaptive Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Perception
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Yaoxin Niu, Zhangquan Chen, Yang Zhang, Xiang An, Zhumei Wang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: EviViT enhances fine-grained visual perception in vision-language models by adaptively guiding token allocation and regional re-reading for improved contextual understanding and accuracy.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Fine-grained visual perception enables vision-language models to distinguish subtle attributes and ground their answers in visual evidence. In high-resolution scenes, processing the whole image at greater resolution spends visual tokens on irrelevant content, while isolated crops can lose the context needed to interpret the selected evidence. We introduce EviViT, a lightweight attachment that learns where a pretrained vision transformer should acquire detail. Human visual-search traces supervise a question-conditioned evidence density, which guides regional re-reading from the original pixels and the allocation of visual tokens. A sparse, coordinate-aware bridge then connects the regional features to the global scene, allowing the host to interpret precise evidence in context. Learned with the host backbone frozen, the attachment serves both the base model and compatible post-trained descendants without refitting. Experiments across nine hosts show consistent gains in average fine-grained accuracy. Matched-budget comparisons further show that EviViT outperforms global-only processing at every tested token ceiling while using fewer visual tokens.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: HaPRL: Human-Anchored Process Reinforcement Learning for Visual Search Agent
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Zhangquan Chen, Yaoxin Niu, Xiang An, Mingze Sun, Zhumei Wang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: HaPRL introduces a framework for visual search agents that enhances reinforcement learning by incorporating human search behavior, significantly improving training effectiveness and model performance.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Multi-turn visual search agents answer questions about high-resolution images by iteratively deciding where to look. Reinforcement learning for these agents rewards only the final answer, leaving the search process unsupervised. Consequently, faulty routes in which the reasoning process is erroneous yet the final result is correct arise frequently, which in turn leads to ineffective training, i.e., scaling along the wrong paths. In this paper, we introduce HaPRL, the first framework to reinforce the search process with human search behavior. We first build an annotation platform and collect 1K+ human-annotated data with fine-grained behavioral signals. During training, a carefully designed judge scores each rollout with task-adaptive weights, anchored on the distilled trace of how a human annotator actually searched the same image. Extensive experiments show that HaPRL consistently outperforms outcome-based RL, and early-stage process supervision yields 6.7x more improvement in subsequent outcome-based scaling. Our results also demonstrate the importance of aligning model behavior with human process annotation signals, which offer new insight into the training of foundation models.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: DSWM: Decomposed Spatio-Temporal World Model for Demand-Driven UAV Base Station Repositioning
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Shengjie Zhong, Zhongliang Zhao, Jingxuan Chen, Xianbin Cao, Xinmei Qiang
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: The DSWM model enhances UAV base station repositioning by integrating demand-driven planning with a latent recurrent state, achieving superior performance across multiple datasets.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle base stations (UAV-BSs) are expected to cover traffic demand that shifts across space and time, yet most repositioning schemes either re-solve an optimization problem per slot or learn reactive policies without an explicit demand model. We cast demand-driven fleet repositioning as latent-space decision-time planning and propose DSWM, a decomposed spatio-temporal world model: an agentic controller that perceives the demand field through a rolling observation window, retains operational context in a latent recurrent state, reasons about candidate motions by imagined rollouts under an uncertainty penalty, and coordinates the fleet through replanned first actions. DSWM learns a recurrent state-space model shaped by an exponential-moving-average (EMA) based latent predictive objective with variance regularization. It attaches a differentiable service simulator that replays the association, probabilistic line-of-sight channel, and Shannon rate chain inside latent rollouts. Planning uses a cross-entropy method whose imagined demand is anchored on the current observation window with mixing coefficient $ρ=0.95$. On a unified pipeline over three real datasets (Milan CDR (call detail record), Shanghai Telecom, YJMob100K) and 14 methods including five reproduced IEEE baselines, DSWM attains weekday served ratios of 0.889, 0.908, and 0.898, ranking first among non-ablated configurations on every dataset. On Milan it improves over the strongest non-learning baseline (Greedy, 0.780) by 0.109, a margin that comes from decision-time use of observations rather than prediction accuracy.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: Learning from synthetic photorealistic raindrop for single image raindrop removal
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Zhixiang Hao, Shaodi You, Yu Li, Kunming Li, Feng Lu
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: This paper presents a novel synthetic dataset of photorealistic raindrops and a deep learning framework for effective raindrop detection and removal in images.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Raindrops adhered to camera lens or windshield are inevitable in rainy scenes and can become an issue for many computer vision systems such as autonomous driving. Because raindrop appearance is affected by too many parameters, therefore it is unlikely to find an effective model based solution. Learning based methods are also problematic, because traditional learning method cannot properly model the complex appearance. Whereas deep learning method lacks sufficiently large and realistic training data. To solve it, in our work, we propose the first photo-realistic dataset of synthetic adherent raindrops for training. The rendering is physics based with consideration of the water dynamic, geometric and photometry. The dataset contains various types of rainy scenes and particularly the rainy driving scenes. Based on the modeling of raindrop imagery, we introduce a detection network which has the awareness of the raindrop refraction as well as its blurring. Based on that, we propose the removal network that can well recover the image structure. Rigorous experiments demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our proposed framework.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Chenxi Song, Yanming Yang, Tong Zhao, Ruibo Li, Joey Tianyi Zhou
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: WorldForge V2 enhances camera control in video diffusion models through a training-free guidance framework, achieving high-quality scene generation with minimal training data.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering. However, their use in spatial tasks is limited by imprecise camera control, spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and entangled camera motion with scene dynamics. Existing approaches, such as task-specific fine-tuning and post-process warping, often introduce visual artifacts, generalize poorly, or incur high computational costs. We propose WorldForge V2 to achieve accurate camera control while preserving the generative capabilities of pretrained video models. We first develop a training-free guidance framework using warped references to iteratively refine generation along a target camera path. Optical-flow analysis identifies motion-related latent channels for selective guidance, helping separate motion control from appearance. A dual-path strategy further compares guided and unguided predictions to correct artifacts from imperfect references. Together, these components guide viewpoint changes while preserving scene appearance and object motion. To reduce refinement costs, v-cache approximates the correction using the preceding denoising prediction, avoiding an additional model evaluation. We further extend motion localization from latent channels to network blocks and introduce Trajectory LoRA, which concentrates adaptation on blocks most responsive to trajectory guidance. A two-stage training strategy teaches these adapters to denoise the states encountered during guided generation, using limited supervision effectively. This enables reliable camera control with very little training data, with a single training scene already supporting generalization to unseen scenes. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations across multiple datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and trajectory accuracy in camera-controlled video generation.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: RoboJudge: Multimodal Language Models as Judges for Embodied Video Generation
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Siyuan Ma, Yu Qi, Cheng Ye, Ruotian Peng, Xinyi Xu
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: The paper introduces RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal language models as judges of embodied video generation, revealing gaps in alignment with human judgments and presenting RoboJudge-9B as a superior model.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Video generation models are promising foundations for embodied world models, but only if their generated rollouts are physically valid and faithful to task instructions. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to judge these properties, yet their agreement with human judgments on embodied videos has not been systematically evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce RoboJudge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs as judges of embodied video generation. The benchmark measures two fundamental dimensions, Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment, across 800 human-annotated videos from 8 source corpora and 10 video generators, spanning grippers, human hands, and dexterous hands. Experiments reveal uneven alignment between existing judges and human ratings: general-purpose MLLMs show lower agreement on physical adherence, while specialized video judges designed for general-domain physical reasoning do not consistently transfer to embodied scenarios. Motivated by these findings, we construct RoboJudge-Train, comprising 12K videos annotated with 25K human-verified scores and model-assisted rationales for Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment. We fine-tune a 9B MLLM on this dataset with supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, yielding RoboJudge-9B. Among the model judges evaluated on RoboJudge-Bench, RoboJudge-9B achieves the highest overall agreement, reaching a Pearson correlation of 0.719 with a statistically significant 0.089 gain over Gemini-3.7-Flash, the best-performing proprietary baseline in our evaluation. Training on RoboJudge-Train also yields gains on external benchmarks, including VideoPhy2 and Physion-Eval. We further use RoboJudge-9B as a downstream evaluator to benchmark video generation models according to Physical Adherence and Instruction Alignment.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Huachen Gao, Yang Yang, Xiaoqian Liang, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: HRoPE introduces a surface-aware positional encoding for multi-view transformers by using plane-induced homographies to enhance token alignment and perspective correction without requiring ground-truth geometry.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. Such sensor-centric formulations, however, describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the rich surface geometry of the scene region depicted by the token. In this paper, we advocate a shift toward surface-aware positional encoding that explicitly grounds patch tokens in the geometry of physical surfaces. We introduce HRoPE, which represents the local geometry of each patch as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of classical multi-view stereo. We inject token-level, plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations. This equips the transformer with a geometric prior for rectifying perspective distortions and aligning patch features across viewpoints. Our encoding requires no ground-truth geometry: the plane parameters can be predicted end-to-end under a view-synthesis objective alone, or derived from foundation models. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV show that our best variant of HRoPE consistently outperforms the evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis. Extensive ablations and analysis show the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. Please refer to our project page at: https://gaohchen.github.io/HRoPE

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Dongxu Wei, Qi Xu, Zhiqi Li, Hangning Zhou, Cong Qiu
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: This paper introduces a novel 3D scene generation method utilizing a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space, enhancing efficiency and spatial consistency over traditional 2D approaches.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the generated scenes. In this paper, we propose to perform 3D scene generation directly within a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space derived from powerful 2D foundation models (e.g., DINOv2, SigLIP2, DA3). Then we tame diffusion transformers to perform diffusion modeling directly in the 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded scene generation. In our experiments, we not only demonstrate the advantages of our method over 2D-based approaches in terms of efficiency and spatial consistency, but also comprehensively analyze the impact of 3D latent representation on 3D scene generation performance. Furthermore, we validate the favorable scalability of our method with respect to representation and model capacity.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: Teach the Magnitude, Not the Direction: Verifier-Anchored Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Multi-Step LLM Agents
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Zechuan Wang, Siyuan Lu, Hongxuan Zhang, Linjian Mo, Chenyi Zhuang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: The paper presents CrEST, a hierarchical credit assignment framework that enhances reinforcement learning for multi-turn agents by optimizing verified rewards and refining token contributions through self-teaching.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) directly optimizes verifier-defined outcomes for multi-turn tool-use agents, yet its trajectory-level credit assignment conflates heterogeneous per-turn outcomes into a single reward signal. On-policy distillation provides dense per-token supervision but uses a teacher-defined token-level objective and can be prone to gradient concentration collapse. We introduce $\textbf{CrEST}$, a hierarchical credit assignment framework that anchors each sampled token's scalar advantage sign to verified rewards while incorporating dense magnitude signals from a privileged self-teacher. $\textbf{CrEST}$ resolves credit at two levels: turn-segmented verified advantages address inter-turn dilution, while entropy-gated self-teacher modulation refines intra-turn token contributions. Experiments on BFCL V3 and WildToolBench show that $\textbf{CrEST}$ consistently outperforms both RL and distillation baselines across two model scales, with the largest gains on long-trajectory and strict session-level metrics. Our work demonstrates that the teacher's role in policy optimization can be reduced from determining token-level reinforcement or suppression to modulating update magnitudes, enabling dense credit assignment while keeping verifier rewards as the training objective.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Yuchen Deng, Shunkai Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu, Haibin Ling, Bingyao Huang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: LICOA enables mobile spatial augmented reality systems to autonomously project light based on language instructions and visual observations, achieving significant real-world task success rates.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Spatial augmented reality (SAR) augments physical environments with projected content, but most systems assume that the projector pose, target region, or motion path has been fixed or specified. We instead make projected light an embodied action: given a language instruction and current visual observations, a system must decide how to move and where and at what scale to place the projection. We introduce LICOA to realize this capability. Its differential-drive chassis provides room-scale approach and repositioning, while a steerable mirror with two degrees of freedom (2DoF) and projection scale provide rapid local control of the beam. A shared interface maps synchronized external and onboard RGB cameras with robot control state to physical optical actions across pretrained action models. Because instruction-conditioned optical action lacks dedicated training data and a common evaluation protocol, we construct a matched simulation embodiment and a corpus with 150 tasks and 7,500 rendered episodes, then evaluate models trained only on this corpus in previously unseen real-world environments. Across 480 complete closed-loop real-world execution trials (rollouts) on 12 tasks, the best adapted action model achieves a 57.50% success rate and 40.64% success weighted by path length, compared with 8.33% and 5.15% for the same architecture trained from scratch. A further 150 real-world ablation rollouts support the need for both camera views and coordinated control of the chassis and mirror. These results establish a physical platform, shared perception and optical action interface, corpus, and real-world evaluation protocol for treating projected light as an embodied action.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: RoboCloth: A Large-Scale Real Cloth Material Dataset for Neural Reflectance Reconstruction
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Zhen Li, Haoran Qin, Francesco Di Sario, Daniel Rebain, Andrea Tagliasacchi
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: RoboCloth is a comprehensive dataset of 500 real cloth materials captured with robotic precision, enabling advanced neural reflectance reconstruction and outperforming existing datasets in material fitting.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: We present RoboCloth, a dataset of 500 real cloth materials captured under flexible, calibrated camera and lighting configurations, where both are robotically controlled during acquisition. Each material is imaged in approximately 580 high-dynamic range frames spanning a wide view-light hemisphere; camera poses are refined via structure-from-motion and aligned to the robot frame, yielding per-material sparse surface geometry and structured per-point reflectance observations ready for neural material training. We demonstrate the value of this data through a two-stage neural reconstruction pipeline: Stage 1 trains a shared MLP decoder on our corpus to learn cloth material priors; Stage 2 then freezes the decoder and fits a dense 2048x2048 latent texture to each target material. Evaluating on held-out materials from our own dataset and on the independent UBO2014 benchmark, we show that a decoder trained on our captures outperforms decoders trained on existing measured reflectance datasets and analytic PBR fitting, transferring to unseen acquisition systems without modification. The dataset, calibration files, observation tensors, and train/test splits are released under CC BY 4.0 on the Hugging Face Hub.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: GRASE: Geometry-native Real-to-sim Agentic Scene Modeling from Video
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Zhaorui Lin, Haohan Liu, Zhen Chen, Xiangru Huang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: GRASE is an innovative framework that enhances real-to-sim 3D scene modeling by iteratively revising hypotheses based on multi-view video feedback, ensuring geometric consistency.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Real-to-sim conversion aims to turn a captured video of a real environment into an editable 3D scene while preserving the geometry and layout of what was observed. Existing methods often follow a one-pass, loosely coupled paradigm: each stage receives only limited feedback from previous stages, allowing errors to propagate without reliable correction and leaving the final scene inconsistent. We present GRASE, an agentic framework that closes this loop by treating the captured multi-view video observations as a standing reference throughout scene modeling. Instead of committing to intermediate estimates, GRASE revises its current hypothesis whenever rendered evidence disagrees with the capture, overcoming the fixed intermediate assumptions of conventional pipelines. Specifically, GRASE first fits the architectural shell and its openings from depth and multi-view cues. An agent then places generated assets in a shared coordinate frame while checking their spatial relationships. Finally, each asset's geometry and placement are refined iteratively to improve agreement across the observed views. By coupling these steps through feedback, GRASE localizes structural discrepancies and revises only the responsible components, while preserving cross-view consistency. The resulting 3D scenes are faithful to the input, consistent across views, and suitable for simulations. In our experiments, GRASE substantially outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including a direct real-to-sim conversion using GPT6-Astra.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: TRACE: Typed Reference-Aware Conversational Editing for Humanoid Motion Diffusion
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Zejian Kang, Yifu Luo, Boyang Shen, Jingxuan Li, Zekai Chen
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: TRACE is a framework that enhances humanoid motion generation and editing by using typed kinematic quantities to improve semantic alignment and motion quality through natural language requests.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Language-conditioned humanoid motion generation enables users to create and refine robot movements through natural language. The central challenge is to connect an underspecified request to concrete motion structure that can subsequently be revised relative to an accepted reference. We present TRACE, a generation and editing framework for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot built around typed, measurable kinematic quantities. Our insight is to ground generation conditions in paired training motions and editing goals in the current motion. A language model learns to predict support, root, and hand events from motion-derived supervision; their time-aligned encodings complement the original text in a diffusion generator. Gravity-referenced states and trajectory--contact objectives improve kinematic consistency. For editing, typed requests define body--time scopes and source-relative goals. A separate reference-conditioned diffusion editor uses these goals and revised events to realize changes, while sampling-time projection preserves protected state coordinates. Quantitative evaluation and human assessment show improved semantic alignment and motion quality over the compared methods. Controlled ablations support the value of motion-grounded conditioning and kinematic consistency, while multi-turn editing evaluations demonstrate more reliable execution of successive relative requests under shared preservation constraints. Together, these results support typed kinematic structure as a common basis for motion generation and reference-aware revision.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Qingsong Xie, Jiahao Tian, Jiacheng Tang, Zhifeng Li, Madalina Ciobanu
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: The paper introduces GroundGUI, a GUI grounding model enhanced by the ScreenRef dataset and a novel Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning method, achieving superior performance across multiple benchmarks.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Constructing robust GUI agents relies on multimodal visual grounding: the ability to precisely map natural language intents to actionable on-screen components. Despite abundant desktop, web, and mobile benchmarks, high-fidelity resources tailored for diverse environments are surprisingly scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Screen Referring Grounding Dataset (ScreenRef), a comprehensive GUI grounding dataset consisting of GUI screenshots paired with natural language referring expressions and box or point annotations. Spanning desktop, web, and mobile domains, ScreenRef comprises 586K screenshots and over 633K referring expression instances, covering tasks such as text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal scenarios. To boost the model's grounding performance, we propose the Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning (D2RL) method to address the limited generalization of supervised fine-tuning and the sparse reward problem in reinforcement learning. Utilizing ScreenRef, we train Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct via sequential SFT and D2RL training, yielding GroundGUI-8B. GroundGUI-8B achieves 95.2% on ScreenSpot-V2, 63.9% on ScreenSpot-Pro, 65.4% on OSWorld-G, 86.8% on MMBench-GUI L2, and 38.3% on UI-Vision. Among 8B-scale models, it produces substantial gains over models trained on open-source datasets, with performance comparable or even superior to models trained on closed-source data. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/PrentisAI/GroundGUI.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Diyuan Shi, Yiqi Tang, Hongyin Zhang, You Wu, Donglin Wang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: VLRLA enhances vision-language-action models with in-context reinforcement learning for adaptive, deployment-time improvement of robotic manipulation tasks based on accumulated interaction experience.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual perception and language understanding with robot control, providing a foundation for instruction-conditioned manipulation. However, conventional pretrained VLA policies lack a mechanism for gradual adaptation through accumulated interaction experience during deployment. We therefore propose VLRLA, a general framework that equips existing VLA models with \textit{in-context reinforcement learning} capabilities for deployment-time adaptation. Our approach augments a VLA model with a reinforcement learning module that learns from historical observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals. During deployment, the policy gradually refines its action generation and progressively improves task success while keeping model parameters fixed. Our approach is also designed for general applicability and compatibility with diverse learning history construction strategies and model training pipelines. Finally, through extensive experiments, we systematically investigate the learning properties of VLRLA in simulation and demonstrate its ability to adapt to unseen scenarios during real-world deployment.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: CoTL: Compact Token Learning for 3D Scene Representation
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Han Liang, Sibo Wu, Anpei Chen, Rüdiger Westermann
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: CoTL introduces a compact token framework for 3D scene representation from unposed multi-view images, enabling efficient novel-view synthesis and generative modeling through learned Gaussian primitives.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: We present CoTL, a framework that learns a compact set of tokens that preserves scene geometry and appearance from unposed multi-view images. Our encoder compresses the input images into small per-view sets of latent tokens that aggregate information across views to form a view-consistent scene representation. Each additional view expands the representation with only a small, resolution-independent set of tokens, allowing its capacity to grow with the available observations. To force this compact bottleneck to retain sufficient scene information, a query-based Gaussian decoder uses scene-independent queries to attend to the learned tokens and recover an explicit, renderable set of 3D Gaussian primitives. Novel-view rendering supervision trains the compact representation end to end through the reconstructed Gaussian scene. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID show that the resulting compact, unstructured token set supports competitive novel-view synthesis and can serve as the latent space of a generative model for 3D Gaussian scene generation. Together, these results show that 3D Gaussian reconstruction is an effective objective for compact scene representation learning and the learned token space provides a basis for broader downstream tasks in 3D vision.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: SDPAD: A Fully Spike-Driven Pipeline for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Chengjun Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Jie Yang, Mohamad Sawan
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: SDPAD is a novel spike-driven autonomous driving pipeline that achieves high accuracy and low energy consumption, outperforming previous spiking neural network planners while matching ANN performance.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving demands trajectory planners that are both highly accurate and cheap enough for edge deployment. State-of-the-art artificial neural network (ANN) planners meet the accuracy requirement at the cost of heavy dense computation, while spiking neural networks (SNNs)---though promising orders-of-magnitude energy savings through sparse, event-driven arithmetic---still lag far behind in planning accuracy. We present \textbf{SDPAD}, a fully spike-driven end-to-end planning pipeline that closes this gap. SDPAD converts a pre-trained ANN perception stack into integer-spike form via quantized ANN2SNN conversion, lifts multi-view images into the bird's-eye-view (BEV) space with a spike-driven-max (SDM) depth distribution (Spike-3D-Lift), and plans through the Spike-QFormer, a spiking query transformer in which ego, agent, and map queries distilled from the BEV scene are fused by learnable waypoint queries via cross-attention, followed by deformable spike-cross-attention refinement. Every operation is gated by integer spikes and inference is a single feed-forward pass without temporal simulation loops. On the nuScenes open-loop benchmark, SDPAD achieves an average $L_2$ error of 0.40\,m and a collision rate of 0.12\%, on par with strong ANN planners while consuming 69.9\,mJ---less than 2\% of recent ANN baselines. In closed-loop evaluation on the NAVSIM navtest split, SDPAD reaches 86.3 PDMS, surpassing the previous SNN planner SAD by 4.3 points and matching mainstream ANN planners at a fraction of their energy. To our knowledge, SDPAD is the first fully spike-driven planner evaluated in end-to-end autonomous driving, demonstrating that SNNs can rival dense ANNs in complex driving tasks.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: Slot3R: Set-Associative Spatial Memory for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Xiyuan Zhang, Yanming Yang, Kaiyuan Xu, Ruibo Li, Chi Zhang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: Slot3R enhances streaming 3D reconstruction by enabling multiple states at shared addresses, significantly improving accuracy and efficiency over Point3R while maintaining a frozen backbone.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction must preserve evidence from each frame while processing an expanding scene online. Spatial memory is a natural fit because it organizes history by reconstructed 3D location. Yet Point3R uses spatial proximity both to associate a new observation with an existing memory entry and to decide whether to fuse it, conflating co-location with state identity. Because pointers summarize image patches, nearby pointers may encode distinct surfaces, viewpoints, or visibility conditions; averaging them can destroy complementary evidence before later frames disambiguate it. We argue that location should determine address, not whether observations must merge. Slot3R realizes this principle as a training-free, set-associative retrofit that lets multiple states coexist at a shared address while keeping the pretrained Point3R backbone frozen. A bounded sparse readout further decouples persistent storage from per-frame decoder access. At 300-500 sampled frames, Slot3R reduces Point3R's point-cloud accuracy error (Acc) by 57.1%-63.1% on 7Scenes and 64.0%-72.0% on NeuralRGBD, lowers Sim(3)-aligned absolute trajectory error (ATE) on all three pose benchmarks, and remains competitive on video-depth estimation. It completes all evaluated settings from 600 to 1000 sampled frames at about 19 FPS under the same protocol, whereas Point3R and InfiniteVGGT run out of memory at 800 frames and beyond.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: EmbodiedSmith: Scaling Embodied Data through Recursive Self-Improvement Flywheel in Simulation
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Yikai Qin, Yifei Deng, Mingjian Liang, Wenxuan Song, Zepeng Lin
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: EmbodiedSmith is a framework that enhances robotic data generation through recursive self-improvement, unifying scene and task generation for diverse, scalable simulation environments.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Scaling robotic foundation models requires diverse training data and reliable evaluation environments. Simulation offers a scalable solution, yet existing generation pipelines remain constrained by predefined assets and skills, a disconnect between scene generation and task generation, and limited support for complex embodiments and physics. We introduce EmbodiedSmith, a framework for scalable embodied data generation through recursive self-improvement (RSI). EmbodiedSmith unifies asset, scene, and task generation in a pipeline that supports autonomous creation and language-driven customization. Its core is an agentic refinement loop: scene generation anticipates downstream task requirements, while task generation guides targeted scene edits, allowing scenes and tasks to iteratively improve one another. This joint refinement improves task generation success, including for long-horizon tasks. The framework further supports mobile manipulators, humanoids, and dexterous hands, as well as interactions involving deformable objects and fluids, broadening the range of behaviors and physical phenomena represented in generated data. Together, these capabilities provide a flexible simulation engine for both robot pretraining and evaluation. Extensive experiments validate the quality, diversity, and generation efficiency of the resulting data, while downstream policy experiments demonstrate that increased data diversity improves generalization.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: Discrete Forcing: Infusing Discrete Guidance into Continuous Denoising for Few-Step Action Experts
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Jingbo Wang, Wenxuan Song, Wenhao Yu, Han Zhao, Xi Wang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: The paper presents Discrete Forcing, a framework that integrates discrete and continuous action representations for efficient, high-precision action generation in vision-language-action models.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Efficient action generation in vision-language-action (VLA) models requires capturing both coarse action structure and fine-grained details. Discrete action tokens provide compact structural representations but sacrifice precision, while continuous action tokens offer high precision but often require multiple denoising steps. We introduce Discrete Forcing, a flow-matching framework that combines these representations through an explicit coarse-to-fine generation process. It first predicts discrete action tokens to establish a coarse action structure, then uses them to guide continuous action refinement. The discrete and continuous components share a common diffusion transformer backbone with specialized branches, maintaining a parameter count comparable to a conventional single-branch model while requiring only one forward pass per branch. Extensive evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate improved performance and faster inference over a parameter-matched continuous action expert, with consistent performance gains as model capacity increases. Real-world experiments further demonstrate improvements on high-precision and dynamic manipulation tasks.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Junshu Pan, Zhizhang Fu, Shulin Huang, Yiran Ding, Zifan Cheng
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: The paper introduces Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), enhancing reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by improving token-level credit assignment to boost reasoning accuracy.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet their predictions remain sensitive to task-irrelevant prompt features. We investigate this sensitivity through semifactual prompt interventions that preserve the underlying problem and its answer. Our analysis reveals substantial variation in token-level sensitivity and shows that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding improves reasoning accuracy without updating model weights. These findings highlight a limitation of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which assigns the same outcome-derived advantage to every response token and may reinforce potential spurious dependence alongside useful reasoning. Motivated by this observation, we introduce Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), a causally inspired variant of GRPO that incorporates semifactual stability into token-level credit assignment. SCAPO measures token probability drift for fixed responses under semifactual interventions and uses normalized stability scores to reduce advantages for relatively unstable tokens during early training, while granting no additional credit for stability alone. On Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, SCAPO improves AIME 2024-2026 accuracy over GRPO by 5.63 and 4.17 percentage points, respectively. At both model scales, SCAPO achieves the best results on most evaluated mathematics benchmarks and all evaluated out-of-distribution benchmarks among the compared methods. These results suggest that semifactual stability provides an effective training signal for improving reasoning and generalization through finer-grained credit assignment in RLVR. The code is available at https://github.com/DtYXs/SCAPO.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: PreferenceFlow: Test-Time Guidance of Flow-Matching Robot Policies from Human Interventions
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Yiqi Tang, Diyuan Shi, Runze Li, Donglin Wang
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: PreferenceFlow enhances flow-matching robot policies at test time using human interventions for guidance, achieving a 90.5% success rate in precision tasks without environment rewards.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Flow-matching policies can represent complex robot behaviors but remain susceptible to local errors under distribution shift at deployment. Many reinforcement learning approaches to policy improvement require reward signals that are difficult to specify or obtain in real-world manipulation. We present PreferenceFlow, a framework for improving a pretrained flow policy at test time without environment rewards or updates to the base policy. Human intervention chunks are paired with robot chunks generated from the same initial conditioning state to train a preference model. During infer- ence, we adopt the QGF sampling update, replacing its value gradient with the preference gradient evaluated at an estimated clean action. A gradient-cap loss penalizes excessive gradients on intervention pairs, while a zero-gradient loss discourages guidance near actions from expert demonstrations. On four real-world precision insertion tasks with a Franka robot, Pref- erenceFlow achieves a mean success rate of 90.5%, compared with 69% for the frozen policy. Ablations support the roles of gradient regularization and correctly ordered preference labels in the evaluated settings. These results demonstrate the utility of human interventions as local preference supervision for guiding frozen generative robot policies.

西安电子科技大学.title: FluxVLA Engine: A One-Stop VLA Engineering Platform for Embodied Intelligence
西安电子科技大学.authors_text: Yinhao Li, Weixin Mao, Zihan Lan, Jikun Rong, Qirui Hu
西安电子科技大学.summary: The FluxVLA Engine is a comprehensive platform that standardizes and integrates various components of embodied intelligence to enhance reproducibility and deployment of VLA models in robotics.
西安电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models, world-action models (WAMs), and offline reinforcement learning methods are rapidly expanding the design space of embodied policies, yet turning these algorithms into reliable robot systems remains constrained by fragmented data formats, training stacks, evaluation protocols, inference runtimes, and embodiment-specific interfaces. We present $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ Engine, an open, configuration-driven platform that turns heterogeneous embodied-policy components into a reproducible data-to-deployment workflow. Rather than introducing another policy model, $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ standardizes interfaces for datasets, visual-language and world models, action heads, reward- or advantage-weighted learning, distributed training, simulation evaluation, optimized inference, and robot operators. The engine further integrates compositional dual-arm simulation, scalable automatic data generation, and model-decoupled human-in-the-loop rollout, takeover, correction collection, and reward annotation. For responsive physical execution, it combines Real-Time Chunking (RTC) with accelerated inference backends, lightweight remote GPU serving, and configurable trajectory post-processing. Together, these capabilities connect offline learning, simulation validation, online correction, and real-robot execution through shared and auditable contracts. $\mathrm{FluxVLA}$ therefore targets the engineering bottlenecks separating promising embodied-learning algorithms from reproducible evaluation and dependable deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/FluxVLA/FluxVLA

西安电子科技大学.title: Learn to Modify: Self-evolving Multi-agent Refinement Framework for Conversational Text-to-Motion Generation
西安电子科技大学.authors_text: Jianan Li, Jiawei Zhao, Yangtao Zhou, Zhifu Zhao, Shaoxin Wu
西安电子科技大学.summary: The paper presents SMART, a self-evolving multi-agent framework for conversational text-to-motion generation that enables efficient, localized motion refinements based on user feedback.
西安电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Despite rapid progress in text-to-motion generation, existing methods are commonly designed for single-shot generation. When users are dissatisfied with specific motion details, they are often forced to regenerate the entire sequence from scratch, which is computationally inefficient and potentially destroys previously established kinematic context. A practical generation system should instead support iterative user feedback and refine only the affected spatio-temporal regions while preserving the remaining motion. Therefore, we introduce a conversational motion generation paradigm that requires the system to coordinate instruction understanding, motion generation, localized editing, and quality assessment. Recent advances in LLM-driven multi-agent systems provide a promising foundation for such role-specialized coordination. To tackle these challenges, a Self-evolving Multi-Agent RefinemenT Framework (SMART) is proposed for conversational motion generation. Within SMART, to preserve semantic consistency, we design a semantic-guided masked motion editing mechanism, which precisely grounds natural language feedback into spatiotemporal motion regions to enable localized refinements without altering unedited regions. To reduce redundant exploration, we propose a memory-based self-evolving strategy that dynamically accumulates motion editing knowledge from interaction history and reuses past successful experience. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMART effectively supports multi-turn conversational motion generation and enables efficient motion refinement.

西安电子科技大学.title: Where Natural Language Ends in Agents: Executable Skill Composition with MetaSkill
西安电子科技大学.authors_text: Meng Shu, Wei He, Hang Zhou, Runke Liu, Kai Han
西安电子科技大学.summary: The paper presents MetaSkill, a hybrid representation enabling executable skill composition in agents by formalizing coordination and dependencies while preserving local task flexibility.
西安电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Agent Skills express open-ended task knowledge in natural language, but composing them requires persistent execution order and upstream-output handoffs. We propose selective formalization at Skill boundaries: coordination relations with stable references and machine-checkable constraints become executable, while substantive task judgments remain within Skills. We introduce MetaSkill, a hybrid representation that preserves complete Skill packages and local instructions while making invocation dependencies and predecessor-text bindings executable through a directed acyclic graph (DAG) runtime. This interface supports explicit coordination without prescribing how each Skill performs its local task. Across 20 multi-Skill artifact tasks and two LLMs, we compare natural-language procedures, prompt-visible graphs, and MetaSkill derived from a common frozen plan per task, using the same designated Skill packages. Additional comparisons evaluate AgentSkillOS with the same available Skill packages as MetaSkill, as well as agent systems using their configured tools. Blinded artifact judgments yield favorable preference point estimates across all reported comparisons, with 95% task-bootstrap intervals excluding parity against Prompt Graph under DeepSeek-V4-Flash and OpenClaw under GLM-5.2. In audited GLM-5.2 execution traces, all planned nodes complete and all declared precedence constraints are satisfied. Together, these findings support MetaSkill as a practical interface for composing open-ended Skills, combining local linguistic flexibility with executable dependencies, explicit predecessor-text bindings, and auditable coordination. Code is available at: https://github.com/TokenRhythm/opensquilla/tree/paper/metaskill-lp4fm-2026

西安电子科技大学.title: Revealing and Bridging the Physical Executability Gap in Vision-Language Navigation
西安电子科技大学.authors_text: Gang He, Zhile Cheng, Kepeng Xu, Zhenyang Liu, Yu-Wing Tai
西安电子科技大学.summary: The paper introduces VeSTA, a framework that aligns vision-language navigation with physically executable actions, addressing the gap between semantic understanding and physical feasibility in robotic navigation.
西安电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Continuous vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is typically evaluated by goal-reaching success, assuming it reflects an agent's ability to execute language-grounded behavior. We show that this assumption can fail: permissive contact models in current simulators may mask physically infeasible actions, creating a physical executability gap between semantic competence and embodied realization. To bridge this gap, we introduce Visual-Semantic Traversability Alignment (VeSTA), a framework that aligns VLN policies with physically executable futures. We define visual-semantic traversability as the ability to predict instruction-conditioned trajectories that are semantically valid, geometrically feasible, and physically robust. VeSTA addresses this misalignment through two complementary mechanisms: improving executable support in trajectory generation and risk-aware selection among multimodal futures. Specifically, Trajectory Relative Group Policy Optimization uses strict-contact feedback to reshape the candidate distribution toward executable regions, while the Traversability Risk Critic learns a risk-adjusted scalar utility for candidate-wise future selection. Experiments on R2R and RxR reveal substantial dependence of existing VLN agents on simulator contact semantics.
