南京大学.summary: This paper presents a method for enhancing LiDAR perception in autonomous driving by improving robustness to point-cloud corruption while reducing latency and memory usage.
南京大学.debug_abstract: LiDAR-based 3D object detection is a core perception service for autonomous driving, but deployment requires robustness to point-cloud corruption while meeting latency and memory requirements. Existing approaches address robustness and resource efficiency separately, resulting in compact detectors that are fragile under corruption or robust detectors that remain costly to deploy. We therefore formulate LiDAR perception provisioning as constructing a detector that remains accurate under point-cloud corruptions while meeting constraints on inference latency and peak GPU memory. To achieve robustness, we first craft corrupted samples that mimic extreme weather conditions. Then we train candidate detectors offline by ordering clean and corrupted samples by perturbation sensitivity, through which detectors learn more from hard corrupted samples. We estimate perturbation sensitivity using an ensemble of seven heterogeneous 3D detectors by tracking changes in confidence, BEV overlap, and unmatched detections. To improve efficiency, we narrow the network and use offline neighborhood-density measurements to determine how many points and neighbors each sampling stage processes. We evaluate our method using AP (Average Precision) under clean and corrupted conditions, inference latency, and peak allocated GPU memory. On KITTI for Car detection with PointRCNN, our method improves Moderate AP under corruption by 3.32 points over the original detector while reducing mean latency by 19.8% and peak allocated GPU memory by 53.9%. Across two datasets, two detector architectures, and three object classes, our method improves AP under corruption by 4.03 points on average over the corresponding original detectors, while reducing mean inference latency and peak allocated GPU memory by 14.4% and 38.0%, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/drunklibai/robust-efficient-lidar-perception.

南京大学.title: Metric Depth Estimation from Arbitrarily Degraded Low-Resolution Depth Prompts
南京大学.authors_text: Kun Wang, Yun Zhu, Pan Zhou, Na Zhao
南京大学.summary: AdaDS is an Adaptive Diffusion Sampling framework that enhances metric depth estimation from low-resolution prompts, effectively mitigating artifacts and improving robustness to degradations.
南京大学.debug_abstract: We propose AdaDS, an Adaptive Diffusion Sampling framework for prompted metric depth estimation, which estimates high-resolution metric depth from an image and an arbitrarily degraded low-resolution depth prompt. This setting is commonly studied as depth super-resolution, where existing methods typically regress depth directly without an explicit prior over high-quality depth, and thus often produce artifacts under severe or unseen degradations. In contrast, AdaDS exploits the contraction property of Gaussian smoothing: as noise accumulates in the forward diffusion process, the noisy distributions of degraded prompts and their high-quality counterparts converge toward an isotropic Gaussian prior, while the prompt content is gradually erased. Accordingly, AdaDS refines the prompt and estimates its uncertainty to adaptively select a starting timestep, and injects learned noise to place the intermediate sample in a high-density region of the depth distribution learned by a pre-trained diffusion model. Denoising from this sample yields high-quality depth with fine-grained details and corrects residual errors, even under imperfect prompt refinement. Experiments on real-world and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate its superior zero-shot generalization and robustness to diverse degradations.

南京大学.title: SPAR: Structural Pruning and Action Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Models
南京大学.authors_text: Shenli Zheng, Zhou Fang, Yuan Du, Yijiang Liu, Li Du
南京大学.summary: SPAR effectively reduces VLA model size by 67% while enhancing performance through structural pruning and reinforcement learning, achieving significant speedup and improved success rates.
南京大学.debug_abstract: The limited onboard computing resources of robots make the inference demands of vision-language-action (VLA) models costly to accommodate. Reducing these demands through aggressive compression, however, can degrade manipulation performance beyond what supervised fine-tuning alone recovers. We present SPAR (Structural Pruning and Action Recovery), which simultaneously prunes the hidden and feed-forward intermediate dimensions of the large language model (LLM) backbone through pruning-aware tuning, then applies reinforcement learning (RL) to recover policy performance. Applied to $π_{0.5}$, SPAR reduces the language backbone from 2.34B to 0.09B parameters and the full model from 3.37B to 1.12B, removing approximately 96% and 67% of their parameters, respectively. At this compression level, RL raises average success across the four LIBERO suites from 84.55% to 93.45%, an 8.90-percentage-point gain. The compressed policy achieves a $1.98\times$ full-policy inference speedup over the unpruned model. These results identify substantial intermediate-dimension redundancy and show that post-pruning RL can recover manipulation performance in compact policies.

南京大学.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
南京大学.authors_text: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li
南京大学.summary: MemForest is a memory compression framework that efficiently partitions and merges agent memory, achieving significant storage reduction and retrieval speedup while maintaining high performance.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Agent memory systems have demonstrated significant potential in long-term dialogue, personalized assistants, and video understanding. However, continuously accumulated memory introduces substantial storage and retrieval costs during inference. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{MemForest}, a general memory compression framework adaptable to various agent memory systems. Specifically, MemForest partitions historical memory into event-centric units by leveraging global semantic similarity and local temporal continuity. For each unit, it constructs a maximum spanning tree, termed an EventTree, and progressively merges redundant memory nodes by selecting high-weight edges, reducing storage overhead. Furthermore, we introduce an anchor-guided propagation retrieval mechanism that retrieves relevant memory nodes from the temporal neighborhoods of key nodes, improving retrieval accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MemForest. Under the unimodal Mem0 framework, MemForest retains \textbf{97.1%} of the original performance while compressing \textbf{50%} of historical memory across three benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and PersonaMem), achieving a \textbf{1.89x} retrieval speedup. Under the multimodal M3-Agent framework, it preserves \textbf{99.7%} of the original performance with a \textbf{50%} compression ratio across two benchmarks (M3-Bench-robot and M3-Bench-web), achieving a \textbf{2.24x} retrieval speedup. \textcolor{RoyalBlue}{\textit{Our code is available at [https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}}](https://github.com/Celina-love-sweet/MemForest.}})

南京大学.title: CoLVR: Enhancing Exploratory Latent Visual Reasoning via Contrastive Optimization
南京大学.authors_text: Ziyang Ding, Linjian Meng, Yiming Wu, Yuhan Li, Yuhao Liu
南京大学.summary: CoLVR enhances exploratory latent visual reasoning in MLLMs through a novel contrastive optimization framework, improving representation diversity and reasoning performance on various benchmarks.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Due to the potential for exploratory reasoning of Latent Visual Reasoning, recent works tend to enable MLLMs (Multimodal Large Language Models) to perform visual reasoning by propagating continuous hidden states instead of decoding intermediate steps into discrete tokens. However, existing works typically rely on hard alignment objectives to force latent representations to match predefined visual features, thereby severely limiting the exploratory of latent reasoning process. To address this problem, we propose CoLVR (Contrastive Optimization for Latent Visual Reasoning). To obtain a more exploratory visual reasoning, CoLVR introduces a latent contrastive training framework. Firstly, CoLVR learns diverse and exploratory representations with a latent contrastive objective guided by angle-based perturbation, which expands the semantic latent space and avoids over-constrained embedding. Then, CoLVR employs a latent trajectory contrastive reward for RL (Reinforcement Learning) post-training to enable fine-grained optimization of latent visual reasoning process and thus fostering diverse reasoning behaviors. Experiments demonstrate that CoLVR significantly enhances the exploratory capability of latent representations, achieving average improvements of 5.83% on VSP and 8.00% on Jigsaw, while also outperforming existing latent models on out of domain benchmarks, with a 3.40% gain on MMStar. The data, codes, and models are released at https://github.com/Oscar-dzy/CoLVR.

南京大学.title: Beyond Semantic Organization: Memory as Execution State Management for Long-Horizon Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Yaoqi Chen, Haibin Lai, Yuru Feng, Chuyu Han, Qianxi Zhang
南京大学.summary: The paper introduces MAGE, a hierarchical memory management system for long-horizon agents that enhances task success rates and reduces token consumption by effectively managing execution states.
南京大学.debug_abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks with interdependent decisions, where each action reshapes future constraints and intermediate errors can cascade. Existing RAG and agent memory systems organize histories by semantic similarity, retrieving content-relevant entries at decision time. We argue that this design mismatches execution-state dependencies: it fragments decision trajectories and mixes valid and erroneous traces, hindering coherent state reconstruction and error isolation. We propose MAGE (Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration), an active execution-state manager that stores interactions in a hierarchical state tree. The agent derives its state from the active root-to-current path, combining subgoal summaries, recent traces, and hints from prior branches. Four coupled operations maintain the tree: Grow records new traces, Compress summarizes completed subgoals, Maintain validates summaries, and Revise restores a target boundary and resumes on a new branch. This design bounds context growth while preserving state integrity and isolating flawed segments from the active path. Experiments on MemoryArena show that MAGE improves the average task success rate by 7.8--20.4 pp over baselines, while reducing token consumption by 55.1%. Code is available at: https://github.com/Komorebi660/MAGE.

南京大学.title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
南京大学.authors_text: Jinglin Dai, Jiawan Wang, Ruiqi Hong, Lei Bu
南京大学.summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical feedback framework that enhances LLMs' ability to generate executable plans for cyber-physical systems by addressing intent misinterpretation and feasibility issues.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.

南京大学.title: VTrajEmbed: Aligning Text with Video Object Trajectories via Spatiotemporal Embeddings
南京大学.authors_text: Ruizhi Chen, Zining Fan, Yudi Guo, Jiang Liu, Zhiyu Lin
南京大学.summary: VTrajEmbed introduces a novel embedding model that aligns text with video object trajectories through enhanced trajectory encoding and contrastive learning, significantly improving retrieval accuracy.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Fine-grained alignment between text and video object trajectories is a core challenge in multimodal understanding. Existing embedding models excel at global retrieval, yet their single global representation entangles multiple objects and their spatiotemporal dynamics, limiting direct object-level grounding. To address this issue, we propose VTrajEmbed, an embedding model that decomposes a video into object trajectories and aligns each trajectory embedding with text for object-level grounding through retrieval. Our main contributions: (1)Slow-Fast Trajectory Encoding, a dual-branch architecture that establishes trajectory representations by densely sampling low-resolution frames for high-frequency motion cues and sparsely selecting high-resolution frames for scene context, aggregated by a shared LLM backbone; (2)Mask-Guided Contrastive Learning, a training objective built upon these representations that couples an intra-group loss and a batch-level bidirectional loss under a relation mask, excluding unverified relations and preventing confirmed matches from becoming false negatives; (3)Text2Traj-Bench, a trajectory-level text-video benchmark with model-assisted construction and human-verified query--trajectory relations. Experimental results show that VTrajEmbed-5B improves text-to-trajectory and trajectory-to-text R@1 over Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B by 15.48 and 18.05 percentage points, respectively, and achieves 49.48% average R@1 across five global retrieval benchmarks, compared with 42.86% for Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B.

南京大学.title: Paint Outside the Box: Synthesizing and Selecting Training Data for Visual Grounding
南京大学.authors_text: Zilin Du, Haoxin Li, Jianfei Yu, Boyang Li
南京大学.summary: The paper presents POBF, a novel framework that synthesizes training data for visual grounding by inpainting and selectively filtering data, improving performance in data-scarce settings.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Visual grounding aims to localize the image regions based on a textual query. Given the difficulty of large-scale data curation, we investigate how to effectively learn visual grounding under data-scarce settings in this paper. To address the data scarcity, we propose a novel framework, POBF (Paint Outside the Box and Filter). POBF synthesizes images by inpainting outside the box, tackling a label misalignment issue encountered in previous works. Furthermore, POBF leverages an innovative filtering scheme to select the most effective training data. This scheme combines a hardness score and an overfitting score, balanced by a penalty term. Extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets demonstrate that POBF consistently improves performance, achieving an average gain of 5.83\% over the real-data-only method and outperforming leading baselines by 2.29\%-3.85\% in accuracy. Additionally, we validate the robustness and generalizability of POBF across various generative models, training data sizes, and model architectures.

南京大学.title: Token-Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning
南京大学.authors_text: Tingxu Han, Zhenting Wang, Chunrong Fang, Shiyu Zhao, Shiqing Ma
南京大学.summary: The paper presents a token-budget-aware framework for LLM reasoning that optimizes token usage, reducing costs while maintaining performance through dynamic adjustment based on problem complexity.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Reasoning is critical for large language models (LLMs) to excel in a wide range of tasks. While methods like Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning and enhance LLM performance by decomposing problems into intermediate steps, they also incur significant overhead in token usage, leading to increased costs. We find that the reasoning process of current LLMs is unnecessarily lengthy and it can be compressed by including a reasonable token budget in the prompt, but the choice of token budget plays a crucial role in the actual compression effectiveness. We then propose a token-budget-aware LLM reasoning framework that dynamically adjusts the number of reasoning tokens based on the reasoning complexity of each problem. Experiments show that our method effectively reduces token costs in CoT reasoning with only a slight performance reduction, offering a practical solution to balance efficiency and accuracy in LLM reasoning. Code: https://github.com/GeniusHTX/TALE

南京大学.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
南京大学.authors_text: Songping Wang, Peiyang Li, Yi Huang, Fengting Li, Xuhao Ran
南京大学.summary: MobileInject is a benchmark for assessing the security of MLLM-based mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks, revealing significant vulnerabilities and reasoning hijacking risks.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based mobile agents are rapidly evolving from conversational assistants into autonomous systems that perceive, reason over, and act on smartphone environments. This capability also exposes a new security risk: adversaries can embed malicious objectives in cross-application mobile content and steer agent behavior through indirect multimodal injection. Although prompt injection has been studied in desktop and web settings, its cross-modal properties in mobile ecosystems remain poorly understood, and existing security analyses are still limited. To close this gap, we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning-to-action security risks. MobileInject provides a high-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances. It further introduces Cross-Modal Consistency Injection to exploit corroboration across modalities, two enhanced attack methods, Multi-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning-Camouflage Injection, to intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine-grained failure analysis. Systematic experiments show that mobile agents are broadly vulnerable to multimodal injection, and that many failures stem from reasoning hijacking at early stages. These findings establish MobileInject as a systematic cross-modal benchmark for studying and improving the security of mobile agents. Code release details are provided in the Appendix Open Science section.

南京大学.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Jin Ye, Yifan Jiang, Lan-zhe Guo
南京大学.summary: SkillBrowser introduces a Meta-Skill-managed framework for agents to selectively access relevant skills on demand, enhancing accuracy while addressing limitations of existing skill exposure methods.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly rely on skills to extend their capabilities in complex tasks. However, scalable skill use requires Selective Skill Exposure (SSE): providing relevant procedural content when needed while avoiding unnecessary exposure that may disrupt reasoning. Existing paradigms fall short in complementary ways. Progressive disclosure exposes metadata for a growing skill library, introducing context pollution; retrieval limits catalog exposure, but static retrieval from the initial task query may be misaligned with capability needs that emerge during reasoning and may still inject unnecessary skills. We propose SkillBrowser, a Meta-Skill-managed framework that enables an agent to identify current capability needs, formulate targeted queries, and selectively load skills on demand. Across six SRA-Bench subsets and five LLMs, SkillBrowser improves aggregate accuracy over static retrieval and LLM-based selection, including multi-step tool use, and mitigates accuracy degradation on already-solvable instances. Benefits remain model- and task-dependent, with under-invocation of useful skills and additional latency as key limitations. These results demonstrate the viability of Meta-Skill-managed SSE for scalable skill repositories.

南京大学.title: Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search-Free Planning in Latent Space
南京大学.authors_text: Guanchen Du, Jinhao Du, Yanpeng Sun, Shan Zhang, Na Zhao
南京大学.summary: The paper introduces Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning (HIJP), a search-free framework that enhances action prediction and goal representation for efficient visual planning in latent space.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Latent world models learn action-conditioned state transitions in a compact representation space, providing a predictive model for visual planning and control. However, planning with these models typically requires costly test-time optimization over action sequences. We propose to replace this online search with a goal-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations. A key challenge is that action prediction alone neither ensures that goal representations encode action-relevant information nor that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent prediction model. We introduce Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning (HIJP), a search-free framework that addresses both aspects during training. HIJP relabels future observations along offline trajectories as goals, providing action supervision across multiple temporal horizons. By retaining gradients through the goal representations, this supervision directly shapes the visual representation. HIJP further feeds predicted actions into the latent predictor model and aligns the resulting next-state representations with encoded successor observations, enforcing action-transition consistency. At inference time, the inverse dynamics model and latent predictor models are applied alternately to generate multi-step action sequences without online search. Across four visual control tasks, HIJP achieves 86.8% overall success and a 1.9-16.5x planning speedup over search-based planning.

南京大学.title: Perceptive Behavior Foundation Model: Adapting Human Motion Priors to Robot-Centric Terrain
南京大学.authors_text: Zifan Wang, Yizhao Li, Teli Ma, Qiang Zhang, Yudong Fan
南京大学.summary: The Perceptive Behavior Foundation Model adapts human motion priors for humanoid robots by integrating terrain awareness, ensuring compatibility with diverse environments through innovative reference synthesis and control techniques.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models aim to acquire reusable whole-body control policies from broad human motion priors, enabling a single controller to produce diverse and expressive behaviors. However, existing motion-centric foundation policies largely assume that the reference motion is already physically compatible with the robot's surroundings. This assumption breaks when the demonstrator, operator, and robot inhabit different environments: a human motion may specify the intended behavior, but not the footholds, clearance, body height, or contact timing required by the robot's local terrain. We introduce \emph{Perceptive Behavior Foundation Model} (Perceptive BFM), a terrain-aware humanoid control framework that grounds human motion priors in robot-centric perception. The model preserves raw kinematic motion references as the behavioral interface, while using local terrain observations to adapt contacts, posture, and timing. To provide scalable terrain supervision, we develop \emph{terrain-conformal reference synthesis} (TCRS), which converts locomotion-oriented human motion clips into terrain-consistent references through contact-aware foothold construction, foot-geometry-aware swing optimization, support-aware root reconstruction, collision repair, and multi-point inverse kinematics. We then train a blind adapted-reference teacher and transfer its terrain-conformal behavior to a deployed raw-reference student through target-frame action alignment. The student is an identity-gated Transformer tracker whose terrain features enter through residual pathways initialized to preserve the motion-tracking prior and trained to produce local corrections only when needed.

南京大学.title: Teach the Magnitude, Not the Direction: Verifier-Anchored Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Multi-Step LLM Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Zechuan Wang, Siyuan Lu, Hongxuan Zhang, Linjian Mo, Chenyi Zhuang
南京大学.summary: The paper presents CrEST, a hierarchical credit assignment framework that enhances reinforcement learning for multi-turn agents by optimizing verified rewards and refining token contributions through self-teaching.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) directly optimizes verifier-defined outcomes for multi-turn tool-use agents, yet its trajectory-level credit assignment conflates heterogeneous per-turn outcomes into a single reward signal. On-policy distillation provides dense per-token supervision but uses a teacher-defined token-level objective and can be prone to gradient concentration collapse. We introduce $\textbf{CrEST}$, a hierarchical credit assignment framework that anchors each sampled token's scalar advantage sign to verified rewards while incorporating dense magnitude signals from a privileged self-teacher. $\textbf{CrEST}$ resolves credit at two levels: turn-segmented verified advantages address inter-turn dilution, while entropy-gated self-teacher modulation refines intra-turn token contributions. Experiments on BFCL V3 and WildToolBench show that $\textbf{CrEST}$ consistently outperforms both RL and distillation baselines across two model scales, with the largest gains on long-trajectory and strict session-level metrics. Our work demonstrates that the teacher's role in policy optimization can be reduced from determining token-level reinforcement or suppression to modulating update magnitudes, enabling dense credit assignment while keeping verifier rewards as the training objective.

南京大学.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
南京大学.authors_text: Xikang Guan, Shaocong Yang, Yanqi Bao, Can Wang, Zheng Gu
南京大学.summary: PhysRepair enhances video generation by diagnosing and selectively repairing physical inconsistencies using causal reasoning and prior repair experiences, improving realism across various physics domains.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.

南京大学.title: LAMP: Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors for Training-Free Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
南京大学.authors_text: Zhipeng Ye, Feng Jiang, Qiufeng Wang, Hao Li
南京大学.summary: LAMP is a training-free framework that enhances few-shot vision-language adaptation by effectively combining global and regional features from multiple encoder layers, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Few-shot adaptation often relies on an encoder's final global representation, leaving complementary information in intermediate layers underused. Combining these features is challenging because their dimensions can differ and their usefulness varies across tasks. We propose LAMP, Layerwise Adaptive Mixing of Predictors, a training-free framework that combines global and regional information from multiple encoder layers. A single forward pass per view supplies all descriptors. Global and support-calibrated regional kernel predictors independently fit the same label residuals. Labeled validation data select their mixture in class-score space, preserving native feature dimensions without learned projections. LAMP-F further adapts text-anchored class prototypes, using a cached response to update the fixed-kernel residual predictions exactly. Experiments cover eleven datasets and ViT and ResNet backbones. LAMP achieves state-of-the-art mean accuracy among the compared published training-free ResNet-50 methods at 4, 8, and 16 shots, reaching 78.73% at 16 shots. Averaged across five support budgets, LAMP improves over a paired global-feature-only baseline by 1.14 and 1.59 percentage points on ViT-B/16 and ResNet-50; LAMP-F raises these gains to 1.96 and 2.54 points. LAMP-F reaches 16-shot accuracies of 83.57% and 79.10%, respectively. Controlled experiments identify multi-layer integration as the main source of improvement and examine pooling, calibration, validation labels, and computational cost. These findings show that combining layer-specific predictions can exploit complementary features from frozen encoders to improve few-shot classification.

南京大学.title: RM-WAM: Reliable Memory-Augmented World Action Models for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
南京大学.authors_text: Cui Miao, Junhao Yu, Ping Liu, Ning Yang, Xuhua Chen
南京大学.summary: RM-WAM enhances long-horizon robotic manipulation by utilizing context-dependent memory to improve decision-making and reduce errors in world action predictions.
南京大学.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) improve robotic manipulation by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, yet most existing methods make decisions primarily from the current observation. This limits their reliability in long-horizon tasks, where visually similar states may correspond to different interaction histories and task stages. Moreover, directly incorporating historical observations can introduce stale, stage-mismatched, or error-contaminated information, leading to inaccurate world prediction and accumulated closed-loop errors. We propose RM-WAM, a reliable memory-augmented World Action Model that treats memory as a context-dependent predictive resource rather than universally useful historical context. RM-WAM represents history using complementary short-term visual state memory and latent event memory, which respectively capture recent interaction dynamics and longer-term state transitions. A counterfactual memory learning scheme varies the accessible history while keeping the current inputs and prediction targets fixed, enabling the model to learn a context-dependent utility estimate for historical memory. Based on this estimate, a utility-aware gating mechanism adaptively controls memory injection into the world-action backbone. Experiments demonstrate that RM-WAM highlights the importance of reliable and selective memory utilization in long-horizon tasks.

南京大学.title: ControlFlow3D: Distilling Multi-View Knowledge into Latent Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling
南京大学.authors_text: Yuang Liu, Zhi Zuo, Zhengkai Zhao, Lirui Zhang, Pan Gao
南京大学.summary: ControlFlow3D enhances point cloud upsampling by distilling multi-view knowledge into a lightweight network, enabling effective performance without requiring multi-view images at test time.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Point cloud upsampling is essential for 3D applications but remains challenging due to sparse, under-constrained observations. Multi-view images can resolve geometric ambiguity, but existing multi-modal methods do not fully exploit visual cues. We propose ControlFlow3D, a framework that distills knowledge from pretrained foundation models into a lightweight generation network during training, enabling strong performance without multi-view images available at test time. Specifically, our method performs conditional flow matching in a structured latent space defined by a frozen 3D encoder. Multi-view image tokens and 3D latent tokens are jointly clustered into shared prototypes via unsupervised soft KMeans; the resulting prototypes guide the flow trajectory through velocity control and are aligned by a consistency loss that progressively transfers image knowledge into the base network. A Mamba-based geometry decoder then maps latent features to dense coordinates with linear complexity. We also construct ShapeNetPU, a 35K-object multi-modal benchmark that is 31 times larger than prior datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and its strong generalization capability.

南京大学.title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu
南京大学.summary: This survey presents a unified framework for analyzing execution provenance and evidence tracing in LLM agents, highlighting gaps in current research and proposing future directions.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are moving beyond text generation to planning, tool use, retrieval, memory access, environmental interaction, and multi-agent collaboration. Because their outputs depend on information and execution steps across an agent run, their execution processes are difficult to verify, debug, and audit. Even a correct final answer does not reveal which evidence supported its claims, whether tool calls were justified, how memory shaped decisions, or where execution failures originated. Relevant research addresses these questions across evidence attribution, tool-use safety, agent memory, and observability, but these areas emphasize different parts of the execution process. This survey brings them into a common framework through execution provenance, a typed graph of an agent run, and evidence tracing, its projection onto evidence-support relations, distinguishing evidence that supports a conclusion from execution that influences it. We introduce a six-dimensional taxonomy covering trace sources, evidence and execution units, provenance relations, tracing granularity and timing, representation forms, and trust functions, complemented by operational definitions of nine provenance relations and two cross-cutting attributes, provenance origin and trace assurance. Applying this framework to the surveyed systems and benchmarks reveals three gaps: limited integration of fine-grained provenance with multiple trust functions, no benchmark in our catalog that evaluates the complete provenance chain, and little reporting of tamper-evident or attested traces. These findings motivate research on unified trace schemas, semantic provenance, memory and multi-agent lineage, provenance-aware safety and recovery, realistic benchmarks, trace assurance, and privacy-aware auditing. Resources are available at https://github.com/xiaoqi-7/Agent-Tracing-Survey.

南京大学.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Bowen Yang, Kaiming Jin, Zichen Ding, Zhenyu Wu, Zehao Li
南京大学.summary: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that integrates GUI interaction and code execution through hybrid training, achieving significant performance improvements in desktop automation tasks.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.

南京大学.title: Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction
南京大学.authors_text: Tianxiang Jiang, Linquan Wu, Sheng Xia, Songze Li, Ziang Yan
南京大学.summary: Future-L1 introduces an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework for video event prediction, enhancing accuracy by preserving visual semantics during autoregressive decoding.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

南京大学.title: TRACE: Typed Reference-Aware Conversational Editing for Humanoid Motion Diffusion
南京大学.authors_text: Zejian Kang, Yifu Luo, Boyang Shen, Jingxuan Li, Zekai Chen
南京大学.summary: TRACE is a framework that enhances humanoid motion generation and editing by using typed kinematic quantities to improve semantic alignment and motion quality through natural language requests.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Language-conditioned humanoid motion generation enables users to create and refine robot movements through natural language. The central challenge is to connect an underspecified request to concrete motion structure that can subsequently be revised relative to an accepted reference. We present TRACE, a generation and editing framework for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot built around typed, measurable kinematic quantities. Our insight is to ground generation conditions in paired training motions and editing goals in the current motion. A language model learns to predict support, root, and hand events from motion-derived supervision; their time-aligned encodings complement the original text in a diffusion generator. Gravity-referenced states and trajectory--contact objectives improve kinematic consistency. For editing, typed requests define body--time scopes and source-relative goals. A separate reference-conditioned diffusion editor uses these goals and revised events to realize changes, while sampling-time projection preserves protected state coordinates. Quantitative evaluation and human assessment show improved semantic alignment and motion quality over the compared methods. Controlled ablations support the value of motion-grounded conditioning and kinematic consistency, while multi-turn editing evaluations demonstrate more reliable execution of successive relative requests under shared preservation constraints. Together, these results support typed kinematic structure as a common basis for motion generation and reference-aware revision.

南京大学.title: ReEnvision: Future-Guided Selective Action Repair for Long-Horizon Manipulation
南京大学.authors_text: Xiyin Zeng, Xuewei Huang, Yi Lu, Weihao Yuan, Hao Wang
南京大学.summary: ReEnvision introduces a future-guided selective action repair framework for long-horizon robotic manipulation, enhancing action success rates by preserving valid actions amid execution deviations.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires robust execution over sequences of interdependent actions. Existing methods typically handle execution deviations by replanning the remaining action chunk or correcting actions step by step as new observations arrive. However, a local deviation may affect only a few actions under distribution shift, yet replanning regenerates the entire chunk from an unfamiliar state, potentially introducing errors into otherwise valid actions. Step-wise correction may react too late, as it does not explicitly anticipate how the deviation affects subsequent actions. We propose ReEnvision, a future-guided selective action repair framework that updates a joint future-action belief using execution feedback. It then learns how the resulting belief revision affects each unexecuted action. The resulting belief revision enables selective repair of only the affected actions within a cached action chunk, preserving valid actions and reserving full replanning for severe deviations. On CALVIN, L-CALVIN, and RLBench, ReEnvision achieves 86.6% 5-step success, improves 10-step success from 56% to 63%, and reaches an average success rate of 88.8%, respectively. On five real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 82.8%. Controlled repair experiments further demonstrate the benefits of localizing affected actions and preserving valid ones during execution.

南京大学.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning
南京大学.authors_text: Yikang Yang, Zhanpeng Hu, Youtian Lin, Mengqi Zhou, Jingxi Xu
南京大学.summary: P3D-Bench introduces a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models in parametric 3D generation, focusing on geometric precision and structural reasoning across various task families.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models can write code to produce complex programs as well as use programs to do 3D modeling, which opens up a new avenue for 3D generation powered by their priors, world knowledge and reasoning. Yet existing benchmarks rarely evaluate 3D modeling through code. Such modeling demands more than runnable code: from a text or visual specification, a model must generate a parametric 3D program that is geometrically precise, semantically aligned and assembly-consistent. We introduce P3D-Bench, a benchmark for parametric 3D generation. Unlike a 3D mesh, a parametric 3D program exposes explicit dimensions, construction operations and part relations, revealing whether a model recovers a design's structure, not just its appearance. Under a unified protocol, P3D-Bench covers three task families (Text-to-3D, Image-to-3D and Assembly-3D) and scores each output for executability, geometric fidelity, topology, text-grounded constraints, multiview semantic alignment and part-level structure. We construct P3D-Dataset, comprising 400 text cases, 400 image cases, and 203 annotated assemblies. Our evaluation on 100 cases from each task family yields three key findings. First, multi-part generation is substantially more challenging than single-part modeling, with models struggling to compose individual parts into a coherent structure. Second, models can often recover the global shape and semantic identity of the target object, yet fail to reproduce the precise parametric geometry specified by the input. Third, part-level modeling remains weak on assemblies, where models recover neither the geometry of each part nor the right number of parts. These results position P3D-Bench as a benchmark for evaluating precise parametric geometry and part-level structure in parametric 3D generation.

南京大学.title: Harness Policy Distillation: Aligning Agent Policies with Runtime Semantics
南京大学.authors_text: Junze Zhu, Weihao Chen, Zhiyang Zhou, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai
南京大学.summary: Harness Policy Distillation (HPD) aligns agent policies with runtime semantics by explicitly training on control documents, significantly improving task success and compliance in deployment.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Deploying a general-purpose model as an agent means running it inside a product-specific runtime harness that decides which actions are executable, how state advances, and when the loop may terminate. Ordinary trajectory supervision shows which action was taken but leaves the runtime semantics behind that action implicit. We introduce Harness Policy Distillation (HPD), which makes these runtime control semantics an explicit training target alongside actions to align the harness policy. HPD replays reference trajectories through the harness to recover the runtime semantics that are implicit in ordinary trajectory data, and represents them as control documents at each model-call boundary. These documents provide privileged information for a teacher to generate actions, while harness verification ensures that the resulting targets are executable under the runtime contract. We jointly train a shared model on the runtime semantics recovered from control-state privileged information and native history, thereby internalizing these semantics into the model policy. At deployment, the trained model uses the original harness interface without requiring the control document or any additional supplement. On TRAJECT-Bench with the Pi harness, Qwen3-8B trained with HPD reaches 22.98% autonomous task success and 49.23% runtime compliance, against 3.09% and 19.90% for the unadapted model. Harness-verified teacher actions substantially improve the native deployment policy, while joint control-state supervision provides further gains in task completion and runtime compliance. HPD turns executable runtime semantics into dense supervision for learning harness-compatible actions at each decision boundary.

南京大学.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion
南京大学.authors_text: Yu He, Weikai Yang
南京大学.summary: SkillCommit is an online framework that evolves agent skills by preserving instance-specific experiences and hierarchically abstracting behaviorally validated strategies to enhance performance.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can continually improve without parameter updates by converting historical experience into reusable procedural knowledge. However, existing methods often consolidate experience based on semantic similarity or LLM judgments, which may merge superficially related but behaviorally incompatible strategies and thereby degrade performance. To address the issue, we propose SkillCommit, an online skill evolution framework that continuously transforms experience into a hierarchical library of reusable skills. Rather than generalizing from individual experiences immediately, SkillCommit first preserves each experience as an instance-specific patch, retaining its locally validated behavior. As patches accumulate, SkillCommit abstracts those sharing a common behavioral mechanism into higher-level skills. Specifically, for each incoming skill, embedding-based retrieval first identifies candidate related skills. Cross-instance replay and an LLM-based mechanism check determine whether these skills transfer across cases and share a common underlying mechanism. Candidates that pass both checks are abstracted into a higher-level skill and committed only if it preserves the validated behavior of all constituent skills. Experiments on RuleArena, OpenExempt and KOR-Bench demonstrate that SkillCommit consistently improves agent performance across diverse domains. Moreover, the learned skills transfer across model scales and families, enabling cross-model experience transfer.

南京大学.title: SEDM: Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Yichen Liu, Anna Min, Yinzhi Wang, Yuhang Yao, Yichen Han
南京大学.summary: SEDM introduces a selective memory framework for agents that optimizes memory sharing and usage, significantly enhancing task success while reducing processing costs.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Agents in a society can reuse each other's experience, but indiscriminate memory use increases processing cost and can reduce task success. We present SEDM (Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory), a framework that selects both what agents share and when recipients use it. On the sender side, SEDM admits memories through paired execution tests, ranks them by relevance and measured utility, and abstracts them for cross-domain reuse. On the recipient side, Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG) predicts success with and without memory in a single forward pass, learning from paired outcomes including ties. It injects memory only when the calibrated success gain outweighs a context-cost penalty. SEDM exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1 points and outperforms G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens. In a controlled HotpotQA study, CMG achieves success comparable to always using memory with 18% fewer agent input tokens. Within the full SEDM pipeline on LoCoMo, CMG outperforms both always-use and no-memory policies for two SEDM memories while using 19-31% fewer input tokens than always-use. These results show that selective use can recover value from shared memories that hurt performance when injected indiscriminately.

南京大学.title: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation
南京大学.authors_text: Shaocheng Liu, Yuan Meng, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll
南京大学.summary: The paper introduces PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that effectively adapts predictive dynamics for unified robotic manipulation across diverse embodiments, achieving superior performance in real-time tasks.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. Collective learning aggregates multi-robot experience to discover shared task structure, yet naive aggregation can average incompatible action modes when different embodiments realize the same Cartesian command through different transition behavior. This leads to strategy ambiguity and performance collapse on dynamically outlying embodiments. To address this, we propose PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. The first stage employs a representation layer pre-trained on offline trajectories to extract task-level context from collective data. The second stage introduces a decision layer equipped with a predictive dynamics adapter. By forcing the latent state to predict future transitions, this adapter acts as a latent regularizer that grounds the policy in the transition behavior of the executing robot while preserving real-time inference without online planning. Evaluations across simulated embodiments demonstrate that our method prevents performance collapse on distinct robots. It achieves over 93\% overall success and 89\% on dynamically out-of-distribution zero-shot simulated robots, outperforming the Transformer behavior cloning (82\%) and diffusion policy baselines (66\%). Physical KUKA deployment further validates the feasibility of the full state-based pipeline under zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

南京大学.title: Frame Evidence:A Benchmark for Reference Frames and Visual Evidence in Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning
南京大学.authors_text: Chunxi Luo, Qishuai Ding, Xingchen Peng, Hengwei Ye, Ke Zhang
南京大学.summary: The Frame Evidence benchmark evaluates spatial reasoning accuracy across varying reference frames and visual evidence, revealing challenges in maintaining correctness amid changes in input conditions.
南京大学.debug_abstract: A spatial answer depends on the reference frame specified in language and its supporting visual evidence. Item accuracy alone obscures whether correctness persists when either changes. We introduce Frame Evidence, a benchmark of 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions from captured and rendered scenes. One family compares three grounded reference frames over fixed images. The other pairs image deletion annotated as insufficient with answer-preserving addition. Joint metrics require correct answers across all three frames and paired evidence variants. Across 20 configurations on 288 held-out questions, GPT three-shot reaches 50.00\% item accuracy, but the best three-frame group accuracy is 5/48 (10.42\%), reached by GPT two-shot. Few-shot prompting and task-specific adaptation improve item accuracy without consistently improving joint correctness. Input controls show where images support matched success, while repeated executions reveal answer instability beneath similar scores.

南京大学.title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
南京大学.authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Tong Lei, Dahan Wang, Peter Bell
南京大学.summary: This paper explores how different textual interface designs impact prompt optimization for audio-visual question answering in multimodal reasoning systems, revealing trade-offs in interpretability and optimization difficulty.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) has shown strong effectiveness for text-based LLMs and LLM systems, but its application to audio-visual understanding systems requires suitable textual interfaces through which multimodal reasoning can be exposed to text-based optimizers. We investigate how the design of textual interfaces affects prompt optimization for multimodal reasoning, on the audio-visual question answering task. We compare three interface designs, including a direct inference system consisting of a single omni-modal large language model (OmniLLM), a captioner-reasoner system, and an agentic architecture in which a primary agent orchestrates subagent OmniLLMs. Experiments with Qwen3-Omni and Gemini show that direct prompt optimization provides model-dependent gains; the captioner-reasoner system and the agentic system expose more interpretable optimization interfaces but are harder to optimize, where error analysis of cases affected by optimization is conducted. Our study highlights textual interface design as an important factor in making prompt optimization effective for omni-modal reasoning systems. Our implementation details are specified in GitHub repo.

南京大学.title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation
南京大学.authors_text: Hongyu Ding, Kanyu Xu, Mingjia Chen, Zixuan Chen, Jieqi Shi
南京大学.summary: HM3D-M3 introduces a comprehensive benchmark for multi-agent, multi-modal, multi-object goal navigation, featuring diverse goals and performance metrics across 1,000 validation episodes.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Rapid progress in AI agents and robotics makes it a matter of the near future that humans are served by a team of robots. Such a team will receive several goals at once, each specified in whatever form is convenient for the human, such as a category name, a photo, or a spoken description. Existing benchmarks study multi-agent, multi-modal, and multi-object goal navigation in isolation, and a benchmark that places all three in one episode is missing. To fill this gap, we introduce HM3D-M3. A team of K agents starts at distributed locations in a photorealistic indoor scene and searches for an unordered set of M object goals, each given as an open-vocabulary category, an instance image, or an instance description. HM3D-M3 provides 1,000 validation episodes over 3,926 goals from 379 open-vocabulary categories, 100K observation-assignment training samples, and two team-level metrics, goal-level SR and makespan-normalized SPL. We further contribute two baselines. HiGA is a trained hierarchical goal assigner on top of a frozen open-vocabulary navigation policy, and LaViRA-M3 is a training-free team of VLM agents with shared mapping and progress analysis. Adapted multi-robot and zero-shot methods reach 16--27% SR, while our baselines reach 38--41% with complementary strengths and distinct failure modes. Furthermore, we deploy LaViRA-M3 on a heterogeneous three-robot team. Project page: https://robo-lavira.github.io/hm3d-m3/

南京大学.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
南京大学.authors_text: Fucai Zhu, Xidong Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Yipan Wang, Fubo Wang
南京大学.summary: TacClaw-Infinity is a comprehensive VTLA dataset for dexterous manipulation, featuring over 10,000 hours of diverse, high-quality, structured tactile and visual data from various environments.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

南京大学.title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
南京大学.authors_text: Yuchen Ling, Shengcheng Yu, Zhenyu Chen, Chunrong Fang
南京大学.summary: The study evaluates Jev's impact on decision-making efficiency in AI agents, revealing mixed effects on task success and resource use across different workflows.
南京大学.debug_abstract: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost. However, it remains unclear whether such local savings can be translated into efficient and reliable task completion. In this paper, we investigate this efficiency transfer across five agents in two representative application settings, embodied tasks in ALFWorld and mobile app use in AndroidWorld. Across 4,500 task executions, we jointly evaluate task effectiveness, decision-level and task-level resource use, and execution behavior. Experimental results show that Jev integration substantially reduces decision cost and latency across all five agents, with task-level gains varying by workflow. Task success remains close to baseline levels on ALFWorld and declines more substantially in two mobile agents. Auxiliary reasoning and additional interactions absorb decision savings, while failed recovery and premature completion limit successful delivery. Mean cost per successful outcome increases in one agent even as spending per attempt falls. These findings highlight the importance of preserving progress, supporting recovery, and verifying completion when integrating efficient decision models into agent workflows. Their practical value should be assessed through successful task delivery, recovery behavior, and resources per delivered outcome.

南京大学.title: CoRE-VLA: Towards Scalable and Robust Vision-Language-Action Modeling via Conditional Routing of Experts
南京大学.authors_text: Haozhe Zhang, Sixian Li, Yifei Zhang, Zezheng Huai, Hao Chen
南京大学.summary: CoRE-VLA introduces a robust vision-language-action framework that utilizes context-conditioned sparse computation for adaptable action generation under varying sensor availability, enhancing multi-task performance and zero-shot generalization.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced generalist robotic manipulation, yet real-world deployment reveals a fundamental challenge: robots are equipped with diverse and heterogeneous sensor configurations, auxiliary sensors can fail unexpectedly during operation, and different robot embodiments often lack certain sensors by design. A unified policy that can exploit auxiliary perceptual inputs when available while remaining reliable under sensor absence, whether incidental or by design, is therefore essential for practical deployment. However, existing VLA policies couple action generation to a fixed sensor set through shared dense computation, making them brittle when sensors are missing and limiting their ability to specialize across diverse tasks and long-horizon behaviors. We propose CoRE-VLA, a scalable and robust VLA framework that formulates action generation as context-conditioned sparse computation. Sensor availability gates modality-specialized experts, enabling graceful degradation under missing sensors without retraining. Task intent further routes action-side representations to task-relevant experts, improving specialization across diverse tasks and long-horizon subgoals. While the framework is designed to accommodate different auxiliary sensors, we focus on depth as a representative and practically important auxiliary modality in our experiments. Experiments on LIBERO, RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop, and real-world dual-arm manipulation show that CoRE-VLA achieves strong results on long-horizon and multi-task benchmarks, and outperforms both a dense-action-generator ablation and a strong pretrained VLA baseline, including in zero-shot generalization to unseen scenarios. Modality analysis shows that CoRE-VLA can exploit auxiliary depth when available while remaining robust when depth is unavailable during deployment.

南京大学.title: 3DTexMOR: 3D Gaussian Multi-Object Removal via Texture-Space Inpainting
南京大学.authors_text: Kunxin Guang, Yonghao Zhao, Jian Yang, Beibei Wang
南京大学.summary: The paper presents 3DTexMOR, a method for 3D multi-object removal that utilizes texture-space inpainting for improved appearance consistency and geometry recovery across views.
南京大学.debug_abstract: 3D object removal aims to remove target objects from reconstructed scenes and complete the geometry and appearance of occluded regions. Existing NeRF- and 3DGS-based methods typically inpaint 2D images to guide 3D completion. However, complex multi-object layouts limit the surrounding context visible in each view, making 2D inpainting prone to artifacts. Inconsistent completions across views also introduce conflicting supervision and blurry reconstructions. We propose 3D Gaussian Multi-Object Removal via Texture-Space Inpainting (3DTexMOR). Our key idea is to perform inpainting in a unified texture space shared by all views. By combining complementary observations, this space provides richer context for recovering missing regions and promotes cross-view appearance consistency. We aggregate multi-view observations into texture maps, inpaint the missing regions, and reproject the completed maps into camera views to supervise Gaussian scene completion. To avoid the influence of view-dependent highlights and reflections, we decompose appearance and aggregate view-independent intrinsic attributes instead of RGB colors. We further introduce geometrically regularized Gaussian completion to constrain the geometry of the completed regions. Extensive experiments demonstrate visually plausible completions and state-of-the-art multi-object removal performance, improving PSNR by 5.8 dB and reducing LPIPS by at least 22% compared with existing methods.

南京大学.title: TaReD: Tool-Aware Recursive Decomposition for Long-Horizon Tasks
南京大学.authors_text: Wei-Xiang Mao, Zhi-Kai Chen, De-Chuan Zhan, Han-Jia Ye
南京大学.summary: TaReD enhances long-horizon task execution by recursively decomposing complex tasks into manageable subtasks, leveraging a hierarchical tool organization to improve success rates significantly.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Agents combine reasoning with tools to interact with external systems and complete real-world tasks. Early agents typically interleave reasoning and actions along a single execution chain. On complex tasks, this chain becomes unreliable because growing histories obscure intermediate dependencies and allow early planning errors to propagate. Recursively decomposing a complex task into smaller subtasks offers a natural solution, yet effective decomposition must account for the system's capabilities so that each subtask can be executed by the available tools. In realistic systems, however, tool libraries can be too large to expose in full. Injecting every tool description consumes substantial context while making relevant tools harder to retrieve and useful task boundaries harder to identify. We propose tool-aware recursive decomposition, which organizes tools by functional relationships into a hierarchy of capabilities. During execution, the agent discovers tools on demand and uses the hierarchy to recursively decompose a complex task into a subtask tree whose levels are aligned with the capabilities required at each stage. Experiments on complex real-world tasks show that the proposed method improves end-to-end task success rate by up to 40 percentage points over the compared baselines. The implementation of TaReD is available on GitHub: https://github.com/WeiXiang-Mao/TaReD.

南京大学.title: Point-Focused Attention Meets Context-Scan State Space: Robust Biological Visual Perception for Point Cloud Representation
南京大学.authors_text: Kanglin Qu, Pan Gao, Qun Dai, Yuanhao Sun
南京大学.summary: PointLearner enhances point cloud representation learning by integrating foveation-inspired point-focused attention and context-scan state space, achieving state-of-the-art robustness and performance.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Synergistically capturing intricate local structures and global contextual dependencies has become a critical challenge in point cloud representation learning. To address this, we introduce PointLearner, a point cloud representation learning network that closely aligns with biological vision which employs an active, foveation-inspired processing strategy, thus enabling local geometric modeling and long-range dependency interactions simultaneously. Specifically, we first design a point-focused attention, which simulates foveal vision at the visual focus through a competitive normalized attention mechanism between local neighbors and spatially downsampled features. The spatially downsampled features are extracted by a pooling method based on learnable inducing points, which can flexibly adapt to the non-uniform distribution of point clouds as the number of inducing points is controlled and they interact directly with point clouds. Second, we propose a context-scan state space that mimics eye's saccade inference, which infers the overall semantic structure and spatial content in the scene through a scan path guided by the Hilbert curve for the bidirectional S6. With this focus-then-context biomimetic design, PointLearner demonstrates remarkable robustness and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple point cloud tasks.

南京大学.title: Experience-Guided Initiation Search for Learned Skills in Skill Composition
南京大学.authors_text: Qixuan Li, Yanhong Zhao, Jincheng Yu
南京大学.summary: The paper introduces EVIS, a framework that optimizes initiation configurations for learned skills in new environments by leveraging historical experience and behavioral validation, reducing deployment costs.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Deploying frozen learned skills, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, in new environments requires identifying initiation configurations that support reliable execution. In skill composition, an initiation configuration affects not only the current skill but also the physical state passed to subsequent skills, so successful execution of an individual skill does not necessarily imply successful completion of the composed task. Estimating target-specific capability through extensive rollouts is costly in real-world deployment, while directly reusing historical experience can be unreliable under environment changes. We propose EVIS, an Experience-Guided and Behavior-Validated Initiation Search framework for discovering reliable initiation configurations under limited target interaction. EVIS uses historical execution experience to prioritize promising candidates and target-environment behavior to validate whether they remain effective. We evaluate EVIS on single-skill and two-stage manipulation tasks with frozen VLA policies. EVIS reduces mean target-environment queries and improves reliable candidate discovery under small interaction budgets. These results show that combining historical guidance with target-side behavioral validation can reduce the interaction cost of deploying frozen learned skills in new environments.

南京大学.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
南京大学.authors_text: Yi Ma, Tianpei Yang, Yaodong Yang, Weixun Wang, Hongyao Tang
南京大学.summary: This paper demonstrates that Jev, a decision model, enhances reinforcement learning performance and sample efficiency by serving as a reference policy, exploration judge, and replay rater.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Foundation models supply reinforcement learning (RL) with priors that mitigate its longstanding weaknesses in sample efficiency and transfer, but their token-by-token generation makes queries sequential and costly. Jev, a recently released decision model, generates nothing and returns calibrated, typed answers in a single forward pass. Existing work studies foundation models in RL either as models to be trained or as generators to be prompted, and Jev belongs to neither category, having so far served only as a black box in single domains. How well such a model decides on its own in RL environments, and how it can improve RL as a component of training, therefore remain unaddressed. To this end, in this paper we first examine the requirements that the objects of an RL system place on the answers they consume, and establish that Jev can fulfill all of them except the cardinal use of a value function. The remaining objects form positions that admit several roles each. We then construct algorithms that employ Jev at three of these positions, as a reference policy, an exploration judge, and a replay rater, to improve sample efficiency, exploration, and learning performance. Across nine MiniGrid tasks and three Atari games, training with Jev outperforms a standard RL learner, including where the learner makes no progress alone, while the model itself remains untrained. To our knowledge, we present the first use of Jev within the RL learning process and establish a frozen decision model as a usable component of RL training, inviting further exploration of how Jev and other advanced decision models can improve RL.

南京大学.title: Trajectory-Guided Fault Localization for Agent Skill Evolution
南京大学.authors_text: Yu Ge, Linna Xie, Zhong Li, Yu Pei, Tian Zhang
南京大学.summary: SkillMorph enhances agent skill evolution by linking execution evidence to specific skill contents, improving accuracy and consistency through trajectory-guided fault localization and targeted revisions.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Agent skills provide reusable guidance for code agents, but incomplete or unsuitable guidance can impair task execution. To reduce the manual effort of skill refinement, recent approaches use LLMs to generate revisions from execution feedback. However, grounding these revisions in explicit behavioral evidence remains challenging. To address this gap, we propose SkillMorph, a skill-evolution approach based on trajectory-guided fault localization in agent skills. Its core idea is to link execution evidence to specific skill contents before generating revisions. Specifically, SkillMorph compares failure and success evidence in abstracted trajectories across repeated runs and tasks, incorporating changes between evolution loops to identify suspicious actions. It then uses these suspicious actions to localize edit sites in the skills and generate corresponding revisions. Experiments on SWE-Skills-Bench and CannBot show that the skills evolved by SkillMorph consistently achieve higher trial-level accuracy and execution consistency than the original skills and those from four existing skill-evolution methods. We have also applied SkillMorph to automated kernel generation with an AI operator-development team, which has accepted 6 skill-revision pull requests.

南京大学.title: ManiUnit: A Manipulation Skill Dataset and Benchmark for Long-Horizon Tasks
南京大学.authors_text: Guoting Wei, Dawei Yan, Xia Yuan, Gengming Zhang, Yelin He
南京大学.summary: ManiUnit introduces a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for evaluating long-horizon mobile manipulation skills, addressing challenges in skill selection and execution consistency.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon mobile manipulation requires a robot to navigate multi-room environments and execute a sequence of manipulation skills under a single natural language instruction. Learning and evaluating these skills present three challenges: similar observations under a fixed task instruction may make skill selection ambiguous; even when a preceding skill succeeds, the robot state inherited by the next skill may deviate from its demonstrated starting states and affect execution; and task-level metrics hinder skill-specific diagnosis, while early failures leave later skills untested. We therefore introduce ManiUnit, a manipulation skill dataset and benchmark built from 50 BEHAVIOR-1K activities. Its dataset contains 137,899 segments across 21 skill types and 417 subtasks, and its benchmark contains 1,260 test instances. Correspondingly, ManiUnit pairs each segment with an explicit subtask instruction; measures sensitivity to perturbations of the robot's starting base position or joint configuration; and restores intermediate simulator states and defines local success conditions so that each skill can be evaluated without executing preceding stages. Evaluations of representative vision-language-action (VLA) policies show that similar aggregate scores can hide substantial per-skill differences. The tested starting-state perturbations also degrade execution: on the full benchmark, joint perturbations reduce success rates by approximately 56% relative to those from demonstrated starting states. On two long-horizon activities, a skill policy trained on ManiUnit segments achieves 78.7% local manipulation success, compared with 49.3% for a task policy trained on complete demonstrations. The trained skills further support complete-task execution on these activities, as coordinating the task and skill policies through a planner raises full-task success from 4.0% to 18.0%.

南京大学.title: Fixed-Reference Pose Residuals for Measuring Cross-Dataset Cue Transfer in Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
南京大学.authors_text: Bowen Yang, Xinliang Xiao, Wenjing Zhang, Li Yang, Wei Zhou
南京大学.summary: The paper investigates a fixed-reference pose residual model for enhancing cross-dataset anticipation in human-robot interactions, revealing significant asymmetries in pose correction effectiveness.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Social and service robots in public spaces need to anticipate which nearby person is about to approach and touch them, so that a response can be prepared before contact. It is largely unknown which cues support this anticipation when a model trained with one robot is used on another robot at a different site. We study this question with a fixed-reference pose residual (FRPR) model: a geometry predictor built from the person's bounding box and mask is trained and frozen, and a temporal network then learns from body pose an additive correction to its logit, so that every prediction splits exactly into a geometry term and a pose term.
