The joint objective enables human demonstrations to supervise contact-aware representation learning, while only robot actions are executed during deployment. In real-robot evaluations across five tasks, our method achieves an average success rate of 70%, outperforming the strongest visual-tactile baseline, which achieves 29%, and an architecture ablation, which achieves 42%. Performance improves consistently with additional human demonstrations and exhibits no saturation at 1,000 demonstrations per task, validating the effectiveness of scalable human tactile data for dexterous manipulation. Project page is available at https://uni-vta.github.io/.

赵波老师实验室.title: LeRF: Learning Reference Coordinate Frames for Perspective Taking Reasoning
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Bang Xiao, Wenqi Jia, Ozgur Kara, Tiancheng Shen, Yibo Yang
赵波老师实验室.summary: LeRF enhances Vision-Language Models by training them to construct explicit reference frames for improved perspective-taking reasoning in spatial tasks.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Perspective taking is a fundamental component of spatial intelligence, requiring models interpret spatial relations from a specified viewpoint, such as that of another entity or an imagined observer. Despite the increasing spatial reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), they still struggle with perspective taking, often defaulting to the camera viewpoint when a query requires reasoning from a different perspective. We introduce Learning Reference Coordinate Frames for Perspective Taking (LeRF), a framework that trains VLMs to construct and use explicit reference frames for viewpoint-dependent reasoning. Given an image and a query, LeRF decides whether a coordinate frame is necessary. If so, it grounds the reference entity and predicts the frame's origin and entity-centered reference frame. A lightweight renderer overlays the frame onto the image, enabling subsequent reasoning over these visual cues without external perception models or explicit 3D reconstruction. To learn this process, we first perform supervised fine-tuning to teach selective tool invocation and reference coordinate frame prediction, followed by reinforcement learning on spatial VQA pairs to improve frame-guided reasoning. Across diverse perspective-taking benchmarks, LeRF consistently improves over its backbone and achieves strong performance against existing open-source methods. Further evaluations also show improved reference-frame grounding and orientation estimation, supporting the effectiveness of learned reference frames for viewpoint-dependent reasoning.

赵波老师实验室.title: Visual sensitivity is not claim retractability: persistence-aware credit assignment for multimodal reinforcement learning
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Zhongan Bi, Kepeng Lin, Xuanang Gao, Yuhan Sun, Lianrun Zhang
赵波老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces Persistence-Aware Credit Gating (PACG) to enhance claim retractability in multimodal reinforcement learning by decoupling visual sensitivity from persistent unsupported claims.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has been extended to Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), and perception-aware methods further encourage policies to rely on visual evidence. Yet relying on the image does not guarantee that visual claims are supported by it. Before RL training, 27.81% of the correctly answered responses of Qwen2.5-VL-7B on four multimodal reasoning benchmarks contain at least one direct visual claim that the image does not support. Since outcome-level RL rewards each response as a whole, these claims inherit the positive credit of the correct answer. We introduce a fixed-rollout counterfactual diagnostic that re-scores the same response under an intervened image to separate Evidence-Function Sensitivity (EFS), how strongly the model's predictions change, from claim persistence, whether the model keeps supporting the same claim rather than retracting it. The diagnostic reveals Sensitivity-Persistence Decoupling (SPD): under DAPO and VPPO, EFS increases and claims become more retractable overall, yet unsupported claims become significantly more persistent, whereas GRPO raises EFS without this deterioration. We therefore propose Persistence-Aware Credit Gating (PACG), which attenuates positive credit for unusually persistent visual claims and leaves all other credit unchanged. It requires no supported/unsupported labels and adds no inference cost. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, PACG raises the nine-benchmark average over three seeds from 58.1% to 59.9% with DAPO and from 59.8% to 60.9% with VPPO, while making unsupported claims more retractable. The gains extend to a larger model, a newer backbone, and the accuracy of HallusionBench also improves consistently. These results suggest that visual sensitivity and claim retractability are complementary dimensions of multimodal credit assignment.

赵波老师实验室.title: Inducing Process Supervision from Outcome-Only Reinforcement Learning
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Shengda Fan, Xin Cong, Zhong Zhang, Haotian Chen, Yankai Lin
赵波老师实验室.summary: The paper presents TIPS, an outcome-only RL framework that effectively trains process reward models by leveraging chain-of-thought reasoning to optimize step-level verification without explicit supervision.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Process reward models (PRMs) have become a key component for LLMs, as their step-level feedback supports both post-training and test-time reasoning. However, training strong PRMs remains costly: human step annotation is difficult to scale, while Monte Carlo estimation is computationally expensive and can drift from the intrinsic correctness of steps. To get effective PRMs at low cost, we introduce TIPS (Thinking-Induced Process Supervision), an outcome-only reinforcement learning (RL) framework for training generative PRMs. In TIPS, the model generates a chain-of-thought (CoT) followed by step-level labels and an outcome label. The reward depends solely on whether the predicted outcome matches the ground truth, and the resulting group-relative advantage is used to optimize the entire generated response. Intuitively, when checking intermediate steps helps determine the outcome, more accurate checks can lead to better outcome judgments and higher rewards. Outcome-only RL can therefore reinforce step-level verification without explicit process supervision. We validate the effectiveness of TIPS across math and agent benchmarks and four backbone families. Notably, TIPS-Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 reaches 85.2 F1 on ProcessBench with only 3.2K outcome-labeled trajectories, surpassing all evaluated trained PRMs and strong prompt-only judges such as GPT-5.4-Instruct and Claude-4.7-Opus, while still trailing o1-mini. Code and data are available at https://github.com/RUCBM/TIPS.

赵波老师实验室.title: Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedural Memory for Spatial Intelligence
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Haokai Zhang, Yuhang Ding, Yunshu Zhou, Xinze Du, Shengtao Zhang
赵波老师实验室.summary: The Spatial Memory Agent (SMA) enhances spatial reasoning in frozen VLMs by leveraging experience-grounded memory without parameter updates or external tools, achieving superior accuracy in spatial tasks.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence is becoming a foundation for embodied agents, robotic planning, and multimodal assistants. To improve the spatial reasoning ability of VLMs, existing work has mainly followed two lines. One line uses post-training methods, such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Another line adopts an agentic paradigm in which the model calls external spatial tools to gather intermediate spatial evidence. We study a complementary and underexplored route: Can a frozen VLM agent improve its spatial reasoning through \textbf{parameter-update-free self-evolution}, without depending on external expert spatial tools at inference time? We present \textbf{Spatial Memory Agent (SMA)}, an experience-grounded runtime memory framework that converts verified spatial experience into reusable transferable lessons. Specifically, SMA first queries the frozen VLM in a verifiable spatial environment, obtains a predicted answer and reward, and uses verifier-guided reflection to distill compact transferable lessons stored in memory cards. SMA further assigns each memory card a \textbf{Transfer Reliability Score (TRS)}, which is initialized uniformly and calibrated from later retrieval outcomes as visit evidence of future transfer reliability. During read-only deployment, SMA retrieves memory cards through semantic filtering and combined similarity--TRS ranking, allowing the retrieved memory to guide frozen model inference. Experiments across five representative spatial benchmarks show that SMA achieves the best macro-average accuracy for all four base VLMs and the best accuracy in most individual evaluations, establishing a practical parameter-update-free path for spatial self-evolution through reusable experience.

赵波老师实验室.title: PARSEE-VAD: Efficient Training-Free Online Video Anomaly Detection via Proposition-Aware Reasoning and Streaming Evidence Escalation
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Ji Wang, Shuangqing Zhang, Guo-Sen Xie, Fang Zhao
赵波老师实验室.summary: PARSEE-VAD introduces a training-free framework for online video anomaly detection that efficiently balances current evidence extraction and temporal continuity through structured reasoning and selective computation.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Training-free online video anomaly detection (VAD) with frozen multimodal language models faces two coupled challenges: extracting reliable current-window semantics under causal and computational constraints, and maintaining temporal continuity without repeatedly transmitting high-dimensional history. Encoding history through text can compress visual evidence and introduce semantic bias, whereas retaining visual history expands multimodal context. We introduce PARSEE-VAD, a two-module framework that separates semantic evidence acquisition from score-state evolution. Proposition-Aware Reasoning (PAR) extracts structured propositional evidence from the current causal window and conditionally activates more specific queries when coarse evidence warrants further refinement. By sharing a reusable causal visual prefix across queries, PAR reduces redundant computation through selective execution. Streaming Evidence Escalation (SEE) maps the acquired proposition evidence into a compact score-domain event state through current evidence escalation, then propagates only the resulting bounded state across decisions to support temporal continuity. Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate strong training-free online performance while selective routing reduces specialist computation and score-state propagation remains sparse. These results support a current-first principle for streaming multimodal inference: resolve present semantics first, then use compact historical state only to repair residual continuity gaps.

赵波老师实验室.title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Kerui Ren, Yingxiang Xu, Kaiwen Song, Linning Xu, Bo Dai
赵波老师实验室.summary: Real2Gym transforms real-world video demonstrations into interactive simulation environments, enabling robots to learn and execute manipulation skills effectively in both simulated and physical settings.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world videos provide rich demonstrations of manipulation, but turning them into reusable robot skills requires visually aligned environments, executable physical interactions, and mechanisms for learning from experience. We introduce Real2Gym, an agentic Real2Sim2Real framework that turns human and robot demonstrations into interactive simulation gyms and brings skills acquired in simulation to physical robots. The Real2Sim module reconstructs editable scenes, aligns objects and cameras with the input, validates demonstrated or retargeted actions through native physics execution, and generates task-conditioned variations with action-feasibility checks. Within these environments, the agent generates executable code for manipulation stages, observes their outcomes, and distills successful attempts and failures into reusable task procedures, object-relative motions, and recovery strategies. Through a shared perception-and-control interface, these skills guide subsequent execution in simulation and on real robots, with motions adapted to current observations and no updates to the underlying model weights. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Real2Gym enables high-fidelity simulation environment reconstruction, outperforming GPT-6 Astra Direct Mode by 16.7% in success rate with approximately 74.9% fewer policy-execution tokens across these environments, while exceeding it by 33.3% in physical robot execution success rate across four tasks on a real Franka robot.

赵波老师实验室.title: V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Yang Zhang, Jiangyuan Zhao, Chenyou Fan, Jiayu Hu, Xiu Yuan
赵波老师实验室.summary: The V-JEPA Policy framework leverages predictive visual latents from a frozen encoder to effectively build world-action models, outperforming traditional methods in various benchmarks.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple future visual-state prediction with action generation. By adapting video generators or image-editing models pretrained at scale, a prominent line of recent WAMs inherits both predictive knowledge and the models in which it was learned. We ask whether a predictive visual latent space induced by large-scale predictive pretraining can instead provide a sufficient foundation for effective WAM learning without inheriting a complete pretrained visual generative model. To answer this question, we introduce V-JEPA Policy, a simple framework that builds a WAM on the latent space of a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. An instruction-conditioned future-latent predictor and a flow-matching action expert are jointly learned from scratch in a single downstream stage, with the predictor's future-informed context key--value states conditioning action generation. With 0.9B total parameters, of which 0.6B are trainable, V-JEPA Policy achieves competitive performance with representative WAM and vision-language-action baselines across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa-GR1. Comparing visual foundations under the same downstream framework and training budget identifies V-JEPA latents as more effective than the discriminative, reconstructive, and video-understanding-oriented alternatives, particularly under distribution shifts. Beyond task-specific learning, pretraining the predictor on DROID video--instruction pairs without action labels and adapting it into a WAM yields substantial gains in downstream control and out-of-distribution generalization. Together, these findings establish predictive visual latents as a foundation for effective WAM learning from task-specific demonstrations and for transferring future-modeling knowledge acquired from broader in-the-wild videos. Our code is available at https://github.com/breez3young/VJEPA-Policy.

赵波老师实验室.title: Beyond a single latent space: a dual-latent world model for long-horizon planning
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Delin Zhao, Zhengrong Yue, Shaobin Zhuang, Junlin He, Xiaoyu Chen
赵波老师实验室.summary: The Dual-Latent World Model enhances long-horizon planning by utilizing distinct low-level and high-level state representations, improving goal discrimination and execution accuracy.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Latent world models often struggle with long-horizon planning despite accurate short-term predictions. Recursive rollouts accumulate errors, while distance concentration in high-dimensional latent spaces can weaken goal discrimination. We introduce the Dual-Latent World Model (Dual-WM), which separates local execution and long-range planning through distinct state representations and dynamics models. The low-level model predicts action-conditioned transitions, while the high-level model uses learned macro-actions to plan over longer temporal spans. We also propose Long-Horizon Representation Learning with Weighted Rollout (LoRe), which supervises self-generated predictions at both levels. An analysis of recursive error propagation motivates exponential horizon weights with separate decay rates for the two temporal scales. During planning, the high-level model generates latent subgoals that the low-level model refines into actions for precise execution. We evaluate from-scratch Dual-WM on five goal-conditioned visual control tasks against the task-wise strongest baselines without actor-guided proposals. At goal offsets of 50 and 100 environment steps, mean success increases from 75.9% to 84.4% and from 61.4% to 69.5%, respectively. At offset 100, Dual-WM outperforms these baselines on all five tasks and improves mean success over LeWM by 30.8 percentage points. Ablations and supporting analyses provide evidence of more informative representations for goal evaluation and greater consistency under recursive prediction. These results highlight the value of separating temporal roles and training across multiple horizons for reliable latent planning. Our core implementation is available at https://github.com/DeLin1001/Dual-WM-Official.

赵波老师实验室.title: Exemplar2VQA: A Scalable Exemplar-Driven Visual Question Answering Generation Framework via Multi-Agent Coding
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Jiayu Ying, Qijian Tian, Ruijie Xu, Xinnan Zhu, Daoguo Dong
赵波老师实验室.summary: Exemplar2VQA is a scalable framework that generates high-fidelity spatial question-answer pairs using multi-agent coding, enhancing performance in visual question answering across diverse benchmarks.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Advancing spatial intelligence in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is bottlenecked by the scarcity of complex, scalable 3D question-answer (QA) data. While manual annotation is labor-intensive, directly utilizing LLMs to synthesize these QA pairs often fails due to their inherent deficiencies in spatial and geometric computation. We introduce Exemplar2VQA, a scalable exemplar-driven visual question answering generation framework that rapidly synthesizes large-scale spatial QA pairs in simulated environments via multi-agent coding. By equipping collaborative agents with a meticulously designed library of geometric utilities, Exemplar2VQA bypasses LLMs' spatial reasoning flaws through deterministic code execution. Crucially, the framework exhibits remarkable versatility: taking diverse static object-centric spatial query templates as exemplars, it seamlessly and autonomously scales them into massive, high-fidelity synthetic datasets. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL (3B/7B) exclusively on Exemplar2VQA-generated synthetic indoor data yields significant performance improvements across various diverse benchmarks. Furthermore, its effectiveness is not limited to in-domain indoor datasets but also robustly extends to outdoor and mixed-scene benchmarks. These results establish Exemplar2VQA as a scalable and powerful paradigm for bridging the sim-to-real gap in Embodied AI. Our code is at https://github.com/yingjiayu12/Exemplar2VQA

赵波老师实验室.title: Faster and Better? Benchmark Bugs and Design Limitations Distort the Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Acceleration
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Qiwei Chen, Kaijun Zhou, Nuohui Shi, Zhiyang Li, Yuxuan Feng
赵波老师实验室.summary: The paper reveals that benchmark flaws distort the evaluation of vision-language-action acceleration methods, necessitating bug fixes and design revisions for reliable performance assessment.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks are the standard tool for evaluating vision-language-action (VLA) policies and the acceleration methods that reduce their inference latency for on-robot deployment. On these benchmarks, we observe that some training-free acceleration methods, which approximate the baseline policy's computation, achieve higher measured success rates than the baseline itself. Success rates alone cannot establish whether such gains come from better task execution or from evaluation flaws. We therefore investigate two kinds of benchmark flaws behind these gains: bugs, where the implementation does not match the intended task or evaluation protocol, and design limitations, where success criteria and simulation settings do not fully capture how acceleration affects task execution. Starting from tasks with anomalous gains, we localize root causes by plotting object trajectories against checker acceptance regions, and classify the resulting bugs into task consistency, initialization, and reproducibility. Extending this audit to seven benchmarks, including RoboTwin, LIBERO-Plus, and VLABench, we identify 22 bugs of these types and 4 design limitations. For the latter, we revise permissive success checkers, correct unrealistic object masses, and add a motion-aware score that favors smoother actions. Experiments show that bug fixes can reverse method rankings, moving the baseline from last to first on one task. Addressing design limitations can likewise remove anomalous gains: on another task, the baseline moves from 21 percentage points behind an accelerated method to 5 points ahead. Gains attributed to acceleration can therefore be artifacts of the benchmark rather than better task execution. We release our bug fixes and revised benchmark settings to support trustworthy evaluation of VLA acceleration.

赵波老师实验室.title: RoboChrono: A Real Robot Benchmark for Streaming Task Understanding
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Yuzhou Wu, Longteng Fan, Zimeng Li, Yu Wanchan, Ting Zhang
赵波老师实验室.summary: RoboChrono is a benchmark for streaming task understanding in robot manipulation, revealing significant performance disparities among vision-language models across various tasks and emphasizing the importance of capability-specific evaluations.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Understanding ongoing robot manipulation requires models to interpret visual observations in relation to interaction history and task progress. We introduce RoboChrono, a benchmark for streaming task understanding comprising 39 scenarios and 34,713 evaluation instances, constructed from real robot executions and complementary bare-hand human recordings. The benchmark evaluates seven tasks grouped into recognition, alignment, and temporal grounding, covering action understanding and anticipation, visual correspondence, temporal ordering, and action localization. Zero-shot evaluation of 18 vision-language models reveals substantial differences across tasks. GPT-6-Astra achieves 98.3% accuracy on Frame Matching but 68.3% on Frame Ordering, while RynnBrain1.1-122B-A10B exhibits a larger gap, reaching 95.4% and 32.9%, respectively. Input ablations on matched questions with five open-weight models further reveal distinct dependencies on visual evidence: removing visual observations reduces Current Action Recognition accuracy by 22.1 percentage points, whereas Next Action Prediction decreases by only 0.7 points. These findings show that strong visual matching does not consistently coincide with strong temporal ordering, and suggest that next-action prediction can be supported by task and action priors even when visual evidence is unavailable. RoboChrono provides a diagnostic setting for examining these differences, highlighting the need for capability-specific evaluation beyond aggregate scores when assessing task understanding in robot manipulation.

赵波老师实验室.title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Ganlin Yang, Zhangzheng Tu, Yuqiang Yang, Sitong Mao, Junyi Dong
赵波老师实验室.summary: EventVLA introduces a sparse visual evidence memory framework that enhances long-horizon VLA policies by dynamically capturing task-critical visual events, improving success rates by 40%.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Memory remains a critical bottleneck for long-horizon robotic manipulation, as standard Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often fail when task-relevant cues become occluded or unobservable over time. While existing memory-augmented methods utilize historical context, they either suffer from severe information bottlenecks, incur high latency via decoupled dual systems, or rely on unselective buffers that accumulate massive visual redundancies. To address these limitations, we introduce EventVLA, an end-to-end framework founded on the concept of sparse visual evidence memory that comprises two core components: foundational visual anchors to retain initial and short-term contexts, and a dynamic Keyframe Evidence Memory (KEM) module. Specifically, KEM directly predicts future keyframe probabilities from the VLA's latent embeddings to autonomously capture and store sparse, task-critical visual events. This foresight-driven mechanism empowers the policy to dynamically evaluate the future causal utility of current observations, preserving transient visual evidence before it becomes unobservable. Furthermore, we propose RoboTwin-MeM, a diagnostic benchmark specifically designed to evaluate non-Markovian manipulation tasks with interactive visual evidence. Extensive evaluations show that across 17 memory-requiring simulation tasks and 4 real-world bimanual tasks, EventVLA achieves an average success rate improvement of +40% over state-of-the-art memory-augmented VLAs.

赵波老师实验室.title: GeoVerse: World-Consistent Novel View Synthesis in Geometric Latent Space
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Kerui Ren, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Changjian Jiang, Mu Huang
赵波老师实验室.summary: GeoVerse synthesizes world-consistent novel views by integrating geometric latent space with video generative appearance priors, enhancing visual quality and geometric consistency.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis from sparse images must reconcile faithful reconstruction of observed regions with plausible completion of unseen content, while maintaining world consistency across viewpoints. Existing geometry-based methods preserve observed scene structure but often struggle to complete unseen regions, whereas video generative models offer rich appearance priors but accumulate inconsistencies during sequential view generation. We propose GeoVerse, a framework that synthesizes world-consistent novel views by performing generation within the geometric latent space of a pretrained 3D foundation model and injecting appearance priors from a video generative model. Specifically, GeoVerse extracts multilevel features from Wan2.2 VACE and injects them into the geometric latent diffusion model via a ControlNet-style adapter, incorporating video-learned appearance priors to enhance structural completion. To enforce cross-view coherence, a global spatial memory continuously aggregates observed and synthesized content, reprojecting target-aligned guidance to anchor subsequent predictions to a shared scene representation. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate improved visual quality and geometric consistency, with a 2.23 dB higher PSNR on DL3DV and 32.4% lower ATE on Mip-NeRF360 compared to GLD.

赵波老师实验室.title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Jiexing Qi, Yu He, Jun Liu, Qichen Huang, Shaohua Hu
赵波老师实验室.summary: VACE enhances language model agents through validation-gated co-evolution of model weights and harnesses, achieving superior performance on OfficeQA and AutomationBench compared to traditional methods.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Language model agents can be improved by updating their model weights or refining the harness that guides task execution. These components are coupled: weight updates change how the model uses the harness, while harness updates change the trajectories used for training. We propose VACE, Validation-Gated Alternating CoEvolution, which alternates agentic reinforcement learning with trajectory-driven harness refinement. After each RL stage, VACE reuses the collected trajectories to propose a harness revision and evaluates the incumbent and candidate with the updated model held fixed. The candidate guides subsequent training only if it improves validation performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, VACE achieves 45.26% test accuracy on OfficeQA and a mean partial-credit score of 75.19% on AutomationBench, exceeding weight-only RL by 6.43 and 9.09 percentage points and ungated alternation by 4.59 and 6.95 points, respectively. Across 44 harness proposals, 17 reduce validation performance at the updated checkpoint and are rejected before subsequent RL training, highlighting the importance of validation gating.

赵波老师实验室.title: FP2: Equipping Robotic Foundation Models with Force Control
赵波老师实验室.authors_text: Hongjie Fang, Shirun Tang, Junjian Hu, Shidong Zhang, Derek Zhang
赵波老师实验室.summary: FP2 enhances robotic foundation models with explicit force control through a lightweight interface, improving task performance and interaction quality in contact-rich environments.
赵波老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic foundation models (RFMs) are increasingly capable of general-purpose manipulation, yet reliable physical interaction remains challenging in contact-rich settings. We present FP2, a lightweight downstream interface that equips task-adapted RFMs with explicit force control while preserving their action-generation capability. FP2 adopts an action-regulation decomposition: the task-adapted RFM serves as a foundation policy responsible for task-level action generation, while a high-frequency force control policy focuses solely on interaction regulation. To condition force regulation on the ongoing manipulation, FP2 compresses foundation-policy contextual representations and combines them with wrench and proprioceptive histories to predict structured force-control parameters. We evaluate FP2 with four RFM backbones across four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks. FP2 consistently improves task performance and force regulation quality over the corresponding foundation policies, while comparing favorably with representative force-aware and force-control baselines. Ablations further show that foundation-policy context and physical feedback are complementary for effective force regulation, while preserving foundation-policy action generation improves both efficiency and novel-object generalization. Project website: http://force-policy.github.io/fp2

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Prior Evolution and Task Alignment for Aerial Grasping
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Weiliang Deng, Zhengyang Dang, Yao Mu, Ximin Lyu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper presents a method for enhancing aerial grasping optimization by learning trajectory priors and using execution-aware feedback to improve reliability and performance.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Aerial grasping is a remarkable capability exhibited by predatory birds, allowing them to capture prey through highly coordinated maneuvers in flight. Inspired by this capability, researchers have developed various formulations to reproduce such maneuvers through trajectory optimization. However, two limitations remain in practice. First, the resulting optimization problem is highly nonconvex and sensitive to initialization, making high-quality solutions difficult to obtain under a limited computational budget. Second, prescribed numerical objectives are human-designed abstractions that describe successful grasping through a limited set of mathematically tractable quantities and may not fully capture what determines task success. We investigate how learning can address these limitations within an analytical planner. Accordingly, a trajectory prior is first learned from optimized motions and then evolved through a CEM-based process that evaluates sampled initializations with the deployed optimizer and retains favorable ones as new supervision. An Execution-Aware Critic learns from contact, lift, and completion outcomes to assess whether the optimized trajectories are likely to succeed in physical execution. Its frozen energy can further serve as a differentiable grasping cost, allowing execution data to directly shape trajectory generation. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate improved optimization reliability, trajectory consistency, and grasping performance.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Josh Qixuan Sun, Xiaoying Xing, Yurun Chen, Huaiyuan Weng, Wentao Zhu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: NavBind evaluates instruction-action binding in navigation VLAs by analyzing how instruction changes affect action distributions at route forks, revealing discrepancies between navigation success and instruction adherence.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) navigation models translate visual observations and instructions into actions. Navigation success assesses whether an agent reaches the goal. However, reaching the goal successfully does not establish whether the model genuinely follows the instructions or relies on visual cues or navigation history. We introduce NavBind to diagnose instruction-action binding: whether changing the instruction influences the probabilistic distribution of the actions, with the navigation context fixed. We construct 3,252 route-fork contexts by recombining route-aligned instruction segments from R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Each context pairs full instructions that share the description of the route already traveled but specify different branches. Both are evaluated under the same agent state and navigation history. We compare generated local action sequences, the likelihoods of fixed reference action sequences under both instructions, and changes in visual attention and attribution. Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yiming Zhang, Jiarui Guo, Haojia Wei, Yifei Liu, Yifan Yang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: FilmFlow is an advanced framework that translates natural language and video references into precise camera trajectories for 3D cinematography, outperforming existing methods in performance and user preference.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and licensed sources, with five camera instructions per scene for 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos associated with a subset of scenes. CinemaBench supports evaluation of both text-directed camera generation and video reference-directed camera generation. Across a diverse set of evaluated baselines, FilmFlow achieves the strongest benchmark performance and the highest user preference, demonstrating effective spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, and visual composition for executable 3D cinematography.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Loop to Look Better: Learning Adaptive Depth for Question-Guided Perception in Vision-Language Models
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Wencheng Ye, Anning Hu, Hongye Fang, Tianyi Wang, Junchi Yan
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: LoopLook enhances Vision-Language Models by introducing a recurrent framework for adaptive visual depth, improving task-directed perception and performance across multiple benchmarks.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Visual perception should be iterative and task-directed, with representations refined in response to the question and the need for further processing. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly support extended reasoning, their visual tokens are still typically acquired in a single, task-agnostic encoder pass. This creates an evidence-acquisition bottleneck: models may reason longer without refining the visual evidence needed to answer the question. We propose LoopLook, a lightweight encoder-side recurrent perception framework that equips pretrained VLMs with adaptive visual depth. LoopLook recurrently revisits a middle-to-late window of the vision encoder, injecting question representations at each loop to guide visual refinement. A learned stopping mechanism adaptively determines the recurrent depth, while a token-wise Mixture-of-Looks (MoL) combines representations from different loops, allowing each visual token to selectively integrate information acquired across recurrent steps. Across four backbones and eight benchmarks, LoopLook consistently improves performance over the baseline, yielding gains of up to 8.6% on MMStar and 8.1% on HallusionBench. Our analysis shows that LoopLook progressively refines visual attention and adaptively allocates depth according to task difficulty. It also better preserves task-relevant visual information under reduced input resolution, while increasing time to first token (TTFT) by only 5.1-6.5%. By bringing recurrence from reasoning back into perception, LoopLook transforms visual perception from a one-shot glimpse into an adaptive process of recurrent refinement.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: LocoManiLab: A Unified Testbed for Data, Policies, Controllers, and Deployment in Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Dewei Wang, Jinrui Han, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Xianbo Lu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: LocoManiLab is a comprehensive testbed for humanoid loco-manipulation, integrating data collection, policy training, and evaluation across diverse tasks and environments.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation in everyday environments, yet progress is difficult to assess across differing policies, controllers, and task settings. LocoManiLab provides an integrated testbed spanning data collection and generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment. Its task suite covers 234 atomic and compositional tasks across five household scene categories, supported by 51.5 hours of simulated teleoperation. The evaluation covers twelve policies with a shared controller across task and scene splits and perturbation levels, two policies across five controllers, and studies of demonstration scale and data-source mixtures. Success rates fall on unseen tasks and scenes and generally decline as visual perturbations increase, with differences in generalization and robustness across policies. For data generation, a humanoid motion generation model is fine-tuned for loco-manipulation to study the alignment of its outputs with task execution requirements and its integration into the data generation pipeline. Three simulated loco-manipulation tasks closely match real-world setups, enabling evaluation of three policies in both domains. Similar policy rankings support the reliability of simulation-based evaluation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Tao Lin, Yuxin Du, Haoxiao Wang, Zile Zhong, Bo Zhao
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: FastHarness optimizes vision-language-action policies by adaptively scheduling supervision, reducing review frequency by 57.2% and increasing task success rates to 97.19%.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Agentic robot systems combine language-model reasoning with robot policies to monitor execution and recover from failures. However, reviewing every action chunk incurs substantial overhead, even in familiar situations. We introduce FastHarness, an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a π0.5 policy. A fast path uses stage memory and reviewed outcomes to reduce review frequency as experience accumulates, while a complementary recovery path focuses supervision on correcting errors. Once recovery is verified, routine execution resumes, with failure experience retained to guide future interventions. The policy remains frozen and generates fresh actions from current observations. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, reviewer token use decreases by an average of 57.2% per task from the first evaluated episode to the mean of the final five episodes. Mean episode time decreases from 85.5 to 52.0 minutes over the same interval. On the same tasks, mean success increases from 80% for GPT-as-Policy (π0.5 + GPT-6 Astra) to 97.19% with FastHarness. These results highlight adaptive supervision as a practical route to more efficient agentic robotics without additional model training.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Dingxuan Zhang, Yanhui Jiang, Jun Wang, Hefeng Zhou
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper presents Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework for coding agents that enhances execution robustness through dynamic skill granularity adjustment and macro-to-micro recovery strategies.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units. Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution. In coding agents, however, execution poses an additional runtime control problem: the same task may be solved through primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery. We introduce Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework that treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures. The system combines a feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state recovery executor. We evaluate the framework with a deterministic coding-agent protocol using verifier-defined success, total cost, and process metrics such as macro adoption, failure recovery, route match, and transition correctness. Results show that fixed macro execution is efficient when applicable but brittle under mismatch, while runtime routing and explicit macro-to-micro recovery improve robustness and recover controlled macro failures that fixed-granularity execution leaves unresolved. Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Hybrid-PCGC: Hybrid Point Cloud Geometry Compression Bridging Generalization-based Model and Implicit Neural Representation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Wenjie Huang, Qi Yang, Shuting Xia, He Huang, Zhu Li
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: Hybrid-PCGC optimizes point cloud geometry compression by balancing fidelity and bitrate through a novel architecture that enhances adaptability and reduces overhead in 3D sensing applications.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Efficient point cloud geometry compression (PCGC) is essential for 3D sensing applications such as autonomous driving and digital twins. Hybrid methods combine the generalization of learned models with the adaptability of Implicit Neural Representations (INRs), but existing schemes often use complex architectures, rigid update strategies, and post-training weight compression, limiting adaptation efficiency and increasing bitstream overhead. This paper proposes Hybrid-PCGC, which formulates hybrid compression as a joint geometry-and-model bitrate allocation problem and optimizes instance-specific weight offsets as rate-constrained transmitted variables. It separates dataset-agnostic prior modeling from instance-specific adaptation through four components: a Frozen General Module (FGM), a Dual Trainable Adaptive Module (DTAM), an Adaptive Scope Controller (ASC), and a Supervised Offset Compression Module (SOCM). FGM captures global geometric regularities, while the parameter-efficient DTAM adapts to individual point clouds. ASC selects the update scope based on coding difficulty, and SOCM jointly optimizes and compresses weight offsets through differentiable entropy supervision during training. Experiments show that Hybrid-PCGC balances fidelity and bitrate, reducing bitrate by 13.96% and 16.33% over G-PCC on lossless and lossy benchmarks, respectively, and saving up to 12.33% bitrate over the state-of-the-art hybrid method on challenging dense point clouds.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Revisiting Distribution Matching for State-to-Vision Policy Distillation in Laparoscopic Robotic Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Mingyu Sheng, Jianan Fan, Dongnan Liu, Guoyan Zheng, Ron Kikinis
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: This paper presents a state-to-vision policy distillation framework for laparoscopic robotic manipulation, improving performance and reducing expert demonstration requirements compared to traditional RL and IL methods.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: End-to-end control policies trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) have emerged as an alternative to conventional surgical robotic control approaches, with recent studies exploring state-based policies trained on privileged state observations. However, such approaches rely on precise physical states that are difficult to obtain reliably in surgical environments. Vision-based RL provides an alternative by learning manipulation policies directly from RGB observations, avoiding explicit state estimation and manually engineered perception pipelines while enabling policies to acquire task-relevant visual representations. Nevertheless, obtaining vision-based policies via pure RL methods for surgical manipulation remains challenging. Thus, imitation learning (IL) becomes another solution, yet it requires a large number of expert demonstrations, which are difficult to obtain in minimally invasive surgery. In this work, we propose a framework for state-to-vision policy distillation in laparoscopic robotic manipulation. Specifically, a state-based policy with privileged observations is employed as the teacher, and a vision-based policy learns from RGB observations and robot proprioceptive information, which requires less expert demonstrations than IL and introduces superior performance than RL methods. We conduct extensive experiments on various surgical manipulation tasks in the simulated environment. Experimental results show that, in the context of laparoscopic robotic manipulation, training vision-based policies with general-purpose RL methods is challenging, whereas our proposed state-to-vision policy distillation leads to more consistent and stable performance across tasks.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Kaijun Zhou, Zhiyang Li, Le Chen, Jinyu Gu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: rMuscle introduces a dual-phase muscle-memory cache for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing inference speed by 1.29-1.42X while preserving task success rates in robotic applications.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Factory work is a promising early scenario for embodied AI: assigning repetitive manual jobs to robots has clear economic payoff, and a structured station keeps the jobs tractable for current policies. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models now dominate as the policy paradigm for these robots. The inference latency of VLA models directly affects robot responsiveness and motion smoothness. However, existing VLA inference frameworks do not fully exploit the characteristics of embodied workloads or account for the distinct bottlenecks across different stages of VLA inference. In this paper, we first characterize embodied workloads and identify substantial task similarity across repeated robot executions. We further find that such similarity extends beyond observations and action trajectories to internal model states. Drawing on these observations, we present rMuscle, a real-time VLA inference framework inspired by human muscle memory. It exploits cross-execution similarity through a dual-phase muscle-memory cache. The Context Cache reuses visual-token outputs to reduce computation, while the Action Cache reuses neuron activation patterns to reduce weight accesses. We keep both the cache memory footprint and access overhead low through online cache recomputation, sliding-window cache retrieval, and mask sharing across consecutive denoising steps. rMuscle achieves 1.29-1.42X speedup on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical manipulation tasks, while maintaining the original success rates on real-world robots.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: DepState-JEPA introduces a dual-stream RGB-Depth architecture for robot manipulation, enhancing predictive state representation by integrating spatial understanding and action-conditioned predictions through shared latent states.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce \textbf{DepState-JEPA}, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, \textbf{DepState}. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yifan Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Xiaojun Ye, Yifei Liu, Donggang Li
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: SpatialBrain enhances spatial reasoning by integrating experience with scene observations, improving decision-making across benchmarks without altering its fixed vision-language backbone.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: AdvFidelity: Unifying Preference Alignment and Few-Step Image Generation within Reinforcement Learning
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Sicong Kang, Fangao Zeng, Yuhan Li, Hao Zhou, Mengfei Xu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: AdvFidelity unifies preference alignment and efficient few-step image generation in reinforcement learning by incorporating artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision through an online adversarial reward mechanism.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Practical image generation requires both human preference alignment and few-step efficiency, yet combining reinforcement learning (RL) with distillation is often multi-stage and may erode RL gains We observe that few-step RL progressively improves structural coherence, even with specialized rewards, but leaves low-level artifacts that these rewards may fail to penalize. To address this gap, we propose AdvFidelity, which integrates artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision into RL through an online adversarial reward. This enables joint reward alignment and high-fidelity few-step generation within a single RL stage, without distribution matching distillation (DMD) or other explicit distillation objectives. We train a discriminator to rank high-quality references (positives) above content-matched reconstructions (negatives) produced by the current generator. Reconstructing moderately noised references largely preserves style and scene layout while exposing low-level degradations. This encourages the discriminator to assess artifacts rather than content differences. With negatives reconstructed online, alternating updates adapt fidelity supervision to the generator's evolving failure modes. References can come from existing target-domain data or full-step model samples. Built on LeapAlign, AdvFidelity backpropagates gradients from both rewards through the few-step sampling trajectories used at inference. Across two model backbones and three task settings, AdvFidelity matches full-step LeapAlign in alignment, task performance, and overall generation quality and remains highly competitive with other evaluated full-step RL methods, using only 4 or 8 steps without CFG.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: This paper presents new linear twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots, enhancing speed and reducing motor strain while improving locomotion on complex terrains.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. Yet its twisting is concentrated in a short buffer segment, imposing most of the workload on the two twist joints in the middle, which can often overburden the motors and limit its locomotion. With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%. Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces S-rolling, a novel steerable rolling gait for snake robots that enables low-clearance maneuverability while maintaining a low swept height and efficient steering.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Snake robots can traverse complex environments with limbless locomotion, but maneuvering in low-clearance environments remains challenging because a gait must maintain a small swept height while also providing planar steering. Existing rolling gaits preserve a low swept height body configuration but generally provide limited steering, whereas steering gaits often introduce vertical undulation and require additional clearance. With that in mind, this paper develops S-rolling, a steerable rolling gait that combines low swept height locomotion with planar maneuverability for twistable snake robots. S-rolling is designed using an S-shaped planar backbone curve, whose head and tail segments roll with independently controlled angular velocities, producing different motion modes. We derive its joint space gait equation, in which a central twist joint realizes the relative rotation between the two segments. We also develop a quasi-static kinematic model relating the segment rolling speeds to the linear and angular velocities of the robot. Real-robot experiments demonstrate the various motion modes, traversal through a 10 cm clearance test track, and maneuvering tasks beneath a large workpiece and a car chassis. In these low-clearance scenarios, S-rolling successfully performs approximately 90$^\circ$ and 180$^\circ$ heading changes, whereas the baseline rolling arc gait cannot change the robot heading.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Meng Luo, Zechen Bai, Shanqing Xu, Yanlin Li, Kaixin Li
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper explores recursive self-improvement in physical AI, emphasizing the integration of behavioral and process enhancements through experiential learning and feedback mechanisms.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Zhaohui Yang, Quanbao Lin, Chengqi Shi, Zhenglang Weng, Jicheng Lin
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The SP-HLM framework enhances humanoid loco-manipulation by integrating sparse poses and a learned motion prior for improved task coordination and real-time motion generation.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: HEHA: Bounded Suboptimal Planning for Constrained Routing and Its Use in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Exploration of Unknown Environments
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Longrui Yang, Yiyu Wang, Jingfan Tang, Yunpeng Lyu, Shizhe Zhao
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper presents HEHA, a hierarchical planning approach that optimizes multi-robot exploration in unknown environments by efficiently solving constrained routing problems for heterogeneous robots.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: This paper considers the path planning problem for autonomous exploration of an unknown environment using multiple heterogeneous robots such as drones, wheeled, and legged robots, with different capabilities to traverse complex terrains. A key challenge there is to intelligently allocate the robots to the unknown areas to be explored and determine the visiting order of those areas subject to traversability constraints, which leads to a large-scale constrained multiple hamiltonian path problem (mHPP) that needs to be quickly and iteratively solved every time when new space is explored. To address the hallenge, we propose HEHA (Hierarchical Exploration with Heterogeneous Agents) using a recent hierarchical method that decomposes the exploration into global planning and local planning. The major contribution in HEHA is its global planning, where we propose a new routing algorithm RCH (Routing with Constraints and Heterogeneity) that can quickly find bounded sub-optimal solutions for mHPP to minimize the maximum path length (i.e., makespan) among the agents subject to traversability constraints. Additionally, the local planner in HEHA also considers heterogeneity to avoid repeated and duplicated exploration among the robots. The experimental results show, in the presence of heterogeneous traversability, our RCH can solve mHPP with up to 47% smaller makespan than several baselines, and HEHA can reduce the exploration time by up to 30% compared with existing approaches.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Fangyu Jiang, Chaoran Xiong, Kehui Ma, Zhen Sun, Zeyu Zhang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: A2I-Calib++ is a kinematics-driven framework that enhances calibration and odometry accuracy in legged robots by mitigating noise through innovative motion and sensor fusion techniques.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Recently, multi-node inertial measurement unit (multi-IMU) systems have shown promise for robust odometry in legged robots. Multi-IMU fusion can improve legged robot odometry but requires accurate spatiotemporal calibration among the sensors. Existing multi-IMU calibration methods, designed for aerial or handheld platforms, face challenges on legged robots because routine locomotion may provide insufficient excitation, while foot slips, impacts, and vibrations introduce measurement disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose A2I-Calib++, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model. It estimates temporal offsets, extrinsic rotations and translations, and inertial biases through temporal correlation search followed by analytic spatial and bias estimation, without artificial calibration targets or complex parameter tuning for the target IMU. A2I-Calib++ comprises three core modules: 1) a Noise-Isotropy-Inspired Trajectory supported by a finite-horizon conditioning proposition that generates sufficient excitation to limit noise sensitivity; 2) a constraint-aware Adversarial Motion Priors controller that combines the anti-noise excitation with a rolling-contact reward for contact-aware execution; and 3) a contact-constrained virtual IMU that fuses pre-calibrated calf IMUs and joint kinematics under a rolling-contact model to construct the calibration reference. Furthermore, evaluations on both simulation and real-world quadruped platforms demonstrate notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jiaru Qian, Yihong Dong, Xue Jiang, Chun-Wah Hsu, Zhi Jin
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper introduces Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), an RL approach that enhances reasoning in Large Language Models by promoting path diversity and outperforming existing methods.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Parallel thinking has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploring multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. However, we identify that parallel thinking via Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically suffers from the mode collapse of reasoning paths, where parallel thinking trajectories degenerate into similar ones. This homogeneity undermines the fundamental motivation of parallel thinking, that is, maintaining multiple hypotheses concurrently to prevent premature loss into a suboptimal solution. In this paper, we propose Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), a simple yet effective RL approach for parallel thinking designed to encourage path diversity. DPT rewards the model to develop distinct reasoning strategies by penalizing the prefix similarity of parallel thinking paths, thereby enhancing a more comprehensive exploration of the reasoning space. We conduct various experiments and analyses across multiple reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of DPT. Results show that DPT successfully outperforms previous parallel thinking methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance over baselines. We validate path diversity as a key element to improve parallel thinking. Our code is available at https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Tingwen Du, Haoyu Guo, Hanxue Zhang, Xuanxu Wang, Junting Dong
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: The paper presents SERA, a self-evolving robotic agent that enhances long-horizon manipulation tasks by integrating memory and feedback to improve planning and execution success.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yumeng He, Eachen Soong, Xiaotian Yang, Weijia Zhang, Zanwei Zhou
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: NeoWorld-Pro transforms monocular images into interactive 3D simulation programs using MLLMs and physics validation, enhancing embodied AI with improved scene reconstruction and manipulation capabilities.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: The advancement of Embodied AI necessitates high-quality simulation assets that faithfully mirror the real world. However, transforming raw visual observations into simulation-ready scenes remains challenging due to the lack of physical grounding and scene-level interactivity in current image-to-URDF methods. We propose NeoWorld-Pro, a framework that reformulates monocular scene reconstruction as procedural programming for interactive 3D environments. Leveraging the zero-shot reasoning and code synthesis capabilities of MLLMs, NeoWorld-Pro converts a single RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties. A physics-in-the-loop mechanism then iteratively refines the generated programs by validating their execution in a physics engine, enforcing physically plausible articulations, valid object compositions and interactions, and accurate spatial relationships. Experiments show that NeoWorld-Pro outperforms open-loop and prior monocular reconstruction methods, while enabling complex downstream tasks such as stable stacking and fine-grained manipulation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: MMedAgent-Plus: Scaling Multimodal Medical Agents across Modalities, Tasks and Workflows
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Ruoxin Wang, Yuanting Pan, Binxu Li, Ruiyang Ji, Yaqian Chen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: MMedAgent-Plus is a multimodal medical AI that effectively orchestrates 18 specialist models across various tasks, achieving high accuracy and synthesis in complex workflows.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Medical workflows often require multiple interdependent analyses, but existing specialist and generalist AI models are not designed to coordinate them. We introduce MMedAgent-Plus, a multimodal medical tool-use agent that combines a vision-language planner with 18 leading specialist models spanning 12 tasks and 8 modalities. Through a unified tool interface, the planner selects specialists, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes responses grounded in their outputs. The planner is instruction-tuned on 208,928 samples from 32 public medical benchmarks, covering single- and multi-tool interactions across single and multiple rounds. We separately evaluate tool orchestration, response synthesis, and end-to-end execution on held-out samples. MMedAgent-Plus achieves tool-call accuracies of 91.0%, 98.1%, and 80.7% in single-tool multi-round, multi-tool multi-round, and multi-tool single-round settings, respectively. Given correct tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus achieves scores of 14.4-14.8 out of 15 for faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness across 600 evaluation samples. In end-to-end execution without pre-supplied tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus correctly invokes the required specialist in 90.6% of 350 evaluation cases spanning seven tasks. Its final-answer accuracy reaches 0.98, matching the dedicated leading specialist and exceeding the strongest baseline (0.28).

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Eachen Soong, Zijian Niu, Haoran Xu, Yihong Dong, Yunbo Wang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: NeoWorld-3 is a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual inputs, enabling high-fidelity simulations and successful physical manipulation by robots.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Simulation-ready world reconstruction demands physical interactivity beyond visual realism, which existing black-box 3D generation fails to deliver. We present NeoWorld-3, a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual observations via tunable, executable programs. At its core, NeoSDK provides the underlying computational engine for low-level geometries, part composition, differentiable parameter refinement, and physics validation. At the same time, NeoMCP exposes these capabilities as structured, tool-callable APIs for vision-language agents to visually inspect, edit code, and iteratively refine programs. Through a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture, the framework scales seamlessly from standalone articulated objects to complex compositional scenes. Evaluations across object-level and scene-level reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that NeoWorld-3 achieves state-of-the-art geometric fidelity and physical readiness. Crucially, manipulation trajectories planned within our reconstructed twins achieve successful zero-shot execution on a physical dual-arm robot, completing the Real-Sim-Real loop.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: WorldScape Policy 2.0: Empowering Steerable World Action Modeling with Reasoning-Augmented Memory and In-Context Learning
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Haisheng Su, Zongdai Liu, Xin Jin, Haoxuan Dou, Chengming Hu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: WorldScape Policy 2.0 enhances robotic manipulation through a controllable World Action Model that integrates reasoning-augmented memory and multimodal learning for improved task execution and planning.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual state transitions and robot actions. However, existing WAMs are constrained by limited temporal context, coarse episode-level language supervision, and predominantly text-only conditioning, which hinder task-progress tracking and fine-grained language-video-action grounding while limiting visual-context reasoning and cross-embodiment transfer. In this paper, we introduce WorldScape Policy 2.0, a controllable WAM with reasoning-augmented long short-term memory. Its causal short-term visual memory supplies recent observations as DiT prefill to preserve local interaction dynamics, while its long short-term event memory organizes historical VLM outputs into global-history, local-active, and event-boundary representations for progress-aware retrieval. The retrieved history augments perception and autoregressively generated planning tokens, yielding an implicit subgoal condition for autonomous planning; semantic forcing further transfers event-level instruction semantics into this latent planning pathway. To establish fine-grained multimodal controllability, we construct ManipEvent-5M, an event-grounded embodied pretraining dataset containing nearly 5 million event segments with aligned action trajectories, episode-level task instructions, segment-level subtask captions, goal images, and video demonstrations. These designs provide a unified interface for autonomous planning from high-level instructions and controllable execution from fine-grained text, goal-image, or video-context prompts. Experiments in both simulation and real-world platforms demonstrate superior capabilities in long-horizon autonomous planning, fine-grained instruction following and in-context adaptation.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yijia Fan, Ziqi Huang, Zhongang Cai, Yan Li, Zimo Wen
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: UMM-Reflection enhances unified multimodal models' self-repair capabilities through interleaved reinforcement learning, significantly improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring external verification.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Unified multimodal models can both look at and render images, so in principle they can repair their own generations: diagnose what an image gets wrong, revise it, observe the result, and diagnose again. Whether a revision helps is known only after it is rendered, so the reflection text and the image generation must be learned jointly, over the whole loop. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on reflection trajectories gives a cold start but does not find the high-success repair paths, and naive RL that optimizes only the renderer or only one head leaves most of the gain untapped. We introduce UMM-Reflection, which applies reinforcement learning (RL) to complete reflection trajectories inside one unified model: sibling trajectories share one initial image, so the group-relative advantage compares reflection strategies, and one trajectory-level advantage updates both the reflection tokens and the flow-based revisions, avoiding the combinatorial blow-up of per-round credit assignment. Unlike single-round editing or pipelines with an external critic, credit flows across rounds and to both roles of the same model, and no verifier is needed at inference. On BAGEL, UMM-Reflection improves GenEval by 12.05 points over SFT, and the gains transfer to WISE (+10.97), OneIG-Bench (+3.48), and T2I-CompBench++ (+4.63), none of which is used in training.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng
