We therefore investigate two kinds of benchmark flaws behind these gains: bugs, where the implementation does not match the intended task or evaluation protocol, and design limitations, where success criteria and simulation settings do not fully capture how acceleration affects task execution. Starting from tasks with anomalous gains, we localize root causes by plotting object trajectories against checker acceptance regions, and classify the resulting bugs into task consistency, initialization, and reproducibility. Extending this audit to seven benchmarks, including RoboTwin, LIBERO-Plus, and VLABench, we identify 22 bugs of these types and 4 design limitations. For the latter, we revise permissive success checkers, correct unrealistic object masses, and add a motion-aware score that favors smoother actions. Experiments show that bug fixes can reverse method rankings, moving the baseline from last to first on one task. Addressing design limitations can likewise remove anomalous gains: on another task, the baseline moves from 21 percentage points behind an accelerated method to 5 points ahead. Gains attributed to acceleration can therefore be artifacts of the benchmark rather than better task execution. We release our bug fixes and revised benchmark settings to support trustworthy evaluation of VLA acceleration.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: RoboChrono: A Real Robot Benchmark for Streaming Task Understanding
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Yuzhou Wu, Longteng Fan, Zimeng Li, Yu Wanchan, Ting Zhang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: RoboChrono is a benchmark for streaming task understanding in robot manipulation, revealing significant performance disparities among vision-language models across various tasks and emphasizing the importance of capability-specific evaluations.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Understanding ongoing robot manipulation requires models to interpret visual observations in relation to interaction history and task progress. We introduce RoboChrono, a benchmark for streaming task understanding comprising 39 scenarios and 34,713 evaluation instances, constructed from real robot executions and complementary bare-hand human recordings. The benchmark evaluates seven tasks grouped into recognition, alignment, and temporal grounding, covering action understanding and anticipation, visual correspondence, temporal ordering, and action localization. Zero-shot evaluation of 18 vision-language models reveals substantial differences across tasks. GPT-6-Astra achieves 98.3% accuracy on Frame Matching but 68.3% on Frame Ordering, while RynnBrain1.1-122B-A10B exhibits a larger gap, reaching 95.4% and 32.9%, respectively. Input ablations on matched questions with five open-weight models further reveal distinct dependencies on visual evidence: removing visual observations reduces Current Action Recognition accuracy by 22.1 percentage points, whereas Next Action Prediction decreases by only 0.7 points. These findings show that strong visual matching does not consistently coincide with strong temporal ordering, and suggest that next-action prediction can be supported by task and action priors even when visual evidence is unavailable. RoboChrono provides a diagnostic setting for examining these differences, highlighting the need for capability-specific evaluation beyond aggregate scores when assessing task understanding in robot manipulation.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: EventVLA: Event-Driven Visual Evidence Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Ganlin Yang, Zhangzheng Tu, Yuqiang Yang, Sitong Mao, Junyi Dong
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: EventVLA introduces a sparse visual evidence memory framework that enhances long-horizon VLA policies by dynamically capturing task-critical visual events, improving success rates by 40%.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Memory remains a critical bottleneck for long-horizon robotic manipulation, as standard Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies often fail when task-relevant cues become occluded or unobservable over time. While existing memory-augmented methods utilize historical context, they either suffer from severe information bottlenecks, incur high latency via decoupled dual systems, or rely on unselective buffers that accumulate massive visual redundancies. To address these limitations, we introduce EventVLA, an end-to-end framework founded on the concept of sparse visual evidence memory that comprises two core components: foundational visual anchors to retain initial and short-term contexts, and a dynamic Keyframe Evidence Memory (KEM) module. Specifically, KEM directly predicts future keyframe probabilities from the VLA's latent embeddings to autonomously capture and store sparse, task-critical visual events. This foresight-driven mechanism empowers the policy to dynamically evaluate the future causal utility of current observations, preserving transient visual evidence before it becomes unobservable. Furthermore, we propose RoboTwin-MeM, a diagnostic benchmark specifically designed to evaluate non-Markovian manipulation tasks with interactive visual evidence. Extensive evaluations show that across 17 memory-requiring simulation tasks and 4 real-world bimanual tasks, EventVLA achieves an average success rate improvement of +40% over state-of-the-art memory-augmented VLAs.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: GeoVerse: World-Consistent Novel View Synthesis in Geometric Latent Space
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Kerui Ren, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Changjian Jiang, Mu Huang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: GeoVerse synthesizes world-consistent novel views by integrating geometric latent space with video generative appearance priors, enhancing visual quality and geometric consistency.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis from sparse images must reconcile faithful reconstruction of observed regions with plausible completion of unseen content, while maintaining world consistency across viewpoints. Existing geometry-based methods preserve observed scene structure but often struggle to complete unseen regions, whereas video generative models offer rich appearance priors but accumulate inconsistencies during sequential view generation. We propose GeoVerse, a framework that synthesizes world-consistent novel views by performing generation within the geometric latent space of a pretrained 3D foundation model and injecting appearance priors from a video generative model. Specifically, GeoVerse extracts multilevel features from Wan2.2 VACE and injects them into the geometric latent diffusion model via a ControlNet-style adapter, incorporating video-learned appearance priors to enhance structural completion. To enforce cross-view coherence, a global spatial memory continuously aggregates observed and synthesized content, reprojecting target-aligned guidance to anchor subsequent predictions to a shared scene representation. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate improved visual quality and geometric consistency, with a 2.23 dB higher PSNR on DL3DV and 32.4% lower ATE on Mip-NeRF360 compared to GLD.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Jiexing Qi, Yu He, Jun Liu, Qichen Huang, Shaohua Hu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: VACE enhances language model agents through validation-gated co-evolution of model weights and harnesses, achieving superior performance on OfficeQA and AutomationBench compared to traditional methods.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Language model agents can be improved by updating their model weights or refining the harness that guides task execution. These components are coupled: weight updates change how the model uses the harness, while harness updates change the trajectories used for training. We propose VACE, Validation-Gated Alternating CoEvolution, which alternates agentic reinforcement learning with trajectory-driven harness refinement. After each RL stage, VACE reuses the collected trajectories to propose a harness revision and evaluates the incumbent and candidate with the updated model held fixed. The candidate guides subsequent training only if it improves validation performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, VACE achieves 45.26% test accuracy on OfficeQA and a mean partial-credit score of 75.19% on AutomationBench, exceeding weight-only RL by 6.43 and 9.09 percentage points and ungated alternation by 4.59 and 6.95 points, respectively. Across 44 harness proposals, 17 reduce validation performance at the updated checkpoint and are rejected before subsequent RL training, highlighting the importance of validation gating.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: FP2: Equipping Robotic Foundation Models with Force Control
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Hongjie Fang, Shirun Tang, Junjian Hu, Shidong Zhang, Derek Zhang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: FP2 enhances robotic foundation models with explicit force control through a lightweight interface, improving task performance and interaction quality in contact-rich environments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic foundation models (RFMs) are increasingly capable of general-purpose manipulation, yet reliable physical interaction remains challenging in contact-rich settings. We present FP2, a lightweight downstream interface that equips task-adapted RFMs with explicit force control while preserving their action-generation capability. FP2 adopts an action-regulation decomposition: the task-adapted RFM serves as a foundation policy responsible for task-level action generation, while a high-frequency force control policy focuses solely on interaction regulation. To condition force regulation on the ongoing manipulation, FP2 compresses foundation-policy contextual representations and combines them with wrench and proprioceptive histories to predict structured force-control parameters. We evaluate FP2 with four RFM backbones across four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks. FP2 consistently improves task performance and force regulation quality over the corresponding foundation policies, while comparing favorably with representative force-aware and force-control baselines. Ablations further show that foundation-policy context and physical feedback are complementary for effective force regulation, while preserving foundation-policy action generation improves both efficiency and novel-object generalization. Project website: http://force-policy.github.io/fp2

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Prior Evolution and Task Alignment for Aerial Grasping
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Weiliang Deng, Zhengyang Dang, Yao Mu, Ximin Lyu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper presents a method for enhancing aerial grasping optimization by learning trajectory priors and using execution-aware feedback to improve reliability and performance.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Aerial grasping is a remarkable capability exhibited by predatory birds, allowing them to capture prey through highly coordinated maneuvers in flight. Inspired by this capability, researchers have developed various formulations to reproduce such maneuvers through trajectory optimization. However, two limitations remain in practice. First, the resulting optimization problem is highly nonconvex and sensitive to initialization, making high-quality solutions difficult to obtain under a limited computational budget. Second, prescribed numerical objectives are human-designed abstractions that describe successful grasping through a limited set of mathematically tractable quantities and may not fully capture what determines task success. We investigate how learning can address these limitations within an analytical planner. Accordingly, a trajectory prior is first learned from optimized motions and then evolved through a CEM-based process that evaluates sampled initializations with the deployed optimizer and retains favorable ones as new supervision. An Execution-Aware Critic learns from contact, lift, and completion outcomes to assess whether the optimized trajectories are likely to succeed in physical execution. Its frozen energy can further serve as a differentiable grasping cost, allowing execution data to directly shape trajectory generation. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate improved optimization reliability, trajectory consistency, and grasping performance.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Josh Qixuan Sun, Xiaoying Xing, Yurun Chen, Huaiyuan Weng, Wentao Zhu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: NavBind evaluates instruction-action binding in navigation VLAs by analyzing how instruction changes affect action distributions at route forks, revealing discrepancies between navigation success and instruction adherence.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) navigation models translate visual observations and instructions into actions. Navigation success assesses whether an agent reaches the goal. However, reaching the goal successfully does not establish whether the model genuinely follows the instructions or relies on visual cues or navigation history. We introduce NavBind to diagnose instruction-action binding: whether changing the instruction influences the probabilistic distribution of the actions, with the navigation context fixed. We construct 3,252 route-fork contexts by recombining route-aligned instruction segments from R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Each context pairs full instructions that share the description of the route already traveled but specify different branches. Both are evaluated under the same agent state and navigation history. We compare generated local action sequences, the likelihoods of fixed reference action sequences under both instructions, and changes in visual attention and attribution. Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yiming Zhang, Jiarui Guo, Haojia Wei, Yifei Liu, Yifan Yang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: FilmFlow is an advanced framework that translates natural language and video references into precise camera trajectories for 3D cinematography, outperforming existing methods in performance and user preference.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and licensed sources, with five camera instructions per scene for 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos associated with a subset of scenes. CinemaBench supports evaluation of both text-directed camera generation and video reference-directed camera generation. Across a diverse set of evaluated baselines, FilmFlow achieves the strongest benchmark performance and the highest user preference, demonstrating effective spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, and visual composition for executable 3D cinematography.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Loop to Look Better: Learning Adaptive Depth for Question-Guided Perception in Vision-Language Models
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Wencheng Ye, Anning Hu, Hongye Fang, Tianyi Wang, Junchi Yan
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: LoopLook enhances Vision-Language Models by introducing a recurrent framework for adaptive visual depth, improving task-directed perception and performance across multiple benchmarks.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Visual perception should be iterative and task-directed, with representations refined in response to the question and the need for further processing. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly support extended reasoning, their visual tokens are still typically acquired in a single, task-agnostic encoder pass. This creates an evidence-acquisition bottleneck: models may reason longer without refining the visual evidence needed to answer the question. We propose LoopLook, a lightweight encoder-side recurrent perception framework that equips pretrained VLMs with adaptive visual depth. LoopLook recurrently revisits a middle-to-late window of the vision encoder, injecting question representations at each loop to guide visual refinement. A learned stopping mechanism adaptively determines the recurrent depth, while a token-wise Mixture-of-Looks (MoL) combines representations from different loops, allowing each visual token to selectively integrate information acquired across recurrent steps. Across four backbones and eight benchmarks, LoopLook consistently improves performance over the baseline, yielding gains of up to 8.6% on MMStar and 8.1% on HallusionBench. Our analysis shows that LoopLook progressively refines visual attention and adaptively allocates depth according to task difficulty. It also better preserves task-relevant visual information under reduced input resolution, while increasing time to first token (TTFT) by only 5.1-6.5%. By bringing recurrence from reasoning back into perception, LoopLook transforms visual perception from a one-shot glimpse into an adaptive process of recurrent refinement.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: LocoManiLab: A Unified Testbed for Data, Policies, Controllers, and Deployment in Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Dewei Wang, Jinrui Han, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Xianbo Lu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: LocoManiLab is a comprehensive testbed for humanoid loco-manipulation, integrating data collection, policy training, and evaluation across diverse tasks and environments.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation in everyday environments, yet progress is difficult to assess across differing policies, controllers, and task settings. LocoManiLab provides an integrated testbed spanning data collection and generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment. Its task suite covers 234 atomic and compositional tasks across five household scene categories, supported by 51.5 hours of simulated teleoperation. The evaluation covers twelve policies with a shared controller across task and scene splits and perturbation levels, two policies across five controllers, and studies of demonstration scale and data-source mixtures. Success rates fall on unseen tasks and scenes and generally decline as visual perturbations increase, with differences in generalization and robustness across policies. For data generation, a humanoid motion generation model is fine-tuned for loco-manipulation to study the alignment of its outputs with task execution requirements and its integration into the data generation pipeline. Three simulated loco-manipulation tasks closely match real-world setups, enabling evaluation of three policies in both domains. Similar policy rankings support the reliability of simulation-based evaluation.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: FastHarness: Experience-Driven Review Scheduling for Vision-Language-Action Policies
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Tao Lin, Yuxin Du, Haoxiao Wang, Zile Zhong, Bo Zhao
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: FastHarness optimizes vision-language-action policies by adaptively scheduling supervision, reducing review frequency by 57.2% and increasing task success rates to 97.19%.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Agentic robot systems combine language-model reasoning with robot policies to monitor execution and recover from failures. However, reviewing every action chunk incurs substantial overhead, even in familiar situations. We introduce FastHarness, an experience-driven execution harness that adaptively schedules GPT-6 Astra supervision of a π0.5 policy. A fast path uses stage memory and reviewed outcomes to reduce review frequency as experience accumulates, while a complementary recovery path focuses supervision on correcting errors. Once recovery is verified, routine execution resumes, with failure experience retained to guide future interventions. The policy remains frozen and generates fresh actions from current observations. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, reviewer token use decreases by an average of 57.2% per task from the first evaluated episode to the mean of the final five episodes. Mean episode time decreases from 85.5 to 52.0 minutes over the same interval. On the same tasks, mean success increases from 80% for GPT-as-Policy (π0.5 + GPT-6 Astra) to 97.19% with FastHarness. These results highlight adaptive supervision as a practical route to more efficient agentic robotics without additional model training.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Dingxuan Zhang, Yanhui Jiang, Jun Wang, Hefeng Zhou
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper presents Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework for coding agents that enhances execution robustness through dynamic skill granularity adjustment and macro-to-micro recovery strategies.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units. Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution. In coding agents, however, execution poses an additional runtime control problem: the same task may be solved through primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery. We introduce Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework that treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures. The system combines a feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state recovery executor. We evaluate the framework with a deterministic coding-agent protocol using verifier-defined success, total cost, and process metrics such as macro adoption, failure recovery, route match, and transition correctness. Results show that fixed macro execution is efficient when applicable but brittle under mismatch, while runtime routing and explicit macro-to-micro recovery improve robustness and recover controlled macro failures that fixed-granularity execution leaves unresolved. Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Hybrid-PCGC: Hybrid Point Cloud Geometry Compression Bridging Generalization-based Model and Implicit Neural Representation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Wenjie Huang, Qi Yang, Shuting Xia, He Huang, Zhu Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: Hybrid-PCGC optimizes point cloud geometry compression by balancing fidelity and bitrate through a novel architecture that enhances adaptability and reduces overhead in 3D sensing applications.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Efficient point cloud geometry compression (PCGC) is essential for 3D sensing applications such as autonomous driving and digital twins. Hybrid methods combine the generalization of learned models with the adaptability of Implicit Neural Representations (INRs), but existing schemes often use complex architectures, rigid update strategies, and post-training weight compression, limiting adaptation efficiency and increasing bitstream overhead. This paper proposes Hybrid-PCGC, which formulates hybrid compression as a joint geometry-and-model bitrate allocation problem and optimizes instance-specific weight offsets as rate-constrained transmitted variables. It separates dataset-agnostic prior modeling from instance-specific adaptation through four components: a Frozen General Module (FGM), a Dual Trainable Adaptive Module (DTAM), an Adaptive Scope Controller (ASC), and a Supervised Offset Compression Module (SOCM). FGM captures global geometric regularities, while the parameter-efficient DTAM adapts to individual point clouds. ASC selects the update scope based on coding difficulty, and SOCM jointly optimizes and compresses weight offsets through differentiable entropy supervision during training. Experiments show that Hybrid-PCGC balances fidelity and bitrate, reducing bitrate by 13.96% and 16.33% over G-PCC on lossless and lossy benchmarks, respectively, and saving up to 12.33% bitrate over the state-of-the-art hybrid method on challenging dense point clouds.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Revisiting Distribution Matching for State-to-Vision Policy Distillation in Laparoscopic Robotic Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Mingyu Sheng, Jianan Fan, Dongnan Liu, Guoyan Zheng, Ron Kikinis
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: This paper presents a state-to-vision policy distillation framework for laparoscopic robotic manipulation, improving performance and reducing expert demonstration requirements compared to traditional RL and IL methods.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: End-to-end control policies trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) have emerged as an alternative to conventional surgical robotic control approaches, with recent studies exploring state-based policies trained on privileged state observations. However, such approaches rely on precise physical states that are difficult to obtain reliably in surgical environments. Vision-based RL provides an alternative by learning manipulation policies directly from RGB observations, avoiding explicit state estimation and manually engineered perception pipelines while enabling policies to acquire task-relevant visual representations. Nevertheless, obtaining vision-based policies via pure RL methods for surgical manipulation remains challenging. Thus, imitation learning (IL) becomes another solution, yet it requires a large number of expert demonstrations, which are difficult to obtain in minimally invasive surgery. In this work, we propose a framework for state-to-vision policy distillation in laparoscopic robotic manipulation. Specifically, a state-based policy with privileged observations is employed as the teacher, and a vision-based policy learns from RGB observations and robot proprioceptive information, which requires less expert demonstrations than IL and introduces superior performance than RL methods. We conduct extensive experiments on various surgical manipulation tasks in the simulated environment. Experimental results show that, in the context of laparoscopic robotic manipulation, training vision-based policies with general-purpose RL methods is challenging, whereas our proposed state-to-vision policy distillation leads to more consistent and stable performance across tasks.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Kaijun Zhou, Zhiyang Li, Le Chen, Jinyu Gu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: rMuscle introduces a dual-phase muscle-memory cache for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing inference speed by 1.29-1.42X while preserving task success rates in robotic applications.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Factory work is a promising early scenario for embodied AI: assigning repetitive manual jobs to robots has clear economic payoff, and a structured station keeps the jobs tractable for current policies. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models now dominate as the policy paradigm for these robots. The inference latency of VLA models directly affects robot responsiveness and motion smoothness. However, existing VLA inference frameworks do not fully exploit the characteristics of embodied workloads or account for the distinct bottlenecks across different stages of VLA inference. In this paper, we first characterize embodied workloads and identify substantial task similarity across repeated robot executions. We further find that such similarity extends beyond observations and action trajectories to internal model states. Drawing on these observations, we present rMuscle, a real-time VLA inference framework inspired by human muscle memory. It exploits cross-execution similarity through a dual-phase muscle-memory cache. The Context Cache reuses visual-token outputs to reduce computation, while the Action Cache reuses neuron activation patterns to reduce weight accesses. We keep both the cache memory footprint and access overhead low through online cache recomputation, sliding-window cache retrieval, and mask sharing across consecutive denoising steps. rMuscle achieves 1.29-1.42X speedup on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical manipulation tasks, while maintaining the original success rates on real-world robots.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: DepState-JEPA introduces a dual-stream RGB-Depth architecture for robot manipulation, enhancing predictive state representation by integrating spatial understanding and action-conditioned predictions through shared latent states.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce \textbf{DepState-JEPA}, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, \textbf{DepState}. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yifan Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Xiaojun Ye, Yifei Liu, Donggang Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: SpatialBrain enhances spatial reasoning by integrating experience with scene observations, improving decision-making across benchmarks without altering its fixed vision-language backbone.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: AdvFidelity: Unifying Preference Alignment and Few-Step Image Generation within Reinforcement Learning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Sicong Kang, Fangao Zeng, Yuhan Li, Hao Zhou, Mengfei Xu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: AdvFidelity unifies preference alignment and efficient few-step image generation in reinforcement learning by incorporating artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision through an online adversarial reward mechanism.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Practical image generation requires both human preference alignment and few-step efficiency, yet combining reinforcement learning (RL) with distillation is often multi-stage and may erode RL gains We observe that few-step RL progressively improves structural coherence, even with specialized rewards, but leaves low-level artifacts that these rewards may fail to penalize. To address this gap, we propose AdvFidelity, which integrates artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision into RL through an online adversarial reward. This enables joint reward alignment and high-fidelity few-step generation within a single RL stage, without distribution matching distillation (DMD) or other explicit distillation objectives. We train a discriminator to rank high-quality references (positives) above content-matched reconstructions (negatives) produced by the current generator. Reconstructing moderately noised references largely preserves style and scene layout while exposing low-level degradations. This encourages the discriminator to assess artifacts rather than content differences. With negatives reconstructed online, alternating updates adapt fidelity supervision to the generator's evolving failure modes. References can come from existing target-domain data or full-step model samples. Built on LeapAlign, AdvFidelity backpropagates gradients from both rewards through the few-step sampling trajectories used at inference. Across two model backbones and three task settings, AdvFidelity matches full-step LeapAlign in alignment, task performance, and overall generation quality and remains highly competitive with other evaluated full-step RL methods, using only 4 or 8 steps without CFG.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: This paper presents new linear twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots, enhancing speed and reducing motor strain while improving locomotion on complex terrains.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. Yet its twisting is concentrated in a short buffer segment, imposing most of the workload on the two twist joints in the middle, which can often overburden the motors and limit its locomotion. With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%. Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Qingling Fan, Zhongqiang Ren
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper introduces S-rolling, a novel steerable rolling gait for snake robots that enables low-clearance maneuverability while maintaining a low swept height and efficient steering.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Snake robots can traverse complex environments with limbless locomotion, but maneuvering in low-clearance environments remains challenging because a gait must maintain a small swept height while also providing planar steering. Existing rolling gaits preserve a low swept height body configuration but generally provide limited steering, whereas steering gaits often introduce vertical undulation and require additional clearance. With that in mind, this paper develops S-rolling, a steerable rolling gait that combines low swept height locomotion with planar maneuverability for twistable snake robots. S-rolling is designed using an S-shaped planar backbone curve, whose head and tail segments roll with independently controlled angular velocities, producing different motion modes. We derive its joint space gait equation, in which a central twist joint realizes the relative rotation between the two segments. We also develop a quasi-static kinematic model relating the segment rolling speeds to the linear and angular velocities of the robot. Real-robot experiments demonstrate the various motion modes, traversal through a 10 cm clearance test track, and maneuvering tasks beneath a large workpiece and a car chassis. In these low-clearance scenarios, S-rolling successfully performs approximately 90$^\circ$ and 180$^\circ$ heading changes, whereas the baseline rolling arc gait cannot change the robot heading.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Meng Luo, Zechen Bai, Shanqing Xu, Yanlin Li, Kaixin Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper explores recursive self-improvement in physical AI, emphasizing the integration of behavioral and process enhancements through experiential learning and feedback mechanisms.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Zhaohui Yang, Quanbao Lin, Chengqi Shi, Zhenglang Weng, Jicheng Lin
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The SP-HLM framework enhances humanoid loco-manipulation by integrating sparse poses and a learned motion prior for improved task coordination and real-time motion generation.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: HEHA: Bounded Suboptimal Planning for Constrained Routing and Its Use in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Exploration of Unknown Environments
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Longrui Yang, Yiyu Wang, Jingfan Tang, Yunpeng Lyu, Shizhe Zhao
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper presents HEHA, a hierarchical planning approach that optimizes multi-robot exploration in unknown environments by efficiently solving constrained routing problems for heterogeneous robots.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: This paper considers the path planning problem for autonomous exploration of an unknown environment using multiple heterogeneous robots such as drones, wheeled, and legged robots, with different capabilities to traverse complex terrains. A key challenge there is to intelligently allocate the robots to the unknown areas to be explored and determine the visiting order of those areas subject to traversability constraints, which leads to a large-scale constrained multiple hamiltonian path problem (mHPP) that needs to be quickly and iteratively solved every time when new space is explored. To address the hallenge, we propose HEHA (Hierarchical Exploration with Heterogeneous Agents) using a recent hierarchical method that decomposes the exploration into global planning and local planning. The major contribution in HEHA is its global planning, where we propose a new routing algorithm RCH (Routing with Constraints and Heterogeneity) that can quickly find bounded sub-optimal solutions for mHPP to minimize the maximum path length (i.e., makespan) among the agents subject to traversability constraints. Additionally, the local planner in HEHA also considers heterogeneity to avoid repeated and duplicated exploration among the robots. The experimental results show, in the presence of heterogeneous traversability, our RCH can solve mHPP with up to 47% smaller makespan than several baselines, and HEHA can reduce the exploration time by up to 30% compared with existing approaches.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Fangyu Jiang, Chaoran Xiong, Kehui Ma, Zhen Sun, Zeyu Zhang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: A2I-Calib++ is a kinematics-driven framework that enhances calibration and odometry accuracy in legged robots by mitigating noise through innovative motion and sensor fusion techniques.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Recently, multi-node inertial measurement unit (multi-IMU) systems have shown promise for robust odometry in legged robots. Multi-IMU fusion can improve legged robot odometry but requires accurate spatiotemporal calibration among the sensors. Existing multi-IMU calibration methods, designed for aerial or handheld platforms, face challenges on legged robots because routine locomotion may provide insufficient excitation, while foot slips, impacts, and vibrations introduce measurement disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose A2I-Calib++, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model. It estimates temporal offsets, extrinsic rotations and translations, and inertial biases through temporal correlation search followed by analytic spatial and bias estimation, without artificial calibration targets or complex parameter tuning for the target IMU. A2I-Calib++ comprises three core modules: 1) a Noise-Isotropy-Inspired Trajectory supported by a finite-horizon conditioning proposition that generates sufficient excitation to limit noise sensitivity; 2) a constraint-aware Adversarial Motion Priors controller that combines the anti-noise excitation with a rolling-contact reward for contact-aware execution; and 3) a contact-constrained virtual IMU that fuses pre-calibrated calf IMUs and joint kinematics under a rolling-contact model to construct the calibration reference. Furthermore, evaluations on both simulation and real-world quadruped platforms demonstrate notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Jiaru Qian, Yihong Dong, Xue Jiang, Chun-Wah Hsu, Zhi Jin
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper introduces Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), an RL approach that enhances reasoning in Large Language Models by promoting path diversity and outperforming existing methods.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Parallel thinking has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploring multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. However, we identify that parallel thinking via Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically suffers from the mode collapse of reasoning paths, where parallel thinking trajectories degenerate into similar ones. This homogeneity undermines the fundamental motivation of parallel thinking, that is, maintaining multiple hypotheses concurrently to prevent premature loss into a suboptimal solution. In this paper, we propose Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), a simple yet effective RL approach for parallel thinking designed to encourage path diversity. DPT rewards the model to develop distinct reasoning strategies by penalizing the prefix similarity of parallel thinking paths, thereby enhancing a more comprehensive exploration of the reasoning space. We conduct various experiments and analyses across multiple reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of DPT. Results show that DPT successfully outperforms previous parallel thinking methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance over baselines. We validate path diversity as a key element to improve parallel thinking. Our code is available at https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Tingwen Du, Haoyu Guo, Hanxue Zhang, Xuanxu Wang, Junting Dong
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper presents SERA, a self-evolving robotic agent that enhances long-horizon manipulation tasks by integrating memory and feedback to improve planning and execution success.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yumeng He, Eachen Soong, Xiaotian Yang, Weijia Zhang, Zanwei Zhou
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: NeoWorld-Pro transforms monocular images into interactive 3D simulation programs using MLLMs and physics validation, enhancing embodied AI with improved scene reconstruction and manipulation capabilities.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: The advancement of Embodied AI necessitates high-quality simulation assets that faithfully mirror the real world. However, transforming raw visual observations into simulation-ready scenes remains challenging due to the lack of physical grounding and scene-level interactivity in current image-to-URDF methods. We propose NeoWorld-Pro, a framework that reformulates monocular scene reconstruction as procedural programming for interactive 3D environments. Leveraging the zero-shot reasoning and code synthesis capabilities of MLLMs, NeoWorld-Pro converts a single RGB image into executable programs specifying object geometry, articulation, and physical properties. A physics-in-the-loop mechanism then iteratively refines the generated programs by validating their execution in a physics engine, enforcing physically plausible articulations, valid object compositions and interactions, and accurate spatial relationships. Experiments show that NeoWorld-Pro outperforms open-loop and prior monocular reconstruction methods, while enabling complex downstream tasks such as stable stacking and fine-grained manipulation.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: MMedAgent-Plus: Scaling Multimodal Medical Agents across Modalities, Tasks and Workflows
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Ruoxin Wang, Yuanting Pan, Binxu Li, Ruiyang Ji, Yaqian Chen
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: MMedAgent-Plus is a multimodal medical AI that effectively orchestrates 18 specialist models across various tasks, achieving high accuracy and synthesis in complex workflows.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Medical workflows often require multiple interdependent analyses, but existing specialist and generalist AI models are not designed to coordinate them. We introduce MMedAgent-Plus, a multimodal medical tool-use agent that combines a vision-language planner with 18 leading specialist models spanning 12 tasks and 8 modalities. Through a unified tool interface, the planner selects specialists, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes responses grounded in their outputs. The planner is instruction-tuned on 208,928 samples from 32 public medical benchmarks, covering single- and multi-tool interactions across single and multiple rounds. We separately evaluate tool orchestration, response synthesis, and end-to-end execution on held-out samples. MMedAgent-Plus achieves tool-call accuracies of 91.0%, 98.1%, and 80.7% in single-tool multi-round, multi-tool multi-round, and multi-tool single-round settings, respectively. Given correct tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus achieves scores of 14.4-14.8 out of 15 for faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness across 600 evaluation samples. In end-to-end execution without pre-supplied tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus correctly invokes the required specialist in 90.6% of 350 evaluation cases spanning seven tasks. Its final-answer accuracy reaches 0.98, matching the dedicated leading specialist and exceeding the strongest baseline (0.28).

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Eachen Soong, Zijian Niu, Haoran Xu, Yihong Dong, Yunbo Wang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: NeoWorld-3 is a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual inputs, enabling high-fidelity simulations and successful physical manipulation by robots.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Simulation-ready world reconstruction demands physical interactivity beyond visual realism, which existing black-box 3D generation fails to deliver. We present NeoWorld-3, a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual observations via tunable, executable programs. At its core, NeoSDK provides the underlying computational engine for low-level geometries, part composition, differentiable parameter refinement, and physics validation. At the same time, NeoMCP exposes these capabilities as structured, tool-callable APIs for vision-language agents to visually inspect, edit code, and iteratively refine programs. Through a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture, the framework scales seamlessly from standalone articulated objects to complex compositional scenes. Evaluations across object-level and scene-level reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that NeoWorld-3 achieves state-of-the-art geometric fidelity and physical readiness. Crucially, manipulation trajectories planned within our reconstructed twins achieve successful zero-shot execution on a physical dual-arm robot, completing the Real-Sim-Real loop.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: WorldScape Policy 2.0: Empowering Steerable World Action Modeling with Reasoning-Augmented Memory and In-Context Learning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Haisheng Su, Zongdai Liu, Xin Jin, Haoxuan Dou, Chengming Hu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: WorldScape Policy 2.0 enhances robotic manipulation through a controllable World Action Model that integrates reasoning-augmented memory and multimodal learning for improved task execution and planning.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) offer a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual state transitions and robot actions. However, existing WAMs are constrained by limited temporal context, coarse episode-level language supervision, and predominantly text-only conditioning, which hinder task-progress tracking and fine-grained language-video-action grounding while limiting visual-context reasoning and cross-embodiment transfer. In this paper, we introduce WorldScape Policy 2.0, a controllable WAM with reasoning-augmented long short-term memory. Its causal short-term visual memory supplies recent observations as DiT prefill to preserve local interaction dynamics, while its long short-term event memory organizes historical VLM outputs into global-history, local-active, and event-boundary representations for progress-aware retrieval. The retrieved history augments perception and autoregressively generated planning tokens, yielding an implicit subgoal condition for autonomous planning; semantic forcing further transfers event-level instruction semantics into this latent planning pathway. To establish fine-grained multimodal controllability, we construct ManipEvent-5M, an event-grounded embodied pretraining dataset containing nearly 5 million event segments with aligned action trajectories, episode-level task instructions, segment-level subtask captions, goal images, and video demonstrations. These designs provide a unified interface for autonomous planning from high-level instructions and controllable execution from fine-grained text, goal-image, or video-context prompts. Experiments in both simulation and real-world platforms demonstrate superior capabilities in long-horizon autonomous planning, fine-grained instruction following and in-context adaptation.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yijia Fan, Ziqi Huang, Zhongang Cai, Yan Li, Zimo Wen
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: UMM-Reflection enhances unified multimodal models' self-repair capabilities through interleaved reinforcement learning, significantly improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring external verification.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Unified multimodal models can both look at and render images, so in principle they can repair their own generations: diagnose what an image gets wrong, revise it, observe the result, and diagnose again. Whether a revision helps is known only after it is rendered, so the reflection text and the image generation must be learned jointly, over the whole loop. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on reflection trajectories gives a cold start but does not find the high-success repair paths, and naive RL that optimizes only the renderer or only one head leaves most of the gain untapped. We introduce UMM-Reflection, which applies reinforcement learning (RL) to complete reflection trajectories inside one unified model: sibling trajectories share one initial image, so the group-relative advantage compares reflection strategies, and one trajectory-level advantage updates both the reflection tokens and the flow-based revisions, avoiding the combinatorial blow-up of per-round credit assignment. Unlike single-round editing or pipelines with an external critic, credit flows across rounds and to both roles of the same model, and no verifier is needed at inference. On BAGEL, UMM-Reflection improves GenEval by 12.05 points over SFT, and the gains transfer to WISE (+10.97), OneIG-Bench (+3.48), and T2I-CompBench++ (+4.63), none of which is used in training.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yanbo Wang, Siqi Luo, Siyu Zhang, Chenming Zhu, Wenzhao Zheng
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: MindView is a benchmark for assessing generative multi-view spatial intelligence, revealing significant improvement opportunities and introducing MindCue for enhanced evidence utilization in expanded contexts.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: RoboCasa-Shift: Stage-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Household Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Haocheng Wang, Youquan Liu, Weiyu Guo, Aokai Zhang, Donghang Wu
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: RoboCasa-Shift introduces a benchmark for evaluating vision-language-action policy robustness in long-horizon tasks, highlighting the complexity of failure dynamics under distribution shifts.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) robustness is commonly summarized by aggregate task success, which obscures how individual executions change under distribution shifts and where failures emerge in long-horizon tasks. We introduce \textbf{RoboCasa-Shift}, a diagnostic robustness benchmark built on RoboCasa365 that combines controlled single-factor shifts, matched clean-perturbed rollouts in which each pair shares the same underlying settings and differs only in the target shift, and simulator-grounded stage-aware diagnostics. We evaluate GR00T N1.5 on four long-horizon tasks that pass a predefined clean-performance gate under four perturbation factors and three calibrated severity levels, including conditions that drive the evaluated policy to complete task failure, totaling 1,040 formal rollouts. Robustness responses vary substantially across factors and tasks, and increasing severity does not always produce monotonic degradation. For example, one camera condition yields $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0$ despite 8 of 80 matched episodes changing outcome. Stage-aware analysis further shows that the same end-to-end degradation can correspond to different execution-depth profiles. Camera $L_2$ and Gaussian blur $L_1$ both yield $Δ\mathrm{SR}=0.188$, yet their first-stage failure rates are 19.0\% and 36.4\%, respectively. Our findings suggest that VLA robustness should be viewed as a multi-dimensional property of execution rather than a single end-to-end performance measure, motivating evaluation protocols that jointly capture outcome degradation, paired outcome sensitivity, and failure progression. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaochengWang23/RoboCasa-Shift.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: GeoV2V: Geometry-Grounded Video Diffusion Model for Driving Scene Generation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yuchen Xi, Yuhan Guo, Chenwei Hou, Zixu Liu, Jin Fang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: GeoV2V is a novel video-to-video diffusion model that enhances driving scene generation by integrating geometric priors and a synthetic dataset for improved visual and geometric consistency.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Novel view synthesis under trajectory changes is essential for autonomous driving simulation, yet existing methods struggle to generate consistent videos when extrapolating to unseen viewpoints such as lane shifts. Reconstruction-based approaches maintain geometric consistency but degrade in visual quality under large viewpoint changes, while reconstruct-then-restore methods often produce visually plausible frames yet suffer from geometric and temporal inconsistencies. We present GeoV2V, a geometry-grounded video-to-video diffusion framework that synthesizes temporally coherent driving videos along novel trajectories by integrating LiDAR and depth-derived geometric priors with full-video conditioning in the Wan 2.1 backbone. A key challenge in learning cross-lane transformations is the lack of synchronized multi-trajectory supervision in real-world datasets. To address this, we also introduce Para4D, a synthetic dataset capturing synchronized multi-lane driving videos within dynamic scenes, which provides explicit supervision for lane-shift generation and serves as a strong training prior for geometry-consistent view synthesis. Experiments on Waymo, nuScenes, and Para4D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in visual quality, geometric consistency, and robustness to complex lighting dynamics under large trajectory shifts. Project page: https://xiyuche.github.io/GeoV2V/

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Jize Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Xinyi Le, Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper advocates for a four-stage research agenda to enhance interpretability in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures by focusing on the dynamics and causal interactions of latent variables.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface. In this Perspective, we argue that as JEPA latents become internal states for prediction and action, interpretability must move beyond what they encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. To this end, we envision a four-stage research agenda, involving Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act, to guide this shift toward actionable latent-world understanding. Within our framework, existing JEPA interpretability efforts provide early evidence for Ground, while systematic analysis of latent structure, causal verification, and intervention remains largely unexplored. Overall, this Perspective aims to call for a broader latent-world interpretability agenda that shifts attention from decoding representations toward understanding, validating, and acting on latent worlds.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: RoboPocket: Improve Robot Policies Instantly with Your Phone
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Junjie Fang, Wendi Chen, Han Xue, Fangyuan Zhou, Tian Le
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: RoboPocket enables real-time, smartphone-based robot policy improvement through augmented reality feedback, enhancing data collection efficiency without deploying physical robots.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Scaling robot learning is bottlenecked not only by data volume, but also by whether the data targets the policy's failures. Existing robot-free handheld interfaces enable portable in-the-wild data collection, yet remain open-loop: users record demonstrations without feedback from the current policy. Interactive methods such as DAgger provide such feedback by collecting corrective on-policy data, but require deploying imperfect policies on physical robots, making them costly, unsafe, and difficult to scale. We present RoboPocket, a smartphone-based system for robot-free policy iteration. By combining on-device sensing, display, and communication with cloud-side policy inference, RoboPocket provides real-time collection guidance and visualizes the policy's predicted trajectory in augmented reality as AR Visual Foresight. This allows users to identify policy weaknesses and collect targeted corrective data without deploying a physical robot. An asynchronous finetuning pipeline continuously incorporates new corrections and updates the policy within minutes, realizing a DAgger-inspired robot-free correction loop. Across diverse real-world manipulation tasks, we validate RoboPocket as a scalable data engine and show that online corrective data collection improves sample efficiency by up to $2\times$ over scaling offline demonstrations. Project page and videos: https://robo-pocket.github.io.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Feiyang Hong, Yujie Wei, Bo Zhao, Xiu Su, Hongxun Yao
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: CondenseVLA introduces a learnable history condensation module for efficient multi-frame visual language action policies, enhancing task performance while reducing computational redundancy.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: FrameGRPO: Incentivizing Video Reasoning via Multi-Frame Rollouts and Temporal Credit
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Jiaxuan Sun, Biao Wang, Shuai Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: FrameGRPO enhances video reasoning in multimodal language models by employing multi-frame rollouts and gated temporal credit to diversify visual evidence and improve learning efficiency.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, particularly Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has improved video reasoning in multimodal large language models. However, standard video GRPO varies only linguistic trajectories while conditioning every rollout in a group on the same sampled frames, which can produce homogeneous rewards and weaken group-relative learning when the shared visual evidence is insufficient or distracting. We propose \textbf{FrameGRPO}, a simple and effective reinforcement-learning framework that requires neither auxiliary networks nor changes to the model architecture. Specifically, FrameGRPO combines two lightweight components: (1) \textbf{Multi-Frame Rollouts}, which use only uniform temporal subsampling of a single maximal-frame decode to construct aligned views that diversify visual evidence and reasoning trajectories; and (2) \textbf{Gated Temporal Efficiency Credit}, which selectively reinforces a correct lower-ratio trajectory when all rollouts in a fixed full-ratio reference subset fail, without imposing an unconditional preference for fewer frames. Extensive experiments across diverse video understanding and reasoning benchmarks demonstrate robust overall improvements over standard GRPO, highlighting temporal-view diversification as an effective mechanism for exploration and credit assignment in video MLLMs.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Compositional Humanoid Manipulation through Isomorphic Teleoperation and Independent Skill Routing
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yiming Wang, Peixian Yang, Lifeng Zhuo, Lai Wei, Xinling Du
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper introduces HS-MoDP, a method for compositional humanoid manipulation using isomorphic teleoperation and skill routing, enhancing skill reuse and performance in robotic tasks.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Humanoid manipulation requires reusable arm skills, yet demonstrating every possible skill combination is impractical. We present Humanoid Semantic Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Policy (HS-MoDP), which composes separately demonstrated arm skills through independent semantic routing over a shared expert pool. This design preserves arm-specific skill control while sharing action-generation parameters across arms. A semantic scheduler integrates the learned policy with an existing locomotion controller through alternating manipulation and repositioning stages, extending the effective workspace and enabling skill reuse across location changes. To acquire demonstrations of whole-body contact manipulation, we develop G1Exo, an isomorphic exoskeleton that provides direct joint-level control of arm configurations. Experiments on a Unitree G1 show stronger skill composition than the baselines. G1Exo enables more reliable contact teleoperation than end-effector VR-IK, and its demonstrations improve contact-skill learning across four policy architectures. For HS-MoDP, switching from VR-IK to G1Exo demonstrations raises full cabinet workflow success from 35% to 65%. All project hardware designs and source code will be released as open source after the review process.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: ALIGN: Aligning Condition Estimation and Expression in Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Zechen Wang, Zhenqi Qiu, Houlong Xiong, Suohang Zhang, Yiyu Ren
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: ALIGN is a novel framework that enhances Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning by accurately aligning condition estimation with action predictions, improving robot manipulation success rates.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Human-collected robot manipulation data often mix successful behavior with retries, pauses, recoveries, and failures. Advantage-Conditioned Behavior Cloning (AC-BC) can exploit such mixed-quality data, but only if the conditioning signal is both accurately constructed from offline trajectories and effectively incorporated into the policy's action-vector-field prediction. Existing pipelines can weaken this signal by thresholding estimator-derived advantage scores into noisy conditions, and by routing conditions through prompts that weakly affect the action vector field. We introduce ALIGN, a condition-aligned AC-BC framework for vision-language-action policies. ALIGN directly predicts categorical pairwise conditions in the policy-facing label space and injects them into a DiT action expert through AdaRMS modulation fused with flow time. We evaluate ALIGN on deliberately mixed real-robot datasets for ARX X5 bowl stacking and Franka key hanging, each combining standard demonstrations with retry-heavy trajectories. ALIGN improves condition fidelity, strengthens conditional vector-field separability, and achieves 90.0% and 56.7% closed-loop success, compared with 56.7% and 33.3% for the strongest AC-BC baseline. These results indicate that aligning conditions from estimation to action prediction is an effective way to extract robust manipulation policies from data in which success, recovery and error coexist.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper presents Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR) to enhance bimanual imitation learning by reducing spurious cross-arm coupling and improving task performance.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: ReInsVLN: Revisiting Historical Evidence for Training-Free Vision-and-Language Navigation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Siwei Cheng, Hao Wu, Zitong Qi, Xinming Zhang, Haoyu Xi
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: ReInsVLN enhances vision-and-language navigation by efficiently utilizing historical data through a training-free framework, improving success rates and reducing memory usage in robotic applications.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) relies on retaining and using relevant observations. Yet growing histories introduce redundancy, and retained information may remain underused. We introduce ReInsBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines history utilization through controlled continuation trials. Its results show that history-review reinstruction can recover navigation failures using the existing task context. Motivated by this finding, we propose ReInsVLN, a training-free framework supporting memory construction and utilization in frozen navigators. Coverage- and Instruction-Aware Compression constructs compact visual context through temporal redundancy reduction, coverage-aware protection, and instruction-guided token selection. Forgetting-Inspired History Reminders guide navigators to revisit retained observations according to a predefined schedule, without additional model calls. On R2R Val-Unseen, ReInsVLN improves success rates by 8.48 and 3.37 percentage points over the native StreamVLN and InternVLA-N1, reaching 64.27% and 64.44%, respectively. Visual compression largely preserves navigation performance while reducing prefill latency and KV cache memory by up to 21.77% and 32.25%, respectively, on matched observation workloads. Real-world trials on humanoid and quadruped robots further support the applicability of ReInsVLN to sequential instruction following and ordinal navigation.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: PICA-WAM: Visual Perturbation Invariance via Cross-Appearance Self-Alignment in World Action Models
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Guanbo Jiao, Jianming Ma, Guanjie Zheng
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: PICA-WAM enhances World Action Models' robustness to visual perturbations by introducing a self-supervised cross-appearance self-alignment task, improving action consistency and real robot performance.
